Sweeping and lamps, setting up of water and seats;<br>these are to be done before the observance-day ceremony.<br><br>Consent, purity, knowing the season, and counting the nuns, instruction;<br>these are called the preliminary duties of the observance-day ceremony.<br><br>it is the observance day, all the nuns who should be present have arrived,<br>there are no shared offenses,<br><br>and there is no-one there who should not be present. If you are silent, I will regard you as pure.<br><br>Just as one responds when asked individually, so too, an announcement is made three times in this kind of gathering.<br><br>If a nun remembers an offense while the announcement is being made up to the third time, but doesn’t reveal it, she is lying in full awareness.<br><br>Lying in full awareness is called an obstacle by the Buddha.<br><br>A nun who remembers an offense and is seeking purification should therefore reveal it. Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ_4.mp3]	33	At one time when the Buddha was staying in the house with the peaked roof in the Great Wood near Vesālī,<br><br>a number of monks who were friends had entered the samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vaseyyāma,<br><br>na ca piṇḍakena kilameyyāmā”ti?<br><br>Ekacce evamāhaṁsu—<br><br>“handa mayaṁ, āvuso, gihīnaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhema,<br><br>evaṁ te amhākaṁ dātuṁ maññissanti.<br><br>Evaṁ mayaṁ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vasissāma,<br><br>na ca piṇḍakena kilamissāmā”ti.<br><br>Ekacce evamāhaṁsu—<br><br>“alaṁ, āvuso, kiṁ gihīnaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhitena.<br><br>Handa mayaṁ, āvuso, gihīnaṁ dūteyyaṁ harāma,<br><br>evaṁ te amhākaṁ dātuṁ maññissanti.<br><br>Evaṁ mayaṁ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vasissāma,<br><br>na ca piṇḍakena kilamissāmā”ti.<br><br>Ekacce evamāhaṁsu—<br><br>“alaṁ, āvuso, kiṁ gihīnaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhitena.<br><br>Kiṁ gihīnaṁ dūteyyaṁ haṭena.<br><br>Handa mayaṁ, āvuso, gihīnaṁ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsissāma—<br><br>‘asuko bhikkhu paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu dutiyassa jhānassa lābhī,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu tatiyassa jhānassa lābhī,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu catutthassa jhānassa lābhī,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu sotāpanno,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu sakadāgāmī,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu anāgāmī,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu arahā,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu tevijjo,<br><br>asuko bhikkhu chaḷabhiñño’ti.<br><br>Evaṁ te amhākaṁ dātuṁ maññissanti.<br><br>Evaṁ mayaṁ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vasissāma,<br><br>na ca piṇḍakena kilamissāmā”ti.<br><br>“Esoyeva kho, āvuso, seyyo yo amhākaṁ gihīnaṁ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito”ti.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū gihīnaṁ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsiṁsu—<br><br>“asuko bhikkhu paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī …pe…<br><br>asuko bhikkhu chaḷabhiñño”ti.<br><br>Atha kho te manussā—<br><br>“lābhā vata no, suladdhaṁ vata no, yesaṁ no evarūpā bhikkhū vassaṁ upagatā;<br><br>na vata no ito pubbe evarūpā bhikkhū vassaṁ upagatā yathayime bhikkhū sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā”ti,<br><br>te na tādisāni bhojanāni attanā paribhuñjanti mātāpitūnaṁ denti puttadārassa denti dāsakammakaraporisassa denti mittāmaccānaṁ denti ñātisālohitānaṁ denti, yādisāni bhikkhūnaṁ denti.<br><br>Te na tādisāni khādanīyāni sāyanīyāni pānāni attanā khādanti sāyanti pivanti mātāpitūnaṁ denti puttadārassa denti dāsakammakaraporisassa denti mittāmaccānaṁ denti ñātisālohitānaṁ denti, yādisāni bhikkhūnaṁ denti.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū vaṇṇavā ahesuṁ pīṇindriyā pasannamukhavaṇṇā vippasannachavivaṇṇā.<br><br>Āciṇṇaṁ kho panetaṁ vassaṁvuṭṭhānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū vassaṁvuṭṭhā temāsaccayena senāsanaṁ saṁsāmetvā pattacīvaraṁ ādāya yena vesālī tena pakkamiṁsu.<br><br>Anupubbena yena vesālī mahāvanaṁ kūṭāgārasālā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena disāsu vassaṁvuṭṭhā bhikkhū kisā honti lūkhā dubbaṇṇā uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā dhamanisanthatagattā;<br><br>vaggumudātīriyā pana bhikkhū vaṇṇavā honti pīṇindriyā pasannamukhavaṇṇā vippasannachavivaṇṇā.<br><br>Āciṇṇaṁ kho panetaṁ buddhānaṁ bhagavantānaṁ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ paṭisammodituṁ.<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū etadavoca—<br><br>“kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīyaṁ kacci yāpanīyaṁ<br><br>kacci samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vasittha, na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti?<br><br>“Khamanīyaṁ, bhagavā, yāpanīyaṁ, bhagavā.<br><br>Samaggā ca mayaṁ, bhante, sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vasimhā, na ca piṇḍakena kilamimhā”ti.<br><br>Jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchanti, jānantāpi na pucchanti …pe…<br><br>dvīhākārehi buddhā bhagavanto bhikkhū paṭipucchanti— “dhammaṁ vā desessāma, sāvakānaṁ vā sikkhāpadaṁ paññapessāmā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū etadavoca—<br><br>“yathā kathaṁ pana tumhe, bhikkhave, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṁ vassaṁ vasittha na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti?<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.<br><br>“Kacci pana vo, bhikkhave, bhūtan”ti?<br><br>“Abhūtaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā—<br><br>“ananucchavikaṁ, moghapurisā, ananulomikaṁ appatirūpaṁ assāmaṇakaṁ akappiyaṁ akaraṇīyaṁ.<br><br>Kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, udarassa kāraṇā gihīnaṁ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsissatha.<br><br>Varaṁ tumhehi, moghapurisā, tiṇhena govikantanena kucchi parikanto, na tveva udarassa kāraṇā gihīnaṁ aññamaññassa uttarimanussadhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito.<br><br>Taṁ kissa hetu?<br><br>Tatonidānañhi, moghapurisā, maraṇaṁ vā nigaccheyya maraṇamattaṁ vā dukkhaṁ,<br><br>na tveva tappaccayā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyya.<br><br>Itonidānañca kho, moghapurisā, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyya.<br><br>Netaṁ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>vigarahitvā dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—<br><br>“Pañcime, bhikkhave, mahācorā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.<br><br>Katame pañca?<br><br>Idha, bhikkhave, ekaccassa mahācorassa evaṁ hoti—<br><br>‘kudāssu nāmāhaṁ satena vā sahassena vā parivuto gāmanigamarājadhānīsu āhiṇḍissāmi<br><br>hananto ghātento chindanto chedāpento pacanto pācento’ti.<br><br>So aparena samayena satena vā sahassena vā parivuto gāmanigamarājadhānīsu āhiṇḍati hananto ghātento chindanto chedāpento pacanto pācento.<br><br>Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekaccassa pāpabhikkhuno evaṁ hoti—<br><br>‘kudāssu nāmāhaṁ satena vā sahassena vā parivuto gāmanigamarājadhānīsu cārikaṁ carissāmi<br><br>sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito gahaṭṭhānañceva pabbajitānañca, lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānan’ti.<br><br>So aparena samayena satena vā sahassena vā parivuto gāmanigamarājadhānīsu cārikaṁ carati sakkato garukato mānito pūjito apacito gahaṭṭhānañceva pabbajitānañca, lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.<br><br>Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo mahācoro santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.<br><br>Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco pāpabhikkhu tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā attano dahati.<br><br>Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo mahācoro santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.<br><br>Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco pāpabhikkhu suddhaṁ brahmacāriṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ carantaṁ amūlakena abrahmacariyena anuddhaṁseti.<br><br>Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo mahācoro santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.<br><br>Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco pāpabhikkhu yāni tāni saṅghassa garubhaṇḍāni garuparikkhārāni, seyyathidaṁ—<br><br>ārāmo ārāmavatthu vihāro vihāravatthu mañco pīṭhaṁ bhisi bibbohanaṁ lohakumbhī lohabhāṇakaṁ lohavārako lohakaṭāhaṁ vāsi parasu kuṭhārī kudālo nikhādanaṁ valli veḷu muñjaṁ pabbajaṁ tiṇaṁ mattikā dārubhaṇḍaṁ mattikābhaṇḍaṁ,<br><br>tehi gihiṁ saṅgaṇhāti upalāpeti.<br><br>Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho mahācoro santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.<br><br>Sadevake, bhikkhave, loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ayaṁ aggo mahācoro yo asantaṁ abhūtaṁ uttarimanussadhammaṁ ullapati.<br><br>Taṁ kissa hetu?<br><br>Theyyāya vo, bhikkhave, raṭṭhapiṇḍo bhutto”ti.<br><br>Aññathā santamattānaṁ,<br><br>aññathā yo pavedaye;<br><br>Nikacca kitavasseva,<br><br>bhuttaṁ theyyena tassa taṁ.<br><br>Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo,<br><br>pāpadhammā asaññatā;<br><br>Pāpā pāpehi kammehi,<br><br>nirayaṁ te upapajjare.<br><br>Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto,<br><br>tatto aggisikhūpamo;<br><br>Yañce bhuñjeyya dussīlo,<br><br>raṭṭhapiṇḍaṁ asaññatoti.<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya dupposatāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—<br><br>“Yo pana bhikkhu anabhijānaṁ uttarimanussadhammaṁ attupanāyikaṁ alamariyañāṇadassanaṁ samudācareyya—‘iti jānāmi iti passāmī’ti,<br><br>tato aparena samayena samanuggāhīyamāno vā asamanuggāhīyamāno vā āpanno visuddhāpekkho evaṁ vadeyya—‘ajānamevaṁ, āvuso, avacaṁ jānāmi, apassaṁ passāmi. Tucchaṁ musā vilapin’ti,<br><br>ayampi pārājiko hoti asaṁvāso”ti.<br><br>Evañcidaṁ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ hoti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū adiṭṭhe diṭṭhasaññino apatte pattasaññino anadhigate adhigatasaññino asacchikate sacchikatasaññino adhimānena aññaṁ byākariṁsu.<br><br>Tesaṁ aparena samayena rāgāyapi cittaṁ namati dosāyapi cittaṁ namati mohāyapi cittaṁ namati.<br><br>Tesaṁ kukkuccaṁ ahosi—<br><br>“bhagavatā sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ.<br><br>Mayañcamha adiṭṭhe diṭṭhasaññino apatte pattasaññino anadhigate adhigatasaññino asacchikate sacchikatasaññino, adhimānena aññaṁ byākarimhā.<br><br>Kacci nu kho mayaṁ pārājikaṁ āpattiṁ āpannā”ti?<br><br>Te āyasmato ānandassa etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.<br><br>Āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesi.<br><br>“Honti ye te, ānanda, bhikkhū adiṭṭhe diṭṭhasaññino apatte pattasaññino anadhigate adhigatasaññino asacchikate sacchikatasaññino adhimānena aññaṁ byākaronti.<br><br>Tañca kho etaṁ abbohārikan”ti.<br><br>“Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—	Yo panāti<br><br>yo yādiso …pe…<br><br>bhikkhūti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.<br><br>Anabhijānanti<br><br>asantaṁ abhūtaṁ asaṁvijjamānaṁ ajānanto apassanto attani kusalaṁ dhammaṁ— atthi me kusalo dhammoti.<br><br>Uttarimanussadhammo nāma<br><br>jhānaṁ vimokkho samādhi samāpatti ñāṇadassanaṁ maggabhāvanā phalasacchikiriyā kilesappahānaṁ vinīvaraṇatā cittassa suññāgāre abhirati.<br><br>Attupanāyikanti<br><br>te vā kusale dhamme attani upaneti attānaṁ vā tesu kusalesu dhammesu upaneti.<br><br>Ñāṇanti<br><br>tisso vijjā.<br><br>Dassananti<br><br>yaṁ ñāṇaṁ taṁ dassanaṁ, yaṁ dassanaṁ taṁ ñāṇaṁ.<br><br>Samudācareyyāti<br><br>āroceyya itthiyā vā purisassa vā gahaṭṭhassa vā pabbajitassa vā.<br><br>Iti jānāmi iti passāmīti<br><br>jānāmahaṁ ete dhamme, passāmahaṁ ete dhamme atthi ca ete dhammā mayi, ahañca etesu dhammesu sandissāmīti.<br><br>Tato aparena samayenāti<br><br>yasmiṁ khaṇe samudāciṇṇaṁ hoti taṁ khaṇaṁ taṁ layaṁ taṁ muhuttaṁ vītivatte.<br><br>Samanuggāhīyamānoti<br><br>yaṁ vatthu paṭiññātaṁ hoti tasmiṁ vatthusmiṁ samanuggāhīyamāno—<br><br>“kinte adhigataṁ,<br><br>kinti te adhigataṁ,<br><br>kadā te adhigataṁ,<br><br>kattha te adhigataṁ,<br><br>katame te kilesā pahīnā,<br><br>katamesaṁ tvaṁ dhammānaṁ lābhī”ti.<br><br>Asamanuggāhīyamānoti<br><br>na kenaci vuccamāno.<br><br>Āpannoti<br><br>pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṁ abhūtaṁ uttarimanussadhammaṁ ullapitvā pārājikaṁ āpattiṁ āpanno hoti.<br><br>Visuddhāpekkhoti<br><br>gihī vā hotukāmo upāsako vā hotukāmo ārāmiko vā hotukāmo sāmaṇero vā hotukāmo.<br><br>Ajānamevaṁ, āvuso, avacaṁ—jānāmi, apassaṁ passāmīti<br><br>nāhaṁ ete dhamme jānāmi, nāhaṁ ete dhamme passāmi, natthi ca ete dhammā mayi, na cāhaṁ etesu dhammesu sandissāmīti.<br><br>Tucchaṁ musā vilapinti<br><br>tucchakaṁ mayā bhaṇitaṁ, musā mayā bhaṇitaṁ, abhūtaṁ mayā bhaṇitaṁ, ajānantena mayā bhaṇitaṁ.<br><br>Aññatra adhimānāti<br><br>ṭhapetvā adhimānaṁ.<br><br>Ayampīti<br><br>purime upādāya vuccati.<br><br>Pārājiko hotīti<br><br>seyyathāpi nāma tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna virūḷhiyā;<br><br>evameva bhikkhu pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṁ abhūtaṁ uttarimanussadhammaṁ ullapitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo.<br><br>Tena vuccati— “pārājiko hotī”ti.<br><br>Asaṁvāsoti<br><br>saṁvāso nāma ekakammaṁ ekuddeso samasikkhatā— eso saṁvāso nāma.<br><br>So tena saddhiṁ natthi. Tena vuccati— “asaṁvāso”ti.<br><br>Uttarimanussadhammo nāma<br><br>jhānaṁ vimokkho samādhi samāpatti ñāṇadassanaṁ maggabhāvanā phalasacchikiriyā kilesappahānaṁ vinīvaraṇatā cittassa suññāgāre abhirati.<br><br>Jhānanti<br><br>paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ.<br><br>Vimokkhoti<br><br>suññato vimokkho animitto vimokkho appaṇihito vimokkho.<br><br>Samādhīti<br><br>suññato samādhi animitto samādhi appaṇihito samādhi.<br><br>Samāpattīti<br><br>suññatā samāpatti animittā samāpatti appaṇihitā samāpatti.<br><br>Ñāṇadassananti<br><br>tisso vijjā.<br><br>Maggabhāvanāti<br><br>cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo.<br><br>Phalasacchikiriyāti<br><br>sotāpattiphalassa sacchikiriyā, sakadāgāmiphalassa sacchikiriyā, anāgāmiphalassa sacchikiriyā, arahattassa sacchikiriyā.<br><br>Kilesappahānanti<br><br>rāgassa pahānaṁ dosassa pahānaṁ mohassa pahānaṁ.<br><br>Vinīvaraṇatā cittassāti<br><br>rāgā cittaṁ vinīvaraṇatā, dosā cittaṁ vinīvaraṇatā, mohā cittaṁ vinīvaraṇatā.<br><br>Suññāgāre abhiratīti<br><br>paṭhamena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati,<br><br>dutiyena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati,<br><br>tatiyena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati,<br><br>catutthena jhānena suññāgāre abhirati.<br><br>Tīhākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjinti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissanti,<br><br>bhaṇantassa hoti musā bhaṇāmīti,<br><br>bhaṇitassa hoti musā mayā bhaṇitanti.<br><br>Catūhākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjinti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissanti,<br><br>bhaṇantassa hoti musā bhaṇāmīti,<br><br>bhaṇitassa hoti musā mayā bhaṇitanti,<br><br>vinidhāya diṭṭhiṁ.<br><br>Pañcahākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjinti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissanti,<br><br>bhaṇantassa hoti musā bhaṇāmīti,<br><br>bhaṇitassa hoti musā mayā bhaṇitanti,<br><br>vinidhāya diṭṭhiṁ vinidhāya khantiṁ.<br><br>Chahākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjinti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissanti,<br><br>bhaṇantassa hoti musā bhaṇāmīti,<br><br>bhaṇitassa hoti musā mayā bhaṇitanti,<br><br>vinidhāya diṭṭhiṁ,<br><br>vinidhāya khantiṁ,<br><br>vinidhāya ruciṁ.<br><br>Sattahākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjinti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissanti,<br><br>bhaṇantassa hoti musā bhaṇāmīti,<br><br>bhaṇitassa hoti musā mayā bhaṇitanti,<br><br>vinidhāya diṭṭhiṁ,<br><br>vinidhāya khantiṁ,<br><br>vinidhāya ruciṁ,<br><br>vinidhāya bhāvaṁ.<br><br>Tīhākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmīti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>pubbevassa hoti musā bhaṇissanti,<br><br>bhaṇantassa hoti musā bhaṇāmīti,<br><br>bhaṇitassa hoti musā mayā bhaṇitanti.<br><br>Catūhākārehi paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajjāmīti sampajānamusā bhaṇantassa āpatti etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“atthāyasmato uttarimanussadhammo”ti?<br><br>“Ārādhanīyo kho, āvuso, dhammo āraddhavīriyenā”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“anāpatti, bhikkhu, anullapanādhippāyassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti.<br><br>Taṁ bhikkhū etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“atthāyasmato uttarimanussadhammo”ti?<br><br>“Ārādhanīyo kho, āvuso, dhammo yuttayogenā”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“anāpatti, bhikkhu, anullapanādhippāyassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti.<br><br>Taṁ bhikkhū etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“kaccāvuso, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyan”ti?<br><br>“Nāvuso, sakkā yena vā tena vā adhivāsetun”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“anāpatti, bhikkhu, anullapanādhippāyassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti.<br><br>Taṁ bhikkhū etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“kaccāvuso, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyan”ti?<br><br>“Nāvuso, sakkā puthujjanena adhivāsetun”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“kiṁcitto tvaṁ, bhikkhū”ti?<br><br>“Ullapanādhippāyo ahaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>“Anāpatti, bhikkhu, pārājikassa;<br><br>āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro brāhmaṇo bhikkhū nimantetvā etadavoca—<br><br>“āyantu bhonto arahanto”ti.<br><br>Tesaṁ kukkuccaṁ ahosi—<br><br>“mayañcamha na arahanto.<br><br>Ayañca brāhmaṇo amhe arahantavādena samudācarati.<br><br>Kathaṁ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabban”ti?<br><br>Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.<br><br>“Anāpatti, bhikkhave, pasādabhaññe”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro brāhmaṇo bhikkhū nimantetvā etadavoca—<br><br>“nisīdantu bhonto arahanto”ti …<br><br>“bhuñjantu bhonto arahanto”ti …<br><br>“tappentu bhonto arahanto”ti …<br><br>“gacchantu, bhonto arahanto”ti.<br><br>Tesaṁ kukkuccaṁ ahosi—<br><br>“mayañcamha na arahanto.<br><br>Ayañca brāhmaṇo amhe arahantavādena samudācarati.<br><br>Kathaṁ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabban”ti?<br><br>Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.<br><br>“Anāpatti, bhikkhave, pasādabhaññe”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu aññatarassa bhikkhuno uttarimanussadhammaṁ ullapati.<br><br>Sopi evamāha—“mayhampi, āvuso, āsavā pahīnā”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“āpattiṁ tvaṁ, bhikkhu, āpanno pārājikan”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu pārājikan”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu aññatarassa bhikkhuno uttarimanussadhammaṁ ullapati.<br><br>Sopi evamāha—“ahampāvuso, tesu dhammesu sandissāmī”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“āpattiṁ tvaṁ, bhikkhu, āpanno pārājikan”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ ñātakā etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“ehi, bhante, agāraṁ ajjhāvasā”ti.<br><br>“Abhabbo kho, āvuso, mādiso agāraṁ ajjhāvasitun”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“anāpatti, bhikkhu, anullapanādhippāyassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ ñātakā etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“ehi, bhante, kāme paribhuñjā”ti.<br><br>“Āvaṭā me, āvuso, kāmā”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“anāpatti, bhikkhu, anullapanādhippāyassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ ñātakā etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“abhiramasi, bhante”ti?<br><br>“Abhirato ahaṁ, āvuso, paramāya abhiratiyā”ti.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi.<br><br>“Ye kho te bhagavato sāvakā te evaṁ vadeyyuṁ.<br><br>Ahañcamhi na bhagavato sāvako.<br><br>Kacci nu kho ahaṁ pārājikaṁ āpattiṁ āpanno”ti?<br><br>Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesi.<br><br>“Kiṁcitto tvaṁ, bhikkhū”ti?<br><br>“Anullapanādhippāyo ahaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>“Anāpatti, bhikkhu, anullapanādhippāyassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū katikaṁ katvā aññatarasmiṁ āvāse vassaṁ upagacchiṁsu—<br><br>“yo imamhā āvāsā paṭhamaṁ pakkamissati taṁ mayaṁ arahāti jānissāmā”ti.<br><br>Aññataro bhikkhu—<br><br>“maṁ arahāti jānantū”ti,<br><br>tamhā āvāsā paṭhamaṁ pakkāmi.<br><br>Tassa kukkuccaṁ ahosi …pe…<br><br>“āpattiṁ tvaṁ, bhikkhu, āpanno pārājikan”ti.<br><br>Tena samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca lakkhaṇo āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharanti.<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaraṁ ādāya yenāyasmā lakkhaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ lakkhaṇaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“āyāmāvuso aññatarasmiṁ padese sitaṁ pātvākāsi.<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“ko nu kho, āvuso moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā”ti?<br><br>“Akālo kho, āvuso lakkhaṇa, etassa pañhassa.<br><br>Bhagavato maṁ santike etaṁ pañhaṁ pucchā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā ca lakkhaṇo āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu;<br><br>upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.<br><br>Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“idhāyasmā mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto aññatarasmiṁ padese sitaṁ pātvākāsi.<br><br>Ko nu kho, āvuso moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā”ti?<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantiṁ.<br><br>Tamenaṁ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā phāsuḷantarikāhi vituḍenti.<br><br>Sā sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ karoti.<br><br>Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi—<br><br>‘acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, evarūpopi nāma satto bhavissati.<br><br>Evarūpopi nāma yakkho bhavissati.<br><br>Evarūpopi nāma attabhāvappaṭilābho bhavissatī’”ti.<br><br>Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“uttarimanussadhammaṁ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno ullapatī”ti.<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi—<br><br>“cakkhubhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti.<br><br>Ñāṇabhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti.<br><br>Yatra hi nāma sāvako evarūpaṁ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sakkhiṁ vā karissati.<br><br>Pubbeva me so, bhikkhave, satto diṭṭho ahosi.<br><br>Api cāhaṁ na byākāsiṁ.<br><br>Ahañcetaṁ byākareyyaṁ pare ca me na saddaheyyuṁ.<br><br>Ye me na saddaheyyuṁ tesaṁ taṁ assa dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.<br><br>Eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe goghātako ahosi.<br><br>So tassa kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni niraye paccitvā tasseva kammassa vipākāvasesena evarūpaṁ attabhāvappaṭilābhaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.<br><br>Saccaṁ, bhikkhave, moggallāno āha.<br><br>Anāpatti, bhikkhave, moggallānassā”ti.<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ maṁsapesiṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantiṁ.<br><br>Tamenaṁ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti vibhajjenti.<br><br>Sā sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ karoti …pe…<br><br>eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe goghātako ahosi …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ maṁsapiṇḍaṁ sākuṇiko ahosi …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ nicchaviṁ purisaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.<br><br>Tamenaṁ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti vibhajjenti.<br><br>So sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ karoti …pe…<br><br>eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe orabbhiko ahosi …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ asilomaṁ purisaṁ …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ sattilomaṁ purisaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.<br><br>Tassa tā sattiyo uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti.<br><br>So sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti.<br><br>So sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ karoti …pe…<br><br>eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe kāraṇiko ahosi …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ sūcilomaṁ purisaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.<br><br>Tassa tā sūciyo uppatitvā uppatitvā tasseva kāye nipatanti.<br><br>So sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ karoti …pe…<br><br>eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe sārathiko ahosi …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ sūcilomaṁ purisaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.<br><br>Tassa tā sūciyo sīse pavisitvā mukhato nikkhamanti;<br><br>mukhe pavisitvā urato nikkhamanti;<br><br>ure pavisitvā udarato nikkhamanti;<br><br>udare pavisitvā ūrūhi nikkhamanti;<br><br>ūrūsu pavisitvā jaṅghāhi nikkhamanti;<br><br>jaṅghāsu kumbhaṇḍaṁ purisaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.<br><br>So gacchantopi teva aṇḍe khandhe āropetvā gacchati,<br><br>nisīdantopi tesveva aṇḍesu nisīdati.<br><br>Tamenaṁ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā …pe….<br><br>“Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ bhikkhuṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.<br><br>Tassa saṅghāṭipi ādittā sampajjalitā sajotibhūtā, pattopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto, sajotibhūto.<br><br>Sā sudaṁ aṭṭassaraṁ karoti.<br><br>Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi—<br><br>‘acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, evarūpopi nāma satto bhavissati.<br><br>Evarūpopi nāma yakkho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi—<br><br>“cakkhubhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti.<br><br>Ñāṇabhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti.<br><br>Yatra hi nāma sāvako evarūpaṁ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sakkhiṁ dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.<br><br>Esā, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane pāpasāmaṇerī ahosi.<br><br>Sā tassa kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni bhikkhave, moggallānassā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi—<br><br>“yatāyaṁ, āvuso, tapodā sandati so daho acchodako sītodako sātodako setako suppatittho ramaṇīyo pahūtamacchakacchapo cakkamattāni ca padumāni pupphantī”ti.<br><br>Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma āyasmā mahāmoggallāno evaṁ vakkhati—<br><br>‘yatāyaṁ, āvuso, tapodā [sound:ABi_PJ_4.mp3]	{-superhuman states} Should any bhikkhunī, without direct knowledge, boast of a superior human state, a truly noble knowledge and vision as present in herself, saying, “Thus do I know; thus do I see,” such that regardless of whether or not she is cross-examined on a later occasion, she—being remorseful and desirous of purification—might say, “Venerables, not knowing, I said I know; not seeing, I said I see—vainly, falsely, idly,” unless it was from overestimation, she also is defeated and no longer in communion. Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ_3.mp3]	29	At one time the Buddha was staying in the house with the peaked roof in the Great Wood near Vesālī.<br><br>At that time the Buddha spoke to the monks in many ways about unattractiveness—he spoke in praise of unattractiveness, of developing the mind in unattractiveness, and of the attainment of unattractiveness.<br><br>The Buddha then addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, I wish to go into solitary retreat for half a month.<br><br>No one should visit me except the one who brings me almsfood.”<br><br>“Yes, venerable sir.”<br><br>Soon afterwards the monks reflected that the Buddha had praised unattractiveness in many ways,<br><br>and they devoted themselves to developing the mind in unattractiveness in its many different facets.<br><br>As a consequence, they became troubled by their own bodies, ashamed of and disgusted with them.<br><br>Just as a young woman or man—someone fond of adornments, with freshly washed hair—would be ashamed, humiliated, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, dog, or man was hung around her neck,<br><br>just so those monks were troubled by their own bodies.<br><br>They took their own lives, took the lives of one another,<br><br>and they went to Migalaṇḍika, the monastic lookalike, and said,<br><br>“Please kill us.<br><br>You will get our bowl and robes.”<br><br>And hired for a bowl and robes, Migalaṇḍika killed a number of monks. He then took his blood-stained knife to the river Vaggumudā.<br><br>While washing it, he became anxious and remorseful, thinking,<br><br>“What the heck have I done?<br><br>I’ve made so much demerit by killing good monks.”<br><br>Then a god from the realm of the Lord of Death, coming across the water, said to Migalaṇḍika,<br><br>“Well done, superior man, you’re truly fortunate.<br><br>You’ve made much merit by helping across those who hadn’t yet crossed.”<br><br>Migalaṇḍika thought,<br><br>“So it seems that I’m fortunate, that I’ve made much merit!”<br><br>He then went from dwelling to dwelling, from yard to yard, and said,<br><br>“Who hasn’t crossed yet? Who can I help across?”<br><br>The monks who still had worldly attachments became fearful and terrified, with goosebumps all over.<br><br>Only those who were free from worldly attachments were unaffected.<br><br>Then, on a single day, Migalaṇḍika killed one monk, two monks, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, even sixty monks.<br><br>At the end of that half-month, when the Buddha came out of seclusion, he said to Venerable Ānanda,<br><br>“Ānanda, why is the Sangha of monks so reduced?”<br><br>Ānanda told him what had happened,<br><br>adding, “Please give another instruction, sir, for the Sangha of monks to become established in perfect insight.”<br><br>“Well then, Ānanda, bring together in the assembly hall all the monks who live supported by Vesālī.”<br><br>“Yes.”<br><br>When he had done so, he went to the Buddha and said,<br><br>“Sir, the Sangha of monks is gathered.<br><br>Please do as you think appropriate.”<br><br>The Buddha then went to the assembly hall, sat down on the prepared seat, and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, when stillness by mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated, it is peaceful and sublime, and a satisfying state of bliss. And it removes bad and unwholesome qualities on the spot, whenever they arise.<br><br>Just as a great, unseasonal storm in the last month of summer removes the dust and dirt from the air,<br><br>just so, when stillness by mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated, it is peaceful and sublime, and it removes bad and unwholesome qualities on the spot, whenever they arise.<br><br>And how is stillness by mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated in this way?<br><br>A monk sits down in the wilderness, at the foot of a tree, or in an empty hut. He crosses his legs, straightens his body, and sets up mindfulness in front of him.<br><br>Simply mindful, he breathes in; mindful, he breathes out.<br><br>When he breathes in long, he knows it; and when he breathes out long, he knows that.<br><br>When he breathes in short, he knows it; and when he breathes out short, he knows that.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in fully experiencing the breath; when breathing out, he trains in fully experiencing the breath.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in calming the activity of the body; when breathing out, he trains in calming the activity of the body.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in experiencing joy; when breathing out, he trains in experiencing joy.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in experiencing bliss; when breathing out, he trains in experiencing bliss.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in experiencing the activity of the mind; when breathing out, he trains in experiencing the activity of the mind.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in calming the activity of the mind; when breathing out, he trains in calming the activity of the mind.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in experiencing the mind; when breathing out, he trains in experiencing the mind.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in gladdening the mind; when breathing out, he trains in gladdening the mind.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in stilling the mind; when breathing out, he trains in stilling the mind.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in freeing the mind; when breathing out, he trains in freeing the mind.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in contemplating impermanence; when breathing out, he trains in contemplating impermanence.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in contemplating fading away; when breathing out, he trains in contemplating fading away.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in contemplating ending; when breathing out, he trains in contemplating ending.<br><br>When breathing in, he trains in contemplating relinquishment; when breathing out, he trains in contemplating relinquishment.<br><br>Monks, when stillness by mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated like this, it is peaceful and sublime, and a satisfying state of bliss. And it removes bad and unwholesome qualities on the spot, whenever they arise.”<br><br>The Buddha then had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that there are monks who have taken their own lives, who have killed one another, and who have said to Migalaṇḍika,<br><br>‘Please kill us. You will get our bowl and robes’?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them,<br><br>“Monks, it’s not suitable for these monks, it’s not proper, it’s not worthy of a monastic, it’s not allowable, it’s not to be done.<br><br>How could those monks do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:<br><br>‘If a monk intentionally kills a human being or seeks an instrument of death for them,<br><br>he too is expelled and excluded from the community.’”<br><br>In this way the Buddha laid down this training rule for the monks.<br><br>At one time a certain lay follower was sick.<br><br>He had a beautiful and pleasant wife,<br><br>who the monks from the group of six had fallen in love with.<br><br>They said to each other,<br><br>“If this lay follower recovers, we won’t get her.<br><br>Come, let’s praise death to him.”<br><br>They then went to that lay follower and said,<br><br>“You’ve done what’s good and wholesome; you’ve made a shelter against fear. You haven’t done anything bad; you haven’t been greedy or immoral.<br><br>So why carry on with this miserable and difficult life?<br><br>Death is better for you.<br><br>When you’ve passed away, you’ll be reborn in a happy place, in heaven.<br><br>There you’ll be able to enjoy the pleasures of heaven.”<br><br>That lay follower thought,<br><br>“The venerables have spoken the truth,<br><br>for I’ve done what’s good and avoided what’s bad,<br><br>and after death I’ll be reborn in a happy place.”<br><br>From then on he ate various kinds of detrimental food and drank detrimental drinks,<br><br>and as a consequence, he became very ill<br><br>and died.<br><br>But his wife complained and criticized those monks,<br><br>“These Sakyan monastics are shameless and immoral liars.<br><br>They claim to have integrity, to be celibate and of good conduct, to be truthful, moral, and good.<br><br>But they don’t have the good character of a monastic or a brahmin.<br><br>They’ve lost the plot!<br><br>They praised death to my husband,<br><br>and as a result my husband is dead.”<br><br>And other people complained and criticized them in the same way.<br><br>The monks heard the criticism of those There is no offense:<br><br>if it is unintentional;<br><br>if he does not know;<br><br>if he is not aiming at death;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The first section for recitation on expulsion in relation to human beings is finished.<br><br>Summary verses of case studies<br><br>“Praising, sitting down,<br><br>And with pestle, with mortar;<br><br>Gone akaraṇīyaṁ.<br><br>Kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū attanāpi attānaṁ jīvitā voropessanti, aññamaññampi jīvitā voropessanti, migalaṇḍikampi samaṇakuttakaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vakkhanti—<br><br>‘sādhu no, āvuso, jīvitā voropehi, idaṁ te pattacīvaraṁ bhavissatī’ti.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—<br><br>“Yo pana bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṁ jīvitā voropeyya satthahārakaṁ vāssa pariyeseyya,<br><br>ayampi pārājiko hoti asaṁvāso”ti.<br><br>Evañcidaṁ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ hoti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako gilāno hoti.<br><br>Tassa pajāpati abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā.<br><br>Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tassā itthiyā paṭibaddhacittā honti.<br><br>Atha kho chabbaggiyānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi—<br><br>“sace kho so, āvuso, upāsako jīvissati na mayaṁ taṁ itthiṁ labhissāma.<br><br>Handa mayaṁ, āvuso, tassa upāsakassa maraṇavaṇṇaṁ saṁvaṇṇemā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yena so upāsako tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ upāsakaṁ etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“tvaṁ khosi, upāsaka, katakalyāṇo katakusalo katabhīruttāṇo akatapāpo akataluddo akatakibbiso.<br><br>Kataṁ tayā kalyāṇaṁ, akataṁ tayā pāpaṁ.<br><br>Kiṁ tuyhiminā pāpakena dujjīvitena.<br><br>Mataṁ te jīvitā seyyo.<br><br>Ito tvaṁ kālaṅkato kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjissasi.<br><br>Tattha dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāressasī”ti.<br><br>Atha kho so upāsako—<br><br>“saccaṁ kho ayyā āhaṁsu.<br><br>Ahañhi katakalyāṇo katakusalo katabhīruttāṇo akatapāpo akataluddo akatakibbiso.<br><br>Kataṁ mayā kalyāṇaṁ, akataṁ mayā pāpaṁ.<br><br>Kiṁ mayhiminā pāpakena dujjīvitena.<br><br>Mataṁ me jīvitā seyyo.<br><br>Ito ahaṁ kālaṅkato kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjissāmi.<br><br>Tattha dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāressāmī”ti,<br><br>so asappāyāni ceva bhojanāni bhuñji asappāyāni ca khādanīyāni khādi asappāyāni ca sāyanīyāni sāyi asappāyāni ca pānāni pivi.<br><br>Tassa asappāyāni ceva bhojanāni bhuñjato asappāyāni ca khādanīyāni khādato asappāyāni ca sāyanīyāni sāyato asappāyāni ca pānāni pivato kharo ābādho uppajji.<br><br>So teneva ābādhena kālamakāsi.<br><br>Tassa pajāpati ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti—<br><br>“alajjino ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dussīlā musāvādino.<br><br>Ime hi nāma dhammacārino samacārino brahmacārino saccavādino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā paṭijānissanti.<br><br>Natthi imesaṁ sāmaññaṁ natthi imesaṁ brahmaññaṁ,<br><br>naṭṭhaṁ imesaṁ sāmaññaṁ naṭṭhaṁ imesaṁ brahmaññaṁ, kuto imesaṁ sāmaññaṁ kuto imesaṁ brahmaññaṁ, apagatā ime sāmaññā apagatā ime brahmaññā.<br><br>Ime me sāmikassa maraṇavaṇṇaṁ saṁvaṇṇesuṁ.<br><br>Imehi me sāmiko mārito”ti.<br><br>Aññepi manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“alajjino ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dussīlā musāvādino.<br><br>Ime hi nāma dhammacārino samacārino brahmacārino saccavādino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā paṭijānissanti.<br><br>Natthi imesaṁ sāmaññaṁ natthi imesaṁ brahmaññaṁ, naṭṭhaṁ imesaṁ sāmaññaṁ naṭṭhaṁ imesaṁ brahmaññaṁ, kuto imesaṁ sāmaññaṁ kuto imesaṁ brahmaññaṁ, apagatā ime sāmaññā apagatā ime brahmaññā.<br><br>Ime upāsakassa maraṇavaṇṇaṁ saṁvaṇṇesuṁ.<br><br>Imehi upāsako mārito”ti.<br><br>Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū upāsakassa maraṇavaṇṇaṁ saṁvaṇṇissantī”ti.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, upāsakassa maraṇavaṇṇaṁ saṁvaṇṇethā”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā—<br><br>“ananucchavikaṁ, moghapurisā, ananulomikaṁ appaṭirūpaṁ assāmaṇakaṁ akappiyaṁ akaraṇīyaṁ.<br><br>Kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, upāsakassa maraṇavaṇṇaṁ saṁvaṇṇissatha.<br><br>Netaṁ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—	Yo panāti<br><br>yo yādiso …pe…<br><br>bhikkhūti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.<br><br>Sañciccāti<br><br>jānanto sañjānanto cecca abhivitaritvā vītikkamo.<br><br>Manussaviggaho nāma<br><br>yaṁ mātukucchismiṁ paṭhamaṁ cittaṁ uppannaṁ paṭhamaṁ viññāṇaṁ pātubhūtaṁ, yāva maraṇakālā etthantare eso manussaviggaho nāma.<br><br>Jīvitā voropeyyāti<br><br>jīvitindriyaṁ upacchindati uparodheti santatiṁ vikopeti.<br><br>Satthahārakaṁ vāssa pariyeseyyāti<br><br>asiṁ vā sattiṁ vā bheṇḍiṁ vā laguḷaṁ vā pāsāṇaṁ vā satthaṁ vā visaṁ vā rajjuṁ vā.<br><br>Maraṇavaṇṇaṁ vā saṁvaṇṇeyyāti<br><br>jīvite ādīnavaṁ dasseti, maraṇe vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati.<br><br>Maraṇāya vā samādapeyyāti<br><br>satthaṁ vā āhara, visaṁ vā khāda, rajjuyā vā ubbandhitvā kālaṁ karohīti.<br><br>Ambho purisāti<br><br>ālapanādhivacanametaṁ.<br><br>Kiṁ tuyhiminā pāpakena dujjīvitenāti<br><br>pāpakaṁ nāma jīvitaṁ<br><br>aḍḍhānaṁ jīvitaṁ upādāya daliddānaṁ jīvitaṁ pāpakaṁ lāmakaṁ,<br><br>sadhanānaṁ jīvitaṁ upādāya adhanānaṁ jīvitaṁ pāpakaṁ,<br><br>devānaṁ jīvitaṁ upādāya manussānaṁ jīvitaṁ pāpakaṁ.<br><br>Dujjīvitaṁ nāma<br><br>hatthacchinnassa pādacchinnassa hatthapādacchinnassa kaṇṇacchinnassa nāsacchinnassa kaṇṇanāsacchinnassa,<br><br>iminā ca pāpakena iminā ca dujjīvitena mataṁ te jīvitā seyyoti.<br><br>Iti cittamanoti<br><br>yaṁ cittaṁ taṁ mano, yaṁ mano taṁ cittaṁ.<br><br>Cittasaṅkappoti<br><br>maraṇasaññī maraṇacetano maraṇādhippāyo.<br><br>Anekapariyāyenāti<br><br>uccāvacehi ākārehi.<br><br>Maraṇavaṇṇaṁ vā saṁvaṇṇeyyāti<br><br>jīvite ādīnavaṁ dasseti, maraṇe vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati—<br><br>“ito tvaṁ kālaṅkato kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjissasi,<br><br>tattha dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāressasī”ti.<br><br>Maraṇāya vā samādapeyyāti<br><br>satthaṁ vā āhara, visaṁ vā khāda, rajjuyā vā ubbandhitvā kālaṁ karohi, sobbhe vā narake vā papāte vā papatāti.<br><br>Ayampīti<br><br>purime upādāya vuccati.<br><br>Pārājiko hotīti<br><br>seyyathāpi nāma puthusilā dvidhā bhinnā appaṭisandhikā hoti,<br><br>evameva bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṁ jīvitā voropetvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo.<br><br>Tena vuccati— “pārājiko hotī”ti.<br><br>Asaṁvāsoti<br><br>saṁvāso nāma ekakammaṁ ekuddeso samasikkhatā— eso saṁvāso nāma.<br><br>So tena saddhiṁ natthi, tena vuccati asaṁvāsoti.<br><br>Sāmaṁ, adhiṭṭhāya, dūtena, dūtaparamparāya, visakkiyena dūtena, gatapaccāgatena dūtena,<br><br>araho rahosaññī,<br><br>raho arahosaññī,<br><br>araho arahosaññī,<br><br>raho rūpūpahāro, saddūpahāro, gandhūpahāro, rasūpahāro, phoṭṭhabbūpahāro, dhammūpahāro, ācikkhanā, anusāsanī, saṅketakammaṁ, nimittakammanti.<br><br>Sāmanti<br><br>sayaṁ hanati kāyena vā kāyapaṭibaddhena vā nissaggiyena vā.<br><br>Adhiṭṭhāyāti<br><br>adhiṭṭhahitvā āṇāpeti— “evaṁ vijjha, evaṁ pahara, evaṁ ghātehī”ti.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So taṁ maññamāno taṁ jīvitā voropeti, āpatti ubhinnaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So taṁ maññamāno aññaṁ jīvitā voropeti, mūlaṭṭhassa anāpatti. Vadhakassa āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So aññaṁ maññamāno taṁ jīvitā voropeti, āpatti ubhinnaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So aññaṁ maññamāno aññaṁ jīvitā voropeti; mūlaṭṭhassa anāpatti, vadhakassa āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmassa pāvada—‘itthannāmo itthannāmassa pāvadatu—itthannāmo itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropetū’”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So itarassa āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Vadhako paṭiggaṇhāti, mūlaṭṭhassa āpatti thullaccayassa.<br><br>So taṁ jīvitā voropeti, āpatti sabbesaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmassa pāvada—‘itthannāmo itthannāmassa pāvadatu—itthannāmo itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropetū’”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So aññaṁ āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Vadhako paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So taṁ jīvitā voropeti, mūlaṭṭhassa anāpatti;<br><br>āṇāpakassa ca vadhakassa ca āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So gantvā puna paccāgacchati— “nāhaṁ sakkomi taṁ jīvitā voropetun”ti.<br><br>So puna āṇāpeti— “yadā sakkosi tadā taṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So taṁ jīvitā voropeti, āpatti ubhinnaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So āṇāpetvā vippaṭisārī na sāveti— “mā ghātehī”ti.<br><br>So taṁ jīvitā voropeti, āpatti ubhinnaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So āṇāpetvā vippaṭisārī sāveti— “mā ghātehī”ti.<br><br>So—“āṇatto ahaṁ tayā”ti taṁ jīvitā voropeti, mūlaṭṭhassa anāpatti. Vadhakassa āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti— “itthannāmaṁ jīvitā voropehī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So āṇāpetvā vippaṭisārī sāveti— “mā ghātehī”ti.<br><br>So sādhūti oramati, ubhinnaṁ anāpatti.<br><br>Araho rahosaññī<br><br>ullapati— “aho itthannāmo hato assā”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Raho arahosaññī<br><br>ullapati— “aho itthannāmo hato assā”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Kāyena saṁvaṇṇeti nāma<br><br>kāyena vikāraṁ karoti— “yo evaṁ marati so dhanaṁ vā labhati yasaṁ vā labhati saggaṁ vā gacchatī”ti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Tāya saṁvaṇṇanāya Vinītavatthuuddānagāthā<br><br>Saṁvaṇṇanā nisīdanto,<br><br>musalodukkhalena ca;<br><br>Vuḍḍhapabbajitābhisanno,<br><br>aggavīmaṁsanāvisaṁ.<br><br>Tayo ca vatthukammehi,<br><br>iṭṭhakāhipare tayo;<br><br>Vāsī gopānasī ceva,<br><br>aṭṭakotaraṇaṁ pati.<br><br>Sedaṁ natthuñca sambāho,<br><br>nhāpanabbhañjanena ca;<br><br>Uṭṭhāpento nipātento,<br><br>annapānena māraṇaṁ.<br><br>Jāragabbho sapattī ca,<br><br>mātā puttaṁ ubho vadhi;<br><br>Ubho na miyyare maddā,<br><br>tāpaṁ vañjhā vijāyinī.<br><br>Patodaṁ niggahe yakkho,<br><br>vāḷayakkhañca pāhiṇi;<br><br>Taṁ maññamāno pahari,<br><br>saggañca nirayaṁ bhaṇe.<br><br>Āḷaviyā tayo rukkhā,<br><br>dāyehi apare tayo;<br><br>Mā kilamesi na tuyhaṁ,<br><br>takkaṁ sovīrakena cāti.	[sound:ABi_PJ_3.mp3]	{-killing a human being} Should any bhikkhunī intentionally deprive a human being of life, or search for an assassin for that person, or praise the advantages of death, or incite that person to die (thus): “My good man (or woman), what use is this wretched, miserable life to you? Death would be better for you than life,” or with such an idea in mind, such a purpose in mind, should in various ways praise the advantages of death or incite that person to die, she also is defeated and no longer in communion. [3]	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::3.Pārājikuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI PJ	PJ Full Section Summary	Tatrime aṭṭha pārājikā dhammā uddesaṁ āgacchanti.<br><br>1. Yā pana bhikkhunī chandaso methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭiseveyya, antamaso tiracchānagatenapi, pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā.<br><br>2. Yā pana bhikkhunī gāmā vā araññā vā adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyeyya, yathārūpe adinnādāne rājāno coriṁ gahetvā haneyyuṁ vā bandheyyuṁ vā pabbājeyyuṁ vā corāsi bālāsi mūḷhāsi thenāsīti, tathārūpaṁ bhikkhunī adinnaṁ ādiyamānā ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā.<br><br>3. Yā pana bhikkhunī sañcicca manussaviggahaṁ jīvitā voropeyya, satthahārakaṁ vāssa pariyeseyya, maraṇavaṇṇaṁ vā saṁvaṇṇeyya, maraṇāya vā samādapeyya, “ambho purisa, kiṁ tuyhiminā pāpakena dujjīvitena, mataṁ te jīvitā seyyo”ti, iti cittamanā cittasaṅkappā anekapariyāyena maraṇavaṇṇaṁ vā saṁvaṇṇeyya, maraṇāya vā samādapeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā.<br><br>4. Yā pana bhikkhunī anabhijānaṁ uttarimanussadhammaṁ attupanāyikaṁ alamariyañāṇadassanaṁ samudācareyya, “iti jānāmi, iti passāmī”ti, tato aparena samayena samanuggāhīyamānā vā asamanuggāhīyamānā vā āpannā visuddhāpekkhā evaṁ vadeyya, “ajānamevaṁ, ayye, avacaṁ jānāmi, apassaṁ passāmi, tucchaṁ musā vilapi”nti, aññatra adhimānā, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā.<br><br>5. Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa, adhakkhaṁ ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalaṁ āmasanaṁ vā parāmasanaṁ vā gahaṇaṁ vā chupanaṁ vā paṭipīḷanaṁ vā sādiyeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā ubbhajāṇumaṇḍalikā.<br><br>6. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannaṁ bhikkhuniṁ nevattanā paṭicodeyya, na gaṇassa āroceyya, yadā ca sā ṭhitā vā assa cutā vā nāsitā vā avassaṭā vā, sā pacchā evaṁ vadeyya: “pubbevāhaṁ, ayye, aññāsiṁ etaṁ bhikkhuniṁ ‘evarūpā ca evarūpā ca sā bhaginī’ti, no ca kho attanā paṭicodeyyaṁ, na gaṇassa āroceyya”nti, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā vajjappaṭicchādikā.<br><br>7. Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṁ bhikkhuṁ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaraṁ appaṭikāraṁ akatasahāyaṁ tamanuvatteyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “eso kho, ayye, bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena ukkhitto, dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaro appaṭikāro akatasahāyo, māyye, etaṁ bhikkhuṁ anuvattī”ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyaṁ ce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, <br>no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā ukkhittānuvattikā.<br><br>8. Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇaṁ vā sādiyeyya, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇaṁ vā sādiyeyya, santiṭṭheyya vā, sallapeyya vā, saṅketaṁ vā gaccheyya, purisassa vā abbhāgamanaṁ sādiyeyya, channaṁ vā anupaviseyya, kāyaṁ vā tadatthāya upasaṁhareyya etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā aṭṭhavatthukā.<br><br>Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, aṭṭha pārājikā dhammā. <br>Yesaṁ bhikkhunī aññataraṁ vā aññataraṁ vā āpajjitvā na labhati bhikkhunīhi saddhiṁ saṁvāsaṁ <br>yathā pure, tathā pacchā, pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā. <br>Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>dutiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>tatiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmīti. <br><br>Pārājikuddeso dutiyo. Yā pana bhikkhunī gāmā vā araññā vā adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyeyya, yathārūpe adinnādāne rājāno coraṁ gahetvā haneyyuṁ vā bandheyyuṁ vā pabbājeyyuṁ vā corāsi bālāsi mūḷhāsi thenāsīti, tathārūpaṁ bhikkhunī adinnaṁ ādiyamānā ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā.<br><br>3. Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṁ bhikkhuṁ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaraṁ appaṭikāraṁ akatasahāyaṁ tamanuvatteyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “eso kho, ayye, bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena ukkhitto, dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaro appaṭikāro akatasahāyo, māyye, etaṁ bhikkhuṁ anuvattī”ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyaṁ ce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, <br>no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā ukkhittānuvattikā.<br><br>8. Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇaṁ vā sādiyeyya, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇaṁ vā sādiyeyya, santiṭṭheyya vā, sallapeyya vā, saṅketaṁ vā gaccheyya, purisassa vā abbhāgamanaṁ sādiyeyya, channaṁ vā anupaviseyya, kāyaṁ vā tadatthāya upasaṁhareyya etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā aṭṭhavatthukā.<br><br>Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, aṭṭha pārājikā dhammā.<br>Yesaṁ bhikkhunī aññataraṁ vā aññataraṁ vā āpajjitvā na labhati bhikkhunīhi saddhiṁ saṁvāsaṁ<br>yathā pure, tathā pacchā, pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā.<br>Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>dutiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>tatiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmīti.<br><br>Pārājikaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.			These eight rules on expulsion come up for recitation.<br><br>1. If a nun willingly has sexual intercourse, even with a male animal, she is expelled and excluded from the community.<br><br>2. If a nun, intending to steal, takes from an inhabited area or from the wilderness what has not been given to her—the sort of stealing for which kings, having caught a thief, would beat, imprison, or banish her, saying, ‘You’re a bandit, you’re a fool, you’ve gone astray, you’re a thief’—she too is expelled and excluded from the community.<br><br>3. If a nun intentionally kills a human being or seeks an instrument of death for them or praises death or incites someone to die, saying, ‘My friend, what’s the point of this miserable and difficult life? Death is better for you than life!’—thinking and intending thus, if she praises death in many ways or incites someone to die—she too is expelled and excluded from the community.<br><br>4. If a nun falsely claims for herself a superhuman quality, a knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, saying, ‘This I know, this I see,’ but after some time—whether she is questioned or not, but having committed the offense and seeking purification—should say: ‘Not knowing I said that I know, not seeing that I see; what I said was empty and false,’ then, except if it is due to overestimation, she too is expelled and excluded from the community.<br><br>5. If a lustful nun consents to a lustful man making physical contact with her, to touching her, to taking hold of her, to contacting her, or to squeezing her, anywhere below the collar bone but above the knees, she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule on above the knees.<br><br>6. If a nun knows that a nun has committed an offense entailing expulsion, but she neither confronts her herself nor tells the<br>community, and afterward—whether that nun remains or has died or has been expelled or has converted—she says, ‘Venerables, although I<br>previously knew that this nun was like this, I thought, “I would neither confront her myself nor tell the community,”’ she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule on those who conceal offenses.<br><br>7. If a nun takes sides with a monk who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha—in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction—and who is disrespectful, who has not made amends, and who has not made friends, the nuns should correct her like this:<br>‘Venerable, this monk has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction. He’s disrespectful, hasn’t made amends, and hasn’t made friends. Venerable, don’t take sides with this monk.’<br>If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop.<br>If she then stops, all is well.<br>If she does not stop, she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule on taking sides with one who has been ejected.<br><br>8. If, for the purpose of indulging in inappropriate sexual conduct, a lustful nun consents to a lustful man holding her hand and the edge of her robe, and she stands with him and chats with him and goes to<br>a rendezvous with him and consents to him coming to her and enters a covered place with him and disposes her body for him for that purpose, she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule having eight parts.<br><br>Venerables, the eight rules on expulsion have been recited.<br>If a nun commits any one of them, she is no longer part of the community of nuns.<br>As before, so after: she’s expelled and excluded from the community.<br>In regard to this I ask you, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A second time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A third time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>You are pure in this and therefore silent. I will remember it thus.<br><br>The recitation of offenses entailing expulsion is the second.	Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ.mp3]	53							[sound:ABi_PJ.mp3]	Herein these eight matters entailing defeat come up for recitation.<br><br>1. {The precept about -sexual intercourse} Should any bhikkhunī willingly engage in the sexual act, even with a male animal, she is defeated and no longer in communion. [See Bhikkhus’ Pārājika 1]<br><br>2. {-taking what is not given} Should any bhikkhunī, in the manner of stealing, take what is not given from an inhabited area or from the wilderness—just as when, in the taking of what is not given, kings arresting the criminal would flog, imprison, or banish her, saying, “You are a robber, you are a fool, you are benighted, you are a thief”—a bhikkhunī in the same way taking what is not given is defeated and no longer in communion. [2]<br><br>3. {-killing a human being} Should any bhikkhunī intentionally deprive a human being of life, or search for an assassin for that person, or praise the advantages of death, or incite that person to die (thus): “My good man (or woman), what use is this wretched, miserable life to you? Death would be better for you than life,” or with such an idea in mind, such a purpose in mind, should in various ways praise the advantages of death or incite that person to die, she also is defeated and no longer in communion. [3]<br><br>4. {-superhuman states} Should any bhikkhunī, without direct knowledge, boast of a superior human state, a truly noble knowledge and vision as present in herself, saying, “Thus do I know; thus do I see,” such that regardless of whether or not she is cross-examined on a later occasion, she—being remorseful and desirous of purification—might say, “Venerables, not knowing, I said I know; not seeing, I said I see—vainly, falsely, idly,” unless it was from overestimation, she also is defeated and no longer in communion. [4]&nbsp;<br><br>5. {-touching above the circle of the knees} Should any bhikkhunī, lusting, consent to a lusting man’s rubbing, rubbing up against, taking hold of, touching, or fondling (her) below the collar-bone and above the circle of the knees, she also is defeated and no longer in communion for being “one above the circle of the knees.” [See Bhikkhus’ Saṅghādisesa 2]<br><br>6. {-concealer of faults} Should any bhikkhunī, knowing that (another) bhikkhunī has fallen into an act (entailing) defeat, neither accuse her herself nor inform the group, and then—whether she (the other bhikkhunī) is still alive or has died, has been expelled or gone over to another sect—if she (this bhikkhunī) should say, “Even before, Venerables, I knew of this bhikkhunī that ‘This sister is of such-and-such a sort,’ and I didn’t accuse her myself nor did I inform the group,” then she also is defeated and no longer in communion for being “one who concealed a fault.” [See Bhikkhus’ Pācittiya 64]<br><br>7. {-the follower of one who is suspended} Should any bhikkhunī follow a bhikkhu suspended by a Saṅgha (of bhikkhus) acting in harmony, in line with the Dhamma, in line with the Vinaya, in line with the teacher’s instructions, and who is disrespectful, has not made amends, has broken off his friendship (with the bhikkhus), the bhikkhunīs should admonish her thus: “Venerable, that bhikkhu has been suspended by a Saṅgha acting in harmony, in line with the Dhamma, in line with the Vinaya, in line with the teacher’s instructions. He is disrespectful, he has not made amends, he has broken off his friendship. Do not follow him, Venerable.” And should that bhikkhunī, admonished thus by the bhikkhunīs, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke her up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times she desists, that is good. If she does not desist, then she also is defeated and no longer in communion for being “a follower of a suspended (bhikkhu).”<br><br>8. {-the doer of eight things} Should any bhikkhunī, lusting, consent to a lusting man’s taking hold of her hand or touching the edge of her outer robe, or should she stand with him or converse with him or go to a rendezvous with him, or should she consent to his approaching her, or should she enter a hidden place with him, or should she dispose her body to him—for the purpose of that unrighteous act—then she also is defeated and no longer in communion for “eight grounds.”<br><br>Recited, Venerables, are the eight matters entailing defeat. If a bhikkhunī has committed one or other of these offences, she may no longer obtain the benefit of living together in communion with bhikkhunīs; as (she was) before (ordination) so (she is) after (the confession of the offence); she becomes defeated, not in communion. Herein I ask the venerables: Are you pure in this? A second time I ask: Are you pure in this? A third time I ask: Are you pure in this? The venerables are pure in this; therefore they are silent. So I remember it.<br><br>The section on defeat is finished.
