bhaṇḍaṁ avaharatū’”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So itarassa āroceti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Avahārako paṭiggaṇhāti, mūlaṭṭhassa āpatti thullaccayassa.<br><br>So taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharati, āpatti sabbesaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti—<br><br>“itthannāmassa pāvada—‘itthannāmo itthannāmassa pāvadatu—itthannāmo itthannāmaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharatū’”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So aññaṁ āṇāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Avahārako paṭiggaṇhāti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharati, mūlaṭṭhassa anāpatti.<br><br>Āṇāpakassa ca avahārakassa ca āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti—<br><br>“itthannāmaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharā”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So gantvā puna paccāgacchati—<br><br>“nāhaṁ sakkomi taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharitun”ti.<br><br>So puna āṇāpeti—<br><br>“yadā sakkosi tadā taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharā”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharati,<br><br>āpatti ubhinnaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti—<br><br>“itthannāmaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharā”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So āṇāpetvā vippaṭisārī na sāveti—<br><br>“mā avaharī”ti.<br><br>So taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharati,<br><br>āpatti ubhinnaṁ pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti—<br><br>“itthannāmaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharā”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So āṇāpetvā vippaṭisārī sāveti—<br><br>“mā avaharī”ti.<br><br>So “āṇatto ahaṁ tayā”ti, taṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharati,<br><br>mūlaṭṭhassa anāpatti.<br><br>Avahārakassa āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Bhikkhu bhikkhuṁ āṇāpeti—<br><br>“itthannāmaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ avaharā”ti,<br><br>āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>So āṇāpetvā vippaṭisārī sāveti—<br><br>“mā avaharī”ti.<br><br>So “sādhū”ti?<br><br>Oramati, ubhinnaṁ anāpatti.<br><br>Pañcahi ākārehi adinnaṁ ādiyantassa āpatti pārājikassa—<br><br>parapariggahitañca hoti,<br><br>parapariggahitasaññī ca,<br><br>garuko ca hoti parikkhāro, pañcamāsako vā atirekapañcamāsako vā,.<br><br>theyyacittañca paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti.<br><br>Āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Phandāpeti, āpatti thullaccayassa.<br><br>Ṭhānā cāveti, āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Pañcahi ākārehi adinnaṁ ādiyantassa āpatti thullaccayassa—<br><br>parapariggahitañca hoti,<br><br>parapariggahitasaññī ca,<br><br>lahuko ca hoti parikkhāro, atirekamāsako vā ūnapañcamāsako vā,<br><br>theyyacittañca paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti.<br><br>Āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Phandāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Ṭhānā cāveti, āpatti thullaccayassa.<br><br>Pañcahi ākārehi adinnaṁ ādiyantassa āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Parapariggahitañca hoti,<br><br>parapariggahitasaññī ca,<br><br>lahuko ca hoti parikkhāro, māsako vā ūnamāsako vā,<br><br>theyyacittañca paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti.<br><br>Āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Phandāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Ṭhānā cāveti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Chahi ākārehi adinnaṁ ādiyantassa āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Na ca sakasaññī,<br><br>na ca vissāsaggāhī,<br><br>na ca tāvakālikaṁ,<br><br>garuko ca hoti parikkhāro, pañcamāsako vā atirekapañcamāsako vā,<br><br>theyyacittañca paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti.<br><br>Āmasati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Phandāpeti, āpatti thullaccayassa.<br><br>Ṭhānā cāveti, āpatti pārājikassa.<br><br>Chahi ākārehi adinnaṁ ādiyantassa āpatti thullaccayassa.<br><br>Na ca sakasaññī,<br><br>na ca …pe…<br><br>“anāpatti, bhikkhu, pārājikassa.<br><br>Āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu rajakattharaṇaṁ gantvā mahagghaṁ dussaṁ passitvā theyyacitto [sound:ABi_PJ_2.mp3]	{-taking what is not given} Should any bhikkhunī, in the manner of stealing, take what is not given from an inhabited area or from the wilderness—just as when, in the taking of what is not given, kings arresting the criminal would flog, imprison, or banish her, saying, “You are a robber, you are a fool, you are benighted, you are a thief”—a bhikkhunī in the same way taking what is not given is defeated and no longer in communion. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::3.Pārājikuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI PJ 7	Ukkhittānuvattikāsikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṁ bhikkhuṁ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaraṁ appaṭikāraṁ akatasahāyaṁ tamanuvatteyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “eso kho, ayye, bhikkhu samaggena saṅghena ukkhitto, dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anādaro appaṭikāro akatasahāyo, māyye, etaṁ bhikkhuṁ anuvattī”ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyaṁ ce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, <br>no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā ukkhittānuvattikā.		Bhikkhu Pācittiya 69		If a nun takes sides with a monk who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha—in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction—and who is disrespectful, who has not made amends, and who has not made friends, the nuns should correct her like this:<br>‘Venerable, this monk has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction. He’s disrespectful, hasn’t made amends, and hasn’t made friends. Venerable, don’t take sides with this monk.’<br>If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop.<br>If she then stops, all is well.<br>If she does not stop, she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule on taking sides with one who has been ejected.	Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ_7.mp3]	45	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nun Thullanandā was taking sides with the monk Ariṭṭha, an ex-vulture-killer, who had been ejected by a unanimous Sangha.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How can Venerable Thullanandā take sides with the monk Ariṭṭha who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā is doing this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How can the nun Thullanandā take sides with the monk Ariṭṭha who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A unanimous Sangha:<br><br>those belonging to the same Buddhist sect and staying within the same monastery zone.<br><br>Who has been ejected:<br><br>who has been ejected for not recognizing an offense, for not making amends, or for not giving up a bad view.<br><br>In accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law:<br><br>in accordance with that Teaching, in accordance with that Monastic Law.<br><br>In accordance with the Teacher’s instruction:<br><br>in accordance with the Victor’s instruction, in accordance with the Buddha’s instruction.<br><br>Who is disrespectful:<br><br>he does not heed the Sangha, groups of monks, individual monks, or legal procedures.<br><br>Who has not made amends:<br><br>he has been ejected and not readmitted.<br><br>Who has not made friends:<br><br>monks belonging to the same Buddhist sect is what is meant by “friends”.<br><br>He is not together with them—therefore it is called “who has not made friends”.<br><br>Takes sides with:<br><br>she has the same view, the same belief, the same persuasion as he does.<br><br>Her:<br><br>that nun who supports one who has been ejected.<br><br>The nuns:<br><br>other nuns who see it or hear about it. They should correct her like this:<br><br>“Venerable, this monk has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction. He’s disrespectful, hasn’t made amends, and hasn’t made friends.<br><br>Venerable, don’t take sides with this monk.”<br><br>And they should correct her a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If she stops, all is well.<br><br>If she does not stop, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If those who hear about it do not say anything, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>That nun, even if she has to be pulled into the midst of the Sangha, should be corrected like this:<br><br>“Venerable, this monk has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction. He’s disrespectful, hasn’t made amends, and hasn’t made friends.<br><br>Venerable, don’t take sides with this monk.”<br><br>They should correct her a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If she stops, all is well.<br><br>If she does not stop, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>Should press her:<br><br>“And, monks, she should be pressed like this.<br><br>A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nun so-and-so is taking sides with a monk who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha—in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction—and who is disrespectful, who has not made amends, and who has not made friends. And she keeps on doing it.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should press her to make her stop.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nun so-and-so is taking sides with a monk who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha—in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction—and who is disrespectful, who has not made amends, and who has not made friends.<br><br>And she keeps on doing it.<br><br>The Sangha presses her to make her stop.<br><br>Any nun who approves of pressing her to make her stop should remain silent.<br><br>Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>For the second time I speak on this matter …<br><br>For the third time I speak on this matter …<br><br>The Sangha has pressed nun so-and-so to stop.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, she commits an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>She too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses entailing expulsion.<br><br>Is expelled:<br><br>just as an ordinary stone that has broken in half cannot be put together again, so is a nun who does not stop when pressed three times not a monastic, not a daughter of the Sakyan. Therefore it is said “she is expelled.”<br><br>Excluded from the community:<br><br>Community: joint legal procedures, a joint recitation, the same training—this is called “community”.<br><br>She does not take part in this—therefore it is called “excluded from the community”.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, but she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she has not been pressed;<br><br>if she stops;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is deranged;<br><br>if she is overwhelmed by pain;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The seventh offense entailing expulsion is finished. [sound:ABi_PJ_7.mp3]	{-the follower of one who is suspended} Should any bhikkhunī follow a bhikkhu suspended by a Saṅgha (of bhikkhus) acting in harmony, in line with the Dhamma, in line with the Vinaya, in line with the teacher’s instructions, and who is disrespectful, has not made amends, has broken off his friendship (with the bhikkhus), the bhikkhunīs should admonish her thus: “Venerable, that bhikkhu has been suspended by a Saṅgha acting in harmony, in line with the Dhamma, in line with the Vinaya, in line with the teacher’s instructions. He is disrespectful, he has not made amends, he has broken off his friendship. Do not follow him, Venerable.” And should that bhikkhunī, admonished thus by the bhikkhunīs, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke her up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times she desists, that is good. If she does not desist, then she also is defeated and no longer in communion for being “a follower of a suspended (bhikkhu).”

Bhikkhus’ Pācittiya 64		If a nun knows that a nun has committed an offense entailing expulsion, but she neither confronts her herself nor tells the<br>community, and afterward—whether that nun remains or has died or has been expelled or has converted—she says, ‘Venerables, although I<br>previously knew that this nun was like this, I thought, “I would neither confront her myself nor tell the community,”’ she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule on those who conceal offenses.	Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ_6.mp3]	40	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Sundarīnandā was pregnant by Migāra’s grandson Sāḷha.<br><br>When the fetus got large, she concealed her condition.<br><br>And when the fetus was fully grown, she disrobed and gave birth.<br><br>The nuns said to the nun Thullanandā,<br><br>“Venerable, Sundarīnandā gave birth shortly after disrobing.”<br><br>“Could it be that she was pregnant while she was still a nun?”<br><br>“Yes, Venerables.”<br><br>“But, Venerable, when you knew that a nun had committed an offense entailing expulsion, why didn’t you either confront her yourself or tell the community?”<br><br>“Her disrepute is my disrepute, her infamy is my infamy, her notoriety is my notoriety, her loss is my loss.<br><br>Why would I tell others of my own disrepute, infamy, notoriety, and loss?”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā, knowing that a nun had committed an offense entailing expulsion, neither confront her herself nor tell the community?”<br><br>Then those nuns told the monks what had happened,<br><br>and the monks in turn told the Buddha.<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā acted like this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā, knowing that a nun had committed an offense entailing expulsion, neither confront her herself nor tell the community?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Knows:<br><br>she knows by herself or others have told her or she has told her.<br><br>Has committed an offense entailing expulsion:<br><br>she has committed any one of the eight offenses entailing expulsion.<br><br>She neither confronts her herself:<br><br>she does not herself accuse her.<br><br>Nor tells the community:<br><br>she does not tell other nuns.<br><br>Whether that nun remains or has died:<br><br>Remains: what is meant is that she remains as a nun.<br><br>Has died: what is meant is that she has passed away.<br><br>Has been expelled:<br><br>she has either disrobed herself or been expelled by others.<br><br>Has converted:<br><br>what is meant is that she has joined another religious community.<br><br>Afterward she says, “Venerables, although I previously knew that this nun was like this, I thought, ‘I will neither confront her myself’”:<br><br>“I won’t accuse her myself.”<br><br>“Nor tell the community”:<br><br>“Nor tell other nuns.”<br><br>She too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses entailing expulsion.<br><br>Is expelled:<br><br>just as a fallen, withered leaf is incapable of becoming green again, so is a nun who knows that a nun has committed an offense entailing expulsion, but who thinks, “I will neither confront her myself nor tell the community,” by the mere fact of abandoning her duty, not a monastic, not a daughter of the Sakyan. Therefore it is said “she is expelled.”<br><br>Excluded from the community:<br><br>Community: joint legal procedures, a joint recitation, the same training—this is called “community”.<br><br>She does not take part in this—therefore it is called “excluded from the community”.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she does not tell because she thinks there will be quarrels or disputes in the Sangha;<br><br>if she does not tell because she thinks there will be a schism or fracture in the Sangha;<br><br>if she does not tell because she thinks the person she is telling about is cruel and harsh and that she might become a threat to life or the monastic life;<br><br>if she does not tell because she does not see any suitable nuns;<br><br>if she does not tell, but not because she wants to conceal;<br><br>if she does not tell because she thinks the other person will be known through her own actions;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is deranged;<br><br>if she is overwhelmed by pain;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The sixth offense entailing expulsion is finished. [sound:ABi_PJ_6.mp3]	{-concealer of faults} Should any bhikkhunī, knowing that (another) bhikkhunī has fallen into an act (entailing) defeat, neither accuse her herself nor inform the group, and then—whether she (the other bhikkhunī) is still alive or has died, has been expelled or gone over to another sect—if she (this bhikkhunī) should say, “Even before, Venerables, I knew of this bhikkhunī that ‘This sister is of such-and-such a sort,’ and I didn’t accuse her myself nor did I inform the group,” then she also is defeated and no longer in communion for being “one who concealed a fault.” [See Bhikkhus’ Pācittiya 64]

Bhikkhus’ Saṅghādisesa 2		If a lustful nun consents to a lustful man making physical contact with her, to touching her, to taking hold of her, to contacting her, or to squeezing her, anywhere below the collar bone but above the knees, she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule on above the knees.	Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ_5.mp3]	36	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>Migāra’s grandson Sāḷha wanted to build a dwelling for the Sangha of nuns.<br><br>He went to the nuns and said,<br><br>“Venerables, I wish to build a dwelling for the Sangha of nuns.<br><br>Please get me the nun in charge of building work.”<br><br>At that time four sisters had gone forth as nuns:<br><br>Nandā, Nandavatī, Sundarīnandā, and Thullanandā.<br><br>Of these, the nun Sundarīnandā had gone forth when she was young, and she was beautiful, intelligent, skilled, and diligent, and she possessed good judgment in regard to doing and arranging things well.<br><br>After appointing Sundarīnandā to be in charge of building work, the Sangha made her work with Sāḷha.<br><br>As a consequence of this, Sundarīnandā would often go to Sāḷha’s house to ask for tools,<br><br>whether an adz, a hatchet, an ax, a spade, or a chisel.<br><br>And Sāḷha would often go to the nuns’ dwelling place to find out about the progress of the building work.<br><br>And because they saw each other frequently, they fell in love.<br><br>But because Sāḷha could not find any opportunity to be intimate with Sundarīnandā, he invited the Sangha of nuns for a meal.<br><br>When preparing the seats in the dining hall, he counted the number of nuns senior to Venerable Sundarīnandā and placed their seats to one side, and he counted the number of nuns junior to her and placed their seats on the other side.<br><br>He then placed Sundarīnandā’s seat in a concealed spot in a corner. In this way the senior nuns would think she was seated close to the junior ones and the junior nuns would think she was seated close to the senior ones.<br><br>Soon afterwards he informed the Sangha that the meal was ready.<br><br>Sundarīnandā thought, “Sāḷha hasn’t prepared a meal for the Sangha as a service, but because he wants to be intimate with me.<br><br>If I go, I will get into trouble.” She then told a nun who was her pupil, “Go and bring back almsfood for me.<br><br>If anyone asks about me, tell them I’m sick.”<br><br>“Yes, Venerable,” she replied.<br><br>Soon afterwards Sāḷha was standing outside his gatehouse repeatedly inquiring after Sundarīnandā:<br><br>“Venerables, where’s Venerable Sundarīnandā?”<br><br>The nun who was Sundarīnandā’s pupil told him: “She’s sick. I’m bringing her almsfood.”<br><br>Sāḷha thought, “I invited the Sangha of nuns because of Sundarīnandā,”<br><br>and after telling the people there to serve the meal to the Sangha of nuns, he left for the nuns’ dwelling place.<br><br>Just then Sundarīnandā was standing outside the monastery gatehouse longing for Sāḷha.<br><br>When she saw him coming, she entered the dwelling, put on her upper robe so that it covered her head, and lay down on her bed.<br><br>Sāḷha approached her and said, “Venerable, what’s wrong with you? Why are you lying down?”<br><br>“That’s what happens when you desire someone who doesn’t desire you in return.”<br><br>“What do you mean I don’t desire you?<br><br>I just couldn’t find an opportunity to be intimate with you.”<br><br>And both having lust, he made physical contact with Sundarīnandā.<br><br>Just then a nun who was weak from old age and had problems with her feet was lying down not far from Sundarīnandā.<br><br>She saw how Sāḷha made physical contact with Sundarīnandā while both of them had lust.<br><br>She complained and criticized her, “How could Venerable Sundarīnandā consent to a man making physical contact with her, when they both had lust?”<br><br>That nun then told the nuns what had happened.<br><br>The nuns of few desires, who had a sense of conscience, and who were contented, afraid of wrongdoing, and fond of the training, complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Sundarīnandā consent to a man making physical contact with her, when they both had lust?”<br><br>Those nuns then told the monks. And the monks of few desires, who had a sense of conscience, and who were contented, afraid of wrongdoing, and fond of the training, criticized her in the same way.<br><br>After rebuking the nun Sundarīnandā in many ways, they told the Buddha.<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Sundarīnandā acted like this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her,<br><br>“It’s not suitable, monks, it’s not proper for the nun Sundarīnandā, it’s not worthy of a monastic, it’s not allowable, it’s not to be done.<br><br>How could Sundarīnandā consent to a man making physical contact with her, when they both had lust?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence,<br><br>and cause some to lose it.”<br><br>And the Buddha spoke in many ways in dispraise of being difficult to support and maintain, in dispraise of great desires, discontent, socializing, and laziness; but he spoke in many ways in praise of being easy to support and maintain, of fewness of wishes, contentment, self-effacement, ascetic practices, serenity, reduction in things, and being energetic. After giving a teaching on what is right and proper, he addressed the monks:<br><br>“Well then, monks, I will lay down a training rule for the following ten reasons:<br><br>for the well-being of the Sangha, for the comfort of the Sangha, for the restraint of bad nuns, for the ease of good nuns, for the restraint of the corruptions relating to the present life, for the restraint of the corruptions relating to future lives, to give rise to confidence in those without it, to increase the confidence of those who have it, for the longevity of the true Teaching, and for supporting the training.<br><br>And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever, of such a kind, of such activity, of such caste, of such name, of such family, of such conduct, of such behavior, of such association, who is senior, who is junior, or who is of middle standing—this is called “a”.<br><br>Nun:<br><br>she is a nun because she lives on alms;<br><br>a nun because she has gone over to living on alms;<br><br>a nun because she wears a patchwork cloth;<br><br>a nun by convention;<br><br>a nun on account of her claim;<br><br>a “come, nun” nun;<br><br>a nun given the full ordination by taking the three refuges;<br><br>a good nun;<br><br>a nun of substance;<br><br>a trainee nun;<br><br>a fully trained nun;<br><br>a nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand.<br><br>The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Lustful:<br><br>having lust, longing for, in love with.<br><br>Lustful:<br><br>having lust, longing for, in love with.<br><br>Man:<br><br>a human male, not a male spirit, not a male ghost, not a male animal. He understands and is capable of making physical contact.<br><br>Below the collar bone:<br><br>down from the collar bone.<br><br>Above the knees:<br><br>up from the knees.<br><br>Making physical contact:<br><br>making mere physical contact.<br><br>Touching:<br><br>touching here and there.<br><br>Taking hold of:<br><br>the mere taking hold of.<br><br>Contacting:<br><br>mere contacting.<br><br>Consents to squeezing:<br><br>consents to the taking hold of a bodily part and then pressing.<br><br>She too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses entailing expulsion.<br><br>Is expelled:<br><br>just as a man with his head cut off is unable to continue living by reconnecting it to the body, so is a lustful nun who consents to a lustful man making physical contact with her, to touching her, to taking hold of her, to contacting her, or to squeezing her, anywhere below the collar bone but above the knees, not a monastic, not a daughter of the Sakyan. Therefore it is said “she is expelled.”<br><br>Excluded from the community:<br><br>Community: joint legal procedures, a joint recitation, the same training—this is called “community”.<br><br>She does There is no offense:<br><br>if it is unintentional;<br><br>if she is not mindful;<br><br>if she does not know;<br><br>if she does not consent;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is deranged;<br><br>if she is overwhelmed by pain;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fifth offense entailing expulsion is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihāraṁ kattukāmo hoti.<br><br>Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca—<br><br>“icchāmahaṁ, ayye, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihāraṁ kātuṁ.<br><br>Detha me navakammikaṁ bhikkhunin”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena catasso bhaginiyo bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā honti—<br><br>nandā, nandavatī, sundarīnandā, thullanandāti.<br><br>Tāsu sundarīnandā bhikkhunī taruṇapabbajitā abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā paṇḍitā byattā medhāvinī dakkhā analasā, tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgatā, alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.<br><br>Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho sundarīnandaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammannitvā sāḷhassa migāranattuno navakammikaṁ adāsi.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sāḷhassa migāranattuno nivesanaṁ abhikkhaṇaṁ gacchati—<br><br>“vāsiṁ detha, parasuṁ detha, kuṭhāriṁ detha, kudālaṁ detha, nikhādanaṁ dethā”ti.<br><br>Sāḷhopi migāranattā bhikkhunupassayaṁ abhikkhaṇaṁ gacchati katākataṁ jānituṁ.<br><br>Te abhiṇhadassanena paṭibaddhacittā ahesuṁ.<br><br>Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā sundarīnandaṁ bhikkhuniṁ dūsetuṁ okāsaṁ alabhamāno etadevaatthāya bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhattaṁ akāsi.<br><br>Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā bhattagge āsanaṁ paññapento “ettakā bhikkhuniyo ayyāya sundarīnandāya vuḍḍhatarā”ti—ekamantaṁ āsanaṁ paññapesi “ettakā navakatarā”ti—ekamantaṁ āsanaṁ paññapesi.<br><br>Paṭicchanne okāse nikūṭe sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā āsanaṁ paññapesi, yathā therā bhikkhuniyo jāneyyuṁ—“navakānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ santike nisinnā”ti; navakāpi bhikkhuniyo jāneyyuṁ—“therānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ santike nisinnā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhunisaṅghassa kālaṁ ārocāpesi—“kālo, ayye, niṭṭhitaṁ bhattan”ti.<br><br>Sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sallakkhetvā—“na bahukato sāḷho migāranattā bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhattaṁ akāsi; maṁ so dūsetukāmo.<br><br>Sacāhaṁ gamissāmi vissaro me bhavissatī”ti, antevāsiniṁ bhikkhuniṁ āṇāpesi—“gaccha me piṇḍapātaṁ nīhara.<br><br>Yo ce maṁ pucchati, ‘gilānā’ti paṭivedehī”ti.<br><br>“Evaṁ, ayye”ti kho sā bhikkhunī sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā paccassosi.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sāḷho migāranattā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito hoti sundarīnandaṁ bhikkhuniṁ paṭipucchanto—<br><br>“kahaṁ, ayye, ayyā sundarīnandā? Kahaṁ, ayye, ayyā sundarīnandā”ti?<br><br>Evaṁ vutte, sundarīnandāya bhikkhuniyā antevāsinī bhikkhunī sāḷhaṁ migāranattāraṁ etadavoca—“gilānāvuso; piṇḍapātaṁ nīharissāmī”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sāḷho migāranattā—“yampāhaṁ atthāya bhikkhunisaṅghassa bhattaṁ akāsiṁ ayyāya sundarīnandāya kāraṇā”ti manusse āṇāpetvā—<br><br>“bhikkhunisaṅghaṁ bhattena parivisathā”ti vatvā yena bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkami.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sundarīnandā bhikkhunī bahārāmakoṭṭhake ṭhitā hoti sāḷhaṁ migāranattāraṁ patimānentī.<br><br>Addasā kho sundarīnandā bhikkhunī sāḷhaṁ migāranattāraṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ. [sound:ABi_PJ_5.mp3]	{-touching above the circle of the knees} Should any bhikkhunī, lusting, consent to a lusting man’s rubbing, rubbing up against, taking hold of, touching, or fondling (her) below the collar-bone and above the circle of the knees, she also is defeated and no longer in communion for being “one above the circle of the knees.” [See Bhikkhus’ Saṅghādisesa 2]	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::3.Pārājikuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI PJ 8	Aṭṭhavatthukāsikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthaggahaṇaṁ vā sādiyeyya, saṅghāṭikaṇṇaggahaṇaṁ vā sādiyeyya, santiṭṭheyya vā, sallapeyya vā, saṅketaṁ vā gaccheyya, purisassa vā abbhāgamanaṁ sādiyeyya, channaṁ vā anupaviseyya, kāyaṁ vā tadatthāya upasaṁhareyya etassa asaddhammassa paṭisevanatthāya, ayampi pārājikā hoti asaṁvāsā aṭṭhavatthukā.		<div>Grasping hand/robe- Bhikkhu Saṅghādisesa 2 (Bodily Contact)</div><div><div>Standing / Conversing/ Concealed Place- Bhikkhu Pācittiya 44 &amp; 45 (Private Sitting), Bhikkhu Aniyata 1 &amp; 2</div></div><div><div>Conversing (Lewdly)- Bhikkhu Saṅghādisesa 3&nbsp;(Lewd Speech)</div></div><div><div>Offering the Body- Bhikkhu Saṅghādisesa 4 (Service to the Body)</div></div>		If, for the purpose of indulging in inappropriate sexual conduct, a lustful nun consents to a lustful man holding her hand and the edge of her robe, and she stands with him and chats with him and goes to<br>a rendezvous with him and consents to him coming to her and enters a covered place with him and disposes her body for him for that purpose, she too is expelled and excluded from the community. The training rule having eight parts.	Pārājikuddeso		[sound:Bi_PJ_8.mp3]	49	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns from the group of six, being lustful and aiming to indulge in inappropriate sexual conduct, consented to lustful men holding their hands and the edge of their robes, and they stood with them, chatted with them, went to rendezvous with them, consented to men coming to them, entered covered places with them, and disposed their bodies for that purpose.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six do such things?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that those nuns do these things?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six, being lustful and aiming to indulge in inappropriate sexual conduct, consent to lustful men holding their hands and the edge of their robes, and how can they stand with them, chat with them, go to rendezvous with them, consent to men coming to them, enter covered places with them, and dispose their bodies for that purpose?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Lustful:<br><br>having lust, longing for, in love with.<br><br>Lustful:<br><br>having lust, longing for, in love with.<br><br>Man:<br><br>a human male, not a male spirit, not a male ghost, not a male animal. Unique to Bhikkhunī		If nuns socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses, then the nuns should correct them like this: ‘Sisters, you socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses. Be secluded, venerables. The Sangha praises seclusion for the Sisters.’ If those nuns continue as before, the nuns should press them up to three times to make them stop. If they then stop, all is well. If they do not stop, then after the third announcement those nuns too have committed an offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_12.mp3]	91	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns who were the pupils of the nun Thullanandā were socializing and behaving badly, had a bad reputation, and were harassing the Sangha of nuns and hiding each other’s offenses.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns behave in this way?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns are behaving like this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns behave in this way?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>Nuns:<br><br>what is meant is that they are fully ordained.<br><br>Socialize:<br><br>they socialize with improper bodily and verbal action.<br><br>Behave badly:<br><br>having bad behavior.<br><br>Have a bad reputation:<br><br>a bad reputation has spread about them.<br><br>Are notorious:<br><br>they make a living by means of a bad and wrong livelihood.<br><br>Harass the Sangha of nuns:<br><br>they object on each other’s behalf when a legal procedure is being carried out against them.<br><br>Hide each other’s offenses:<br><br>they hide one another’s offenses.<br><br>Them:<br><br>those nuns who socialize.<br><br>The nuns:<br><br>other nuns who see it or hear about it. They should correct them like this:<br><br>“Sisters, you socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses.<br><br>Be secluded, Venerables. The Sangha praises seclusion for the Sisters.”<br><br>And they should correct them a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If they stop, all is well.<br><br>If they do not stop, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If those who hear about it do not say anything, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>Those nuns, even if they have to be pulled into the Sangha, should be corrected like this:<br><br>“Sisters, you socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses.<br><br>Be secluded, Venerables. The Sangha praises seclusion for the Sisters.”<br><br>They should correct them a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If they stop, all is well.<br><br>If they do not stop, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>Should press them:<br><br>“And, monks, they should be pressed like this.<br><br>A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nuns so-and-so and so-and-so socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses.<br><br>And they keep on doing it.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should press them to make them stop.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nuns so-and-so and so-and-so socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses.<br><br>And they keep on doing it.<br><br>The Sangha presses them to make them stop.<br><br>Any nun who approves of pressing the nuns so-and-so and so-and-so to make them stop should remain silent.<br><br>Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>For the second time I speak on this matter …<br><br>For the third time I speak on this matter …<br><br>The Sangha has pressed the nuns so-and-so and so-and-so to stop.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>After the motion, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, they commit a serious offense.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, they commit an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If they commit the offense entailing suspension, the offense of wrong conduct and the serious offenses are annulled.<br><br>Two or three may be pressed together, but not more than that.<br><br>Those nuns too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses.<br><br>After the third announcement:<br><br>there is an offense when they have been pressed for the third time, not as soon as the misconduct has been committed.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>they are sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and they perceive it as such, and they do not stop, they commit an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but they are unsure of it, and they do not stop, they commit an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but they perceive it as illegitimate, and they do not stop, they commit an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but they perceive it as legitimate, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but they are unsure of it, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and they perceive it as such, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if they have not been pressed;<br><br>if they stop;<br><br>if they are insane;<br><br>if they are the first offenders.<br><br>The twelfth offense entailing suspension is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā antevāsikā bhikkhuniyo saṁsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo saṁsaṭṭhā viharissanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo saṁsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo saṁsaṭṭhā viharissanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā, bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā, aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Bhikkhuniyo panevāti<br><br>upasampannāyo vuccanti.<br><br>Saṁsaṭṭhā viharantīti<br><br>saṁsaṭṭhā nāma ananulomikena kāyikavācasikena saṁsaṭṭhā viharanti.<br><br>Pāpācārāti<br><br>pāpakena ācārena samannāgatā.<br><br>Pāpasaddāti<br><br>pāpakena kittisaddena abbhuggatā.<br><br>Pāpasilokāti<br><br>pāpakena micchājīvena jīvitaṁ kappenti.<br><br>Bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikāti<br><br>aññamaññissā kamme karīyamāne paṭikkosanti.<br><br>Aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikāti<br><br>aññamaññaṁ vajjaṁ paṭicchādenti.<br><br>Tā bhikkhuniyoti<br><br>yā tā saṁsaṭṭhā bhikkhuniyo.<br><br>Bhikkhunīhīti<br><br>aññāhi bhikkhunīhi. [sound:ABi_SA_12.mp3]	{-1st about evil conduct} In case bhikkhunīs are living entangled, depraved in their conduct, depraved in their reputation, depraved in their notoriety (depraved in their livelihood), exasperating the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, hiding one another’s faults, the bhikkhunīs should admonish them thus: “The sisters are living entangled, depraved in their conduct, depraved in their reputation, depraved in their notoriety, {exasperating the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, hiding one another’s faults.} Split up (your group), Venerables. The Saṅgha recommends isolation for the sisters.” And should those bhikkhunīs, thus admonished, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke them up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times by the bhikkhunīs they desist, that is good. If they do not desist, then these bhikkhunīs, also, as soon as they have fallen into the third act of offence, are to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha.

Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun is angry because she has lost a legal case, saying, ‘The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear,’ then the nuns should correct her like this: ‘Venerable, just because you’re angry that you’ve lost a legal case, don’t say, “The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.” Perhaps it’s you who are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.’ If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop. If she then stops, all is well.<br>If she does not stop, then after the third announcement that nun too has committed an offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_11.mp3]	87	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Caṇḍakāḷī was angry that she had lost a legal case, saying,<br><br>“The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How can Venerable Caṇḍakāḷī say such things just because she’s angry that she has lost a legal case?”<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī says this because she’s angry?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How can the nun Caṇḍakāḷī say such things just because she’s angry that she has lost a legal case?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A legal issue:<br><br>there are four kinds of legal issues: legal issues arising from disputes, legal issues arising from accusations, legal issues arising from offenses, legal issues arising from business.<br><br>Has lost:<br><br>what is meant is that she has been defeated.<br><br>Angry:<br><br>discontent, having hatred, hostile.<br><br>Saying:<br><br>“The nuns are acting out of favoritism … and fear.”<br><br>Her:<br><br>that nun who speaks thus.<br><br>The nuns:<br><br>other nuns who see it or hear about it. They should correct her like this:<br><br>“Venerable, just because you’re angry that you’ve lost a legal case, don’t say,<br><br>‘The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.’<br><br>Perhaps it’s you who are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.”<br><br>And they should correct her a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If she stops, all is well.<br><br>If she does not stop, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If those who hear about it do not say anything, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>That nun, even if she has to be pulled into the Sangha, should be corrected like this:<br><br>“Venerable, just because you’re angry that you’ve lost a legal case, don’t say,<br><br>‘The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.’<br><br>Perhaps it’s you who are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.”<br><br>They should correct her a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If she stops, all is well.<br><br>If she does not stop, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>Should press her:<br><br>“And, monks, she should be pressed like this.<br><br>A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. The nun so-and-so, because she’s angry that she has lost a legal case, says this:<br><br>“The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.”<br><br>And she keeps on saying it.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should press her to make her stop.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nun so-and-so, because she’s angry that she has lost a legal case, says this:<br><br>“The nuns are acting out of favoritism, ill will, confusion, and fear.”<br><br>And she keeps on saying it.<br><br>The Sangha presses her to make her stop.<br><br>Any nun who approves of pressing her to make her stop should remain silent.<br><br>Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>For the second time I speak on this matter …<br><br>For the third time I speak on this matter …<br><br>The Sangha has pressed nun so-and-so to stop.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>For one who commits the offense entailing suspension, the offense of wrong conduct<br><br>and the serious offenses are annulled.<br><br>That too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses.<br><br>After the third announcement:<br><br>there is an offense when she has been pressed for the third time, not as soon as the misconduct has been committed.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>she is sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she has not been pressed;<br><br>if she stops;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The eleventh offense entailing suspension is finished. [sound:ABi_SA_11.mp3]	{-anger about a legal issue} Should any bhikkhunī, turned down in even a trifling issue, angry and displeased, say, “The bhikkhunīs are prejudiced by favoritism, prejudiced by aversion, prejudiced by delusion, prejudiced by fear,” the bhikkhunīs should admonish her thus: “Venerable, don’t—turned down in even a trifling issue, angry and displeased—say, ‘The bhikkhunīs are prejudiced by favoritism, prejudiced by aversion, prejudiced by delusion, prejudiced by fear.’ It may be that you, Venerable, are prejudiced by favoritism, prejudiced by aversion, prejudiced by delusion, prejudiced by fear.” And should that bhikkhunī, admonished thus by the bhikkhunīs, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke her up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times she desists, that is good. If she does not desist, then this bhikkhunī, also, as soon as she has fallen into the third act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 13	Pāpasamācāradutiyasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī evaṁ vadeyya: “saṁsaṭṭhāva, ayye, tumhe viharatha, mā tumhe nānā viharittha, santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṁsaddā evaṁsilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā, tā saṅgho na kiñci āha tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha: ‘bhaginiyo kho saṁsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā, viviccathāyye, vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṁ saṅgho vaṇṇetī”’ti, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “māyye, evaṁ avaca, saṁsaṭṭhāva ayye tumhe viharatha, mā tumhe nānā viharittha, santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṁsaddā evaṁsilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā, tā saṅgho na kiñci āha, tumhaññeva saṅgho uññāya paribhavena akkhantiyā vebhassiyā dubbalyā evamāha: ‘bhaginiyo kho saṁsaṭṭhā viharanti pāpācārā pāpasaddā pāpasilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā, viviccathāyye, vivekaññeva bhaginīnaṁ saṅgho vaṇṇetī”’ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi bhikkhunī yāvatatiyakaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun says, ‘Venerables, you should socialize. Don’t live separately.<br>There are other nuns in the Sangha who have such behavior, reputation, and notoriety, and who harass the Sangha of nuns and hide each other’s offenses. The Sangha says nothing to them. It’s because of disrespect, contempt, impatience, and slander, and because you are weak that the Sangha says to you, “Sisters, you socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses. Be secluded, venerables. The Sangha praises seclusion for the Sisters,”’<br>then the nuns should correct her like this:<br>‘Venerable, don’t say such things:<br>“Venerables, you should socialize. Don’t live separately.<br>There are other nuns in the Sangha who have such behavior, reputation, and notoriety, and who harass the Sangha of nuns and hide each other’s offenses. The Sangha says nothing to them.<br>It’s because of disrespect, contempt, impatience, and slander, and because you are weak that the Sangha says to you, ‘Sisters, you socialize, behave badly, have a bad reputation, are notorious, harass the Sangha of nuns, and hide each other’s offenses. Be secluded, venerables. The Sangha praises seclusion for the Sisters,’”’<br>If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop. If she then stops, all is well. If she does not stop, then after the third announcement that nun too has committed an offense entailing sending away and suspension.
