[sound:ABi_SA_15.mp3]	{-siding with a schism} Should bhikkhunīs—one, two, or three—who are followers and partisans of that bhikkhunī, say, “Do not, Venerables, admonish that bhikkhunī in any way. She is an exponent of the Dhamma, an exponent of the Vinaya. She acts with our consent and approval. She knows, she speaks for us, and that is pleasing to us,” other bhikkhunīs are to admonish them thus: “Do not say that, Venerables. That bhikkhunī is not an exponent of the Dhamma and she is not an exponent of the Vinaya. Do not, Venerables, approve of a schism in the Saṅgha. Let the venerables’ (minds) be reconciled with the Saṅgha, for a Saṅgha in concord, on complimentary terms, without dispute, with a common recitation, dwells in peace.” And should those bhikkhunīs, thus admonished, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke them up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times by the bhikkhunīs they desist, that is good. If they do not desist, then these bhikkhunīs, also, as soon as they have fallen into the third act of offence, are to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha. Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_8.mp3]	74	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove,<br><br>Venerable Dabba the Mallian realized perfection at the age of seven.<br><br>He had achieved all there is to achieve by a disciple<br><br>and had nothing further to do.<br><br>Then, while reflecting in private,<br><br>he thought, “How can I be of service to the Sangha?<br><br>Why don’t I assign the dwellings and designate the meals?”<br><br>In the evening Dabba came out of seclusion and went to the Buddha. He bowed, sat down,<br><br>and said,<br><br>“Sir, while I was reflecting in private, it occurred to me that I’ve achieved all there is to achieve by a disciple, and I was wondering how I could be of service to the Sangha.<br><br>I thought,<br><br>‘Why don’t I assign the dwellings and designate the meals?’”<br><br>“Good, good, Dabba,<br><br>please do so.”<br><br>“Yes.”<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, the Sangha should appoint Dabba the Mallian as the assigner of dwellings and the designator of meals.<br><br>And he should be appointed like this.<br><br>First Dabba should be asked.<br><br>A competent and capable monk should then inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should appoint Venerable Dabba the Mallian as assigner of dwellings and designator of meals.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The Sangha appoints Venerable Dabba the Mallian as assigner of dwellings and designator of meals.<br><br>Any monk who approves of appointing Venerable Dabba as assigner of dwellings and designator of meals should remain silent.<br><br>Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>The Sangha has appointed Venerable Dabba the Mallian as assigner of dwellings and designator of meals.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent.<br><br>I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>Dabba assigned dwellings to the monks according to their character.<br><br>He assigned dwellings in the same place to those monks who were experts on the discourses, thinking,<br><br>“They’ll recite the discourses to one another.”<br><br>And he did likewise for the experts on the Monastic Law, thinking,<br><br>“They’ll discuss the Monastic Law;”<br><br>for the expounders of the Teaching, thinking,<br><br>“They’ll discuss the Teaching;”<br><br>for the meditators, thinking,<br><br>“They won’t disturb each other;”<br><br>and for the gossips and the body-builders, thinking,<br><br>“In this way even these venerables will be happy.”<br><br>When monks arrived at night, he entered the fire element and assigned dwellings with the help of that light.<br><br>Monks even arrived late on purpose,<br><br>hoping to see the marvel of Dabba’s supernormal powers.<br><br>They would approach Dabba and say,<br><br>“Venerable Dabba, please assign us a dwelling.”<br><br>“Where would you like to stay?”<br><br>They would intentionally suggest somewhere far away:<br><br>“On the Vulture Peak,”<br><br>“At Robbers’ Cliff,”<br><br>“On Black Rock on the slope of Mount Isigili,”<br><br>“In the Sattapaṇṇi Cave on the slope of Mount Vebhāra,”<br><br>“In Cool Grove on the hill at the Snake’s Pool,”<br><br>“At Gotamaka Gorge,”<br><br>“At Tinduka Gorge,”<br><br>“At Tapoda Gorge,”<br><br>“In Tapoda Park,”<br><br>“In Jīvaka’s Mango Grove,”<br><br>“In the deer park at Maddakucchi.”<br><br>Dabba then entered the fire element, and with his finger glowing, he walked in front of those monks.<br><br>They followed behind him with the help of that light.<br><br>And he would assign them dwellings:<br><br>“This is the bed, this the bench, this the mattress, this the pillow, this the place for defecating, this the place for urinating, this the water for drinking, this the water for washing, this the walking stick;<br><br>these are the Sangha’s agreements concerning the right time to enter and the right time to leave.”<br><br>Dabba then returned to the Bamboo Grove.<br><br>At that time the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka were only newly ordained. They had little merit,<br><br>getting inferior dwellings and meals.<br><br>The people of Rājagaha were keen to give specially prepared almsfood to the senior monks—ghee, oil, and special curries—<br><br>but to the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka they gave ordinary food of porridge and broken rice.<br><br>When they had eaten their meal and returned from almsround, they asked the senior monks,<br><br>“What did you get at the dining hall?”<br><br>Some said,<br><br>“We got ghee, oil, and special curries.”<br><br>But the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka said,<br><br>“We didn’t get anything except ordinary food of porridge and broken rice.”<br><br>At that time there was a householder who gave a regular meal of fine food to four monks.<br><br>He made his offering in the dining hall together with his wives and children.<br><br>Some of them offered rice, some bean curry, some oil, and some special curries.<br><br>On one occasion the meal to be given by this householder on the following day had been designated to the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka.<br><br>Just then that householder went to the monastery on some business.<br><br>He approached Dabba, bowed, and sat down.<br><br>And Dabba instructed, inspired, and gladdened him with a teaching.<br><br>After the talk, he asked Dabba,<br><br>“Sir, who has been designated to receive tomorrow’s meal in our house?”<br><br>“Mettiya and Bhūmajaka.”<br><br>He was disappointed, and thought,<br><br>“Why should bad monks eat in our house?”<br><br>After returning to his house, he told a female slave,<br><br>“For those who are coming for tomorrow’s meal, prepare seats in the gatehouse and serve them broken rice and porridge.”<br><br>“Yes, sir.”<br><br>The monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka said to each other,<br><br>“Yesterday we were designated a meal from that householder who offers fine food.<br><br>Tomorrow he’ll serve us together with his wives and children.<br><br>Some of them will offer us rice, some bean curry, some oil, and some special curries.”<br><br>And because they were excited, they did not sleep properly that night.<br><br>The following morning they robed up, took their bowls and robes, and went to the house of that householder.<br><br>When the female slave saw them coming, she prepared seats in the gatehouse and said to them,<br><br>“Please sit, venerables.”<br><br>They thought,<br><br>“The meal can’t be ready, since we’re given seats in the gatehouse.”<br><br>She then brought them broken rice and porridge, and said,<br><br>“Eat, sirs.”<br><br>“But, Sister, we’ve come for the regular meal.”<br><br>“I know.<br><br>But yesterday I was told by the head of the household to serve you like this.<br><br>Please eat.”<br><br>They said to each other,<br><br>“Yesterday this householder came to the monastery and spoke with Dabba.<br><br>Dabba must be responsible for this split between the householder and us.”<br><br>And because they were dejected, they did not eat as much as they had intended.<br><br>When they had eaten their meal and returned from almsround, they put their bowls and robes away and squatted on their heels outside the monastery gatehouse, using their upper robes as back-and-knee straps. They were silent and humiliated, their shoulders drooping and their heads down, glum and speechless.<br><br>Just then the nun Mettiyā came to them and said,<br><br>“My respectful greetings to you, venerables.”<br><br>But they did not respond.<br><br>A second time<br><br>and a third time she said<br><br>the same thing,<br><br>but they still did not respond.<br><br>“Have I done something wrong?<br><br>Why don’t you respond?”<br><br>“It’s because we’ve been badly treated by Dabba the Mallian, and you’re not taking an interest.”<br><br>“But what can I do?”<br><br>“If you like, you could make the Buddha expel Dabba.”<br><br>“And how can I do that?”<br><br>“Go to the Buddha and say,<br><br>‘Sir, this isn’t proper or appropriate.<br><br>There’s fear, distress, and oppression in this district, where none of these should exist.<br><br>From where one would expect security, there’s insecurity.<br><br>It’s as if water is burning.<br><br>Venerable Dabba the Mallian has raped me.’”<br><br>Saying, “Alright, venerables,” she went to the Buddha, bowed,<br><br>and then repeated what she had been told to say.<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha had the Sangha gathered and questioned Dabba:<br><br>“Dabba, do you remember doing as the nun Mettiyā says?”<br><br>“Sir, you know what I’m like.”<br><br>A second and<br><br>a third time the Buddha asked<br><br>the same question<br><br>and got the same response.<br><br>He then said, “Dabba, the Dabbas don’t give such evasive answers.<br><br>If it was done by you, say so;<br><br>if it wasn’t, then say that.”<br><br>“Since I was born, sir, I don’t recall having sexual intercourse even in a dream, let alone when awake.”<br><br>The Buddha addressed the monks:<br><br>“Well then, monks, expel the nun Mettiyā,<br><br>and call these monks to account.”<br><br>The Buddha then got up from his seat and entered his dwelling.<br><br>When the monks had expelled the nun Mettiyā,<br><br>the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka said to them,<br><br>“Don’t expel the nun Mettiyā;<br><br>she’s done nothing wrong.<br><br>She was urged on by us. We were angry and displeased, and trying to get Dabba to leave the monastic life.”<br><br>“But did you groundlessly charge Venerable Dabba with an offense entailing expulsion?”<br><br>“Yes.”<br><br>The monks of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How could the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka groundlessly charge Venerable Dabba with an offense entailing expulsion?”<br><br>They rebuked those monks in many ways and then told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned those monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that you did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“Foolish men, how could you do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Monk:<br><br>… The monk who has been given the full ordination by a unanimous Sangha through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of monk is meant in this case.<br><br>A monk:<br><br>another monk.<br><br>Angry:<br><br>upset, dissatisfied, discontent, having hatred, hostile.<br><br>Displeased:<br><br>because of that upset, that ill will, that dissatisfaction, and that discontent, he is displeased.<br><br>Groundlessly:<br><br>not seen, not heard, not suspected.<br><br>With an offense entailing expulsion:<br><br>with one of the four.<br><br>Charges:<br><br>accuses him or has him accused.<br><br>To make him leave the monastic life:<br><br>to make him leave the monkhood, leave the state of a monastic, leave his morality, leave the virtue of monasticism.<br><br>And then after some time:<br><br>the moment, the instant, the second after he has laid the charge.<br><br>He is questioned:<br><br>he is questioned about the grounds of his charge.<br><br>Not:<br><br>he is not spoken to by anyone.<br><br>The legal issue:<br><br>there are four kinds of legal issues: legal issues arising from disputes, legal issues arising from accusations, legal issues arising from offenses, legal issues arising from business.<br><br>And he admits to his ill will:<br><br>“What I said was empty,” “What I said was false,” “What I said was unreal,” “I said it without knowing.”<br><br>He commits an offense entailing suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called “an offense entailing suspension”.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br><b>Permutations part 1</b><br><br><b>Doing the accusing oneself</b><br><br>Although he has not seen it, he accuses someone of having committed an offense 2</b><br><br><b>Summary</b><br><br>Someone is impure, but viewed as pure;<br><br>someone is pure, but viewed as impure;<br><br>someone is impure and viewed as impure;<br><br>someone is pure and viewed as pure.<br><br><b>Exposition</b><br><br><b>Impure but viewed as pure</b><br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, one commits one offense entailing suspension and one offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, one commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits one offense for abusive speech and one offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits an offense for abusive speech.<br><br><b>Pure but viewed as impure</b><br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, one commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, there is no offense.<br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits one offense for abusive speech and one offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits an offense for abusive speech.<br><br><b>Impure and viewed as impure</b><br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, one commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, there is no offense.<br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits one offense for abusive speech and one offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>An impure person has committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as impure, and then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits an offense for abusive speech.<br><br><b>Pure and viewed as pure</b><br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, one commits one offense entailing suspension and one offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of making him leave the monastic life, one commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion.<br><br>If one views him as pure, but then, without having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits one offense for abusive speech and one offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>A pure person has not committed an offense entailing expulsion. If one views him as pure, but then, having gotten his permission, speaks with the aim of abusing him, one commits an offense for abusive speech.	There is no offense:<br><br>if he views a pure person as impure;<br><br>if he views an impure person as impure;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The training rule on groundless, the eighth, is finished. sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.<br><br>Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā dabbo mallaputto bhagavantaṁ anupattaṁ, natthi ca me kiñci uttari karaṇīyaṁ, katassa vā paticayo, kiṁ nu kho ahaṁ saṅghassa veyyāvaccaṁ kareyyanti.<br><br>Tassa mayhaṁ, bhante, etadahosi—<br><br>‘yannūnāhaṁ saṅghassa senāsanañca senāsanapaññāpakañca bhattuddesakañca sammannatu.<br><br>Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo.<br><br>Paṭhamaṁ dabbo mallaputto yācitabbo.<br><br>Yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo—<br><br>‘Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho.<br><br>Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ saṅgho āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ senāsanapaññāpakañca bhattuddesakañca sammanneyya.<br><br>Esā ñatti.<br><br>Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho.<br><br>Saṅgho āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ senāsanapaññāpakañca bhattuddesakañca sammannati.<br><br>Yassāyasmato khamati āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa senāsanapaññāpakassa ca bhattuddesakassa ca sammuti, so tuṇhassa;<br><br>yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.<br><br>Sammato saṅghena āyasmā dabbo mallaputto senāsanapaññāpako ca bhattuddesako ca.<br><br>Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī,<br><br>evametaṁ dhārayāmī’”ti.<br><br>Sammato ca panāyasmā dabbo mallaputto sabhāgānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ ekajjhaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū suttantikā tesaṁ ekajjhaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti—<br><br>“te aññamaññaṁ suttantaṁ saṅgāyissantī”ti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū vinayadharā tesaṁ ekajjhaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti—<br><br>“te aññamaññaṁ vinayaṁ vinicchinissantī”ti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū dhammakathikā tesaṁ ekajjhaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti—<br><br>“te aññamaññaṁ dhammaṁ sākacchissantī”ti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū jhāyino tesaṁ ekajjhaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti—<br><br>“te aññamaññaṁ na byābādhissantī”ti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū tiracchānakathikā kāyadaḷhibahulā viharanti tesampi ekajjhaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti—<br><br>“imāyapime āyasmanto ratiyā acchissantī”ti.<br><br>Yepi te bhikkhū vikāle āgacchanti tesampi tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā teneva ālokena senāsanaṁ paññapeti.<br><br>Apisu bhikkhū sañcicca vikāle āgacchanti—<br><br>“mayaṁ āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa iddhipāṭihāriyaṁ passissāmā”ti.<br><br>Te āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadanti—<br><br>“amhākaṁ, āvuso dabba, senāsanaṁ paññapehī”ti.<br><br>“katthāyasmantā icchanti, kattha paññapemī”ti?<br><br>Te sañcicca dūre apadisanti—<br><br>“amhākaṁ, āvuso dabba, gijjhakūṭe pabbate senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, corapapāte senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhāyaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāre senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, gotamakakandarāyaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, tindukakandarāyaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, tapodakandarāyaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, tapodārāme senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, jīvakambavane senāsanaṁ paññapehi.<br><br>Amhākaṁ, āvuso, maddakucchismiṁ migadāye senāsanaṁ paññapehī”ti.<br><br>Tesaṁ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā aṅguliyā jalamānāya purato purato gacchati.<br><br>Tepi teneva ālokena āyasmato dabbassa mallaputtassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gacchanti.<br><br>Tesaṁ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto evaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapeti—<br><br>“ayaṁ mañco, idaṁ pīṭhaṁ, ayaṁ bhisi, idaṁ bibbohanaṁ, idaṁ vaccaṭṭhānaṁ, idaṁ passāvaṭṭhānaṁ, idaṁ pānīyaṁ, idaṁ paribhojanīyaṁ, ayaṁ kattaradaṇḍo,<br><br>idaṁ saṅghassa katikasaṇṭhānaṁ, imaṁ kālaṁ pavisitabbaṁ, imaṁ kālaṁ nikkhamitabban”ti.<br><br>Tesaṁ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto evaṁ senāsanaṁ paññapetvā punadeva veḷuvanaṁ paccāgacchati.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū navakā ceva honti appapuññā ca.<br><br>Yāni saṅghassa lāmakāni senāsanāni tāni tesaṁ pāpuṇanti lāmakāni ca bhattāni.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe manussā icchanti therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ abhisaṅkhārikaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ dātuṁ sappimpi telampi uttaribhaṅgampi.<br><br>Mettiyabhūmajakānaṁ pana bhikkhūnaṁ pākatikaṁ denti yathārandhaṁ kaṇājakaṁ bilaṅgadutiyaṁ.<br><br>Te pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā there bhikkhū pucchanti—<br><br>“tumhākaṁ, āvuso, bhattagge kiṁ ahosi? Tumhākaṁ, āvuso, bhattagge kiṁ ahosī”ti?<br><br>Ekacce therā evaṁ vadanti—<br><br>“amhākaṁ, āvuso, sappi ahosi telaṁ ahosi uttaribhaṅgaṁ ahosī”ti.<br><br>Mettiyabhūmajakā pana bhikkhū evaṁ vadanti—<br><br>“amhākaṁ, āvuso, na kiñci ahosi, pākatikaṁ yathārandhaṁ kaṇājakaṁ bilaṅgadutiyan”ti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati saṅghassa catukkabhattaṁ deti niccabhattaṁ.<br><br>So bhattagge saputtadāro upatiṭṭhitvā parivisati.<br><br>Aññe odanena pucchanti, aññe sūpena pucchanti, aññe telena pucchanti, aññe uttaribhaṅgena pucchanti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino bhattaṁ svātanāya mettiyabhūmajakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ uddiṭṭhaṁ hoti.<br><br>Atha kho kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati ārāmaṁ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena.<br><br>So yenāyasmā dabbo mallaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.<br><br>Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho kalyāṇabhattikaṁ gahapatiṁ āyasmā dabbo mallaputto dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.<br><br>Atha kho kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati āyasmatā dabbena mallaputtena dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṁsito āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“kassa, bhante, amhākaṁ ghare svātanāya bhattaṁ uddiṭṭhan”ti?<br><br>“Mettiyabhūmajakānaṁ kho, gahapati, bhikkhūnaṁ tumhākaṁ ghare svātanāya bhattaṁ uddiṭṭhan”ti.<br><br>Atha kho kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati anattamano ahosi—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma pāpabhikkhū amhākaṁ ghare bhuñjissantī”ti.<br><br>Gharaṁ gantvā dāsiṁ āṇāpesi—<br><br>“ye, je, sve bhattikā āgacchanti te koṭṭhake āsanaṁ paññapetvā kaṇājakena bilaṅgadutiyena parivisā”ti.<br><br>“Evaṁ, ayyā”ti kho sā dāsī kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino paccassosi.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū—<br><br>“hiyyo kho, āvuso, amhākaṁ kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino bhattaṁ uddiṭṭhaṁ,<br><br>sve amhe kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati saputtadāro upatiṭṭhitvā parivisissati;<br><br>aññe odanena pucchissanti, aññe sūpena pucchissanti, aññe telena pucchissanti, aññe uttaribhaṅgena pucchissantī”ti.<br><br>Te teneva somanassena na cittarūpaṁ rattiyā supiṁsu.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaraṁ ādāya yena kalyāṇabhattikassa gahapatino nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu.<br><br>Addasā kho sā dāsī mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna koṭṭhake āsanaṁ paññapetvā mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca—<br><br>“nisīdatha, bhante”ti.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi—<br><br>“nissaṁsayaṁ kho na tāva bhattaṁ siddhaṁ bhavissati. Yathā mayaṁ koṭṭhake nisīdeyyāmā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā dāsī kaṇājakena bilaṅgadutiyena upagacchi—<br><br>“bhuñjatha, bhante”ti.<br><br>“Mayaṁ kho, bhagini, niccabhattikā”ti.<br><br>“Jānāmi, ayyā, niccabhattikāti.<br><br>Api cāhaṁ hiyyova gahapatinā āṇattā— ‘ye, je, sve bhattikā āgacchanti te koṭṭhake āsanaṁ paññapetvā kaṇājakena bilaṅgadutiyena parivisā’ti.<br><br>Bhuñjatha, bhante”ti.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū—<br><br>“hiyyo kho, āvuso, kalyāṇabhattiko gahapati ārāmaṁ agamāsi dabbassa mallaputtassa santike.<br><br>Nissaṁsayaṁ kho mayaṁ dabbena mallaputtena gahapatino antare paribhinnā”ti.<br><br>Te teneva domanassena na cittarūpaṁ bhuñjiṁsu.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā ārāmaṁ gantvā pattacīvaraṁ paṭisāmetvā bahārāmakoṭṭhake saṅghāṭipallatthikāya nisīdiṁsu tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyā bhikkhunī yena mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca—<br><br>“vandāmi, ayyā”ti.<br><br>Evaṁ vutte, mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū nālapiṁsu.<br><br>Dutiyampi kho …pe…<br><br>tatiyampi kho mettiyā bhikkhunī mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū etadavoca—<br><br>“vandāmi, ayyā”ti.<br><br>Tatiyampi kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū nālapiṁsu.<br><br>“Kyāhaṁ ayyānaṁ aparajjhāmi?<br><br>Kissa maṁ ayyā nālapantī”ti?<br><br>“Tathā hi pana tvaṁ, bhagini, amhe dabbena mallaputtena viheṭhīyamāne ajjhupekkhasī”ti?<br><br>“Kyāhaṁ, ayyā, karomī”ti?<br><br>“Sace kho tvaṁ, bhagini, iccheyyāsi ajjeva bhagavā dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ nāsāpeyyā”ti.<br><br>“Kyāhaṁ, ayyā, karomi, kiṁ mayā sakkā kātun”ti?<br><br>“Ehi tvaṁ, bhagini, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ evaṁ vadehi—<br><br>‘idaṁ, bhante, nacchannaṁ nappatirūpaṁ.<br><br>Yāyaṁ, bhante, disā abhayā anītikā anupaddavā sāyaṁ disā sabhayā saītikā saupaddavā.<br><br>Yato nivātaṁ tato savātaṁ.<br><br>Udakaṁ maññe ādittaṁ.<br><br>Ayyenamhi dabbena mallaputtena dūsitā’”ti.<br><br>“Evaṁ, ayyā”ti kho mettiyā bhikkhunī mettiyabhūmajakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.<br><br>Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā mettiyā bhikkhunī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṁ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ paṭipucchi—<br><br>“sarasi tvaṁ, dabba, evarūpaṁ kattā yathāyaṁ bhikkhunī āhā”ti?<br><br>“Yathā maṁ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti.<br><br>Dutiyampi kho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“sarasi tvaṁ, dabba, evarūpaṁ kattā yathāyaṁ bhikkhunī āhā”ti?<br><br>“Yathā maṁ, bhante, bhagavā jānātī”ti.<br><br>“Na kho, dabba, dabbā evaṁ nibbeṭhenti.<br><br>Sace tayā kataṁ katanti vadehi,<br><br>sace tayā akataṁ akatanti vadehī”ti.<br><br>“Yato ahaṁ, bhante, jāto nābhijānāmi supinantenapi methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevitā, pageva jāgaro”ti.<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi—<br><br>“tena hi, bhikkhave, mettiyaṁ bhikkhuniṁ nāsetha.<br><br>Ime ca bhikkhū anuyuñjathā”ti.<br><br>Idaṁ vatvā bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū mettiyaṁ bhikkhuniṁ nāsesuṁ.<br><br>Atha kho mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū te bhikkhū etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“māvuso, mettiyaṁ bhikkhuniṁ nāsetha.<br><br>Na sā kiñci aparajjhati.<br><br>Amhehi sā ussāhitā kupitehi anattamanehi cāvanādhippāyehī”ti.<br><br>“Kiṁ pana tumhe, āvuso, āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṁsethā”ti?<br><br>“Evamāvuso”ti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma mettiyabhūmajakā bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṁsessantī”ti.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū mettiyabhūmajake bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṁsethā”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>“kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, dabbaṁ mallaputtaṁ amūlakena pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṁsessatha.<br><br>Netaṁ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—	Yo panāti<br><br>yo yādiso …pe…<br><br>bhikkhūti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.<br><br>Bhikkhunti<br><br>aññaṁ bhikkhuṁ.<br><br>Duṭṭho dosoti<br><br>kupito anattamano anabhiraddho āhatacitto khilajāto.<br><br>Appatītoti<br><br>tena ca kopena tena ca dosena tāya ca anattamanatāya tāya ca anabhiraddhiyā appatīto hoti.<br><br>Amūlakaṁ nāma<br><br>adiṭṭhaṁ asutaṁ aparisaṅkitaṁ.<br><br>Pārājikena dhammenāti<br><br>catunnaṁ aññatarena.<br><br>Anuddhaṁseyyāti<br><br>codeti vā codāpeti vā.<br><br>Appeva nāma naṁ imamhā brahmacariyā cāveyyanti<br><br>bhikkhubhāvā cāveyyaṁ, samaṇadhammā cāveyyaṁ, sīlakkhandhā cāveyyaṁ, tapoguṇā cāveyyaṁ.<br><br>Tato aparena samayenāti<br><br>yasmiṁ khaṇe anuddhaṁsito hoti taṁ khaṇaṁ taṁ layaṁ taṁ muhuttaṁ vītivatte.<br><br>Samanuggāhīyamānoti<br><br>yena vatthunā anuddhaṁsito hoti tasmiṁ vatthusmiṁ samanuggāhīyamāno.<br><br>Asamanuggāhīyamānoti<br><br>na kenaci vuccamāno.<br><br>Adhikaraṇaṁ nāma<br><br>cattāri adhikaraṇāni— vivādādhikaraṇaṁ, anuvādādhikaraṇaṁ, āpattādhikaraṇaṁ, kiccādhikaraṇaṁ.<br><br>Bhikkhu ca dosaṁ patiṭṭhātīti<br><br>tucchakaṁ mayā bhaṇitaṁ, musā mayā bhaṇitaṁ, abhūtaṁ mayā bhaṇitaṁ, ajānantena mayā bhaṇitaṁ.<br><br>Saṅghādisesoti<br><br>…pe… tenapi vuccati saṅghādisesoti.<br><br>Adiṭṭhassa hoti pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpajjanto.<br><br>Tañce codeti—“diṭṭho mayā, pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannosi,<br><br>assamaṇosi, asakyaputtiyosi,<br><br>natthi tayā saddhiṁ uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā saṅghakammaṁ vā”ti,<br><br>āpatti vācāya, vācāya saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Asutassa hoti—<br><br>“pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpanno”ti.<br><br>Tañce codeti—“suto mayā, pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannosi,<br><br>assamaṇosi, asakyaputtiyosi,<br><br>natthi tayā saddhiṁ uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā saṅghakammaṁ vā”ti,<br><br>āpatti vācāya, vācāya saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Aparisaṅkitassa hoti—<br><br>“pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpanno”ti.<br><br>Tañce codeti—“parisaṅkito mayā, pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannosi,<br><br>assamaṇosi, asakyaputtiyosi,<br><br>natthi tayā saddhiṁ uposatho vā pavāraṇā vā saṅghakammaṁ vā”ti,<br><br>āpatti vācāya, vācāya saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Adiṭṭhassa hoti pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpajjanto.<br><br>Tañce codeti—“diṭṭho mayā parisaṅkito ca, pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannosi,<br><br>assamaṇosi …pe…<br><br>āpatti vācāya, vācāya saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Adiṭṭhassa hoti pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpajjanto.<br><br>Tañce codeti—“diṭṭho mayā suto ca parisaṅkito ca, pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannosi,<br><br>assamaṇosi …pe…<br><br>āpatti vācāya, vācāya saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Asutassa hoti—<br><br>“pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpanno”ti.<br><br>Tañce codeti—“suto mayā parisaṅkito ca …pe…<br><br>suto mayā diṭṭho ca …pe…<br><br>suto mayā parisaṅkito ca diṭṭho ca, pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ ajjhāpannosi,<br><br>assamaṇosi …pe…<br><br>āpatti vācāya, vācāya saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Aparisaṅkitassa hoti—<br><br>“pārājikaṁ [sound:ABi_SA_8.mp3]	{-being corrupted by malice} Should any bhikkhunī, malicious, angered, displeased, charge a (fellow) bhikkhunī with an unfounded case involving defeat, (thinking), “Surely with this I may bring about her fall from the monastic life,” then regardless of whether or not she is cross-examined on a later occasion, if the issue is unfounded and the bhikkhunī confesses her anger: this bhikkhunī, also, as soon as she has fallen into the first act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 10	Sikkhaṁpaccācikkhaṇasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī kupitā anattamanā evaṁ vadeyya: “buddhaṁ paccācikkhāmi dhammaṁ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṁ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṁ paccācikkhāmi, kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro, santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṁ santike brahmacariyaṁ carissāmī”ti. Sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “māyye kupitā anattamanā evaṁ avaca ‘buddhaṁ paccācikkhāmi, dhammaṁ paccācikkhāmi, saṅghaṁ paccācikkhāmi, sikkhaṁ paccācikkhāmi, kinnumāva samaṇiyo yā samaṇiyo sakyadhītaro, santaññāpi samaṇiyo lajjiniyo kukkuccikā sikkhākāmā, tāsāhaṁ santike brahmacariyaṁ carissāmī’ti, abhiramāyye, svākkhāto dhammo, cara brahmacariyaṁ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, no ce paṭinissajjeyya, ayampi bhikkhunī yāvatatiyakaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun says in anger, ‘I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training! The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics. There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them,’ then the nuns should correct her like this: ‘Venerable, don’t say such things in anger, “I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training! The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics. There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.” Take delight, venerable; the Teaching is well proclaimed. Practice the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.’ If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop. If she then stops, all is well. If she does not stop, then after the third announcement that nun too has committed an offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_10.mp3]	83	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nun Caṇḍakāḷī had argued with the nuns. In anger she said this:<br><br>“I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training!<br><br>The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics. There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could the nun Caṇḍakāḷī say this in anger?”<br><br>…<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī said this in anger?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Caṇḍakāḷī say this in anger?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>In anger:<br><br>discontent, having hatred, hostile.<br><br>Says:<br><br>“I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training! The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics. There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.”<br><br>Her:<br><br>that nun who speaks thus.<br><br>The nuns:<br><br>other nuns who see it or hear about it. They should correct her like this:<br><br>“Venerable, don’t say such things in anger:<br><br>‘I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training!<br><br>The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics.<br><br>There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.’<br><br>Take delight, Venerable; the Teaching is well proclaimed.<br><br>Practice the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”<br><br>And they should correct her a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If she stops, all is well.<br><br>If she does not stop, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If those who hear about it do not say anything, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>That nun, even if she has to be pulled into the Sangha, should be corrected like this:<br><br>“Venerable, don’t say such things in anger:<br><br>‘I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training!<br><br>The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics.<br><br>There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.’<br><br>Take delight, Venerable; the Teaching is well proclaimed.<br><br>Practice the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”<br><br>They should correct her a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>If she stops, all is well.<br><br>If she does not stop, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>Should press her:<br><br>“And, monks, she should be pressed like this.<br><br>A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nun so-and-so says this in anger:<br><br>“I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training!<br><br>The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics.<br><br>There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.”<br><br>And she keeps on saying it.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should press her to make her stop.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The nun so-and-so says this in anger:<br><br>“I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Teaching, I renounce the Sangha, I renounce the training!<br><br>The Sakyan daughters are not the only monastics.<br><br>There are other monastics who have a sense of conscience, who are afraid of wrongdoing and fond of the training. I’ll practice the spiritual life with them.”<br><br>And she keeps on saying it.<br><br>The Sangha presses her to make her stop.<br><br>Any nun who approves of pressing her to make her stop should remain silent.<br><br>Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>For the second time I speak on this matter …<br><br>For the third time I speak on this matter …<br><br>The Sangha has pressed nun so-and-so to stop.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>For one who commits the offense entailing suspension, the offense of wrong conduct and the serious offenses are annulled.<br><br>That too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses.<br><br>After the third announcement:<br><br>there is an offense when she has been pressed for the third time, not as soon as the misconduct has been committed.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>she is sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she has not been pressed;<br><br>if she stops;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The tenth offense entailing suspension is finished. Since when were the Sakyan- daughter contemplatives the only contemplatives? There are other contemplatives who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. I will practice the monastic life in their company,” the bhikkhunīs should admonish her thus: “Venerable, don’t—angry and displeased—say, ‘I repudiate the Buddha, I repudiate the Dhamma, I repudiate the Saṅgha, I repudiate the Training. Since when were the Sakyan-daughter contemplatives the only contemplatives? There are other contemplatives who are conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. I will practice the monastic life in their company.’ Take delight, Venerable. The Dhamma is well-expounded. Follow the monastic life for the right ending of suffering.” And should that bhikkhunī, admonished thus by the bhikkhunīs, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke her up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times she desists, that is good. If she does not desist, then this bhikkhunī, also, as soon as she has fallen into the third act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha.

Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 1	Ussayavādikāsikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī ussayavādikā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā dāsena vā kammakārena vā antamaso samaṇaparibbājakenāpi, ayam bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.	Yā pana bhikkhunī ussayavādikā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā dāsena vā kammakārena vā antamaso samaṇaparibbājakenāpi, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.	Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun takes legal action against a householder or a householder’s offspring or a slave or a worker or even toward a monastic or a wanderer, then that nun has committed an immediate offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_1.mp3]	57	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.<br><br>At that time a lay follower who had given a storehouse to the Sangha of nuns had died.<br><br>He had two sons,<br><br>one with and one without faith and confidence,<br><br>and they divided their father’s property between them.<br><br>Then the one without faith said to the other,<br><br>“The storehouse is ours; let’s allocate it to one of us.”<br><br>But the one with faith responded,<br><br>“No,<br><br>our father gave it to the Sangha of nuns.”<br><br>A second time they both said the same thing,<br><br>and a third time the one without faith repeated his proposal.<br><br>The one with faith then thought,<br><br>“If I get it, I too would give it to the Sangha of nuns,”<br><br>and he said,<br><br>“Alright, let’s allocate it.”<br><br>But when they allocated it, it fell to the one without faith.<br><br>He then went to the nuns and said,<br><br>“Please leave, Venerables, this storehouse is mine.”<br><br>The nun Thullanandā said to him,<br><br>“No, your father gave it to the Sangha of nuns.”<br><br>Because they were unable to agree, they asked judges to decide on the matter.<br><br>They said,<br><br>“Venerable, who knows that it was given to the Sangha of nuns?”<br><br>Thullanandā replied,<br><br>“But Sirs, didn’t you appoint a witness who saw or heard the giving of the gift?”<br><br>Saying,<br><br>“It’s true what the Venerable says,” the judges made the storehouse the property of the Sangha of nuns.<br><br>The defeated man complained and criticized the nuns,<br><br>“They’re not monastics these shaven-headed sluts.<br><br>How could they take my storehouse?”<br><br>Thullanandā told the judges of this<br><br>and they punished him.<br><br>That man then made a dwelling place for Ājīvaka ascetics not far from the nuns,<br><br>inciting them to abuse the nuns.<br><br>Once again Thullanandā told the judges<br><br>and the judges jailed him.<br><br>People then complained and criticized those nuns,<br><br>“First the nuns take his storehouse, then they have him punished, and then they have him jailed.<br><br>Next they’ll have him executed!”<br><br>Nuns heard the complaints of those people,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā take legal action?”<br><br>Then those nuns told the monks …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā is taking legal action?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā take legal action?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Takes legal action:<br><br>what is meant is that she is the initiator of a lawsuit.<br><br>A householder:<br><br>anyone who lives at home.<br><br>A householder’s offspring:<br><br>whoever is an offspring or a sibling.<br><br>A slave:<br><br>one born in the household, one who has been bought, one who has been brought back as a captive.<br><br>A worker:<br><br>a paid worker, a servant.<br><br>A monastic or a wanderer:<br><br>anyone who is a wanderer apart from Buddhist monks, nuns, trainee nuns, novice monks, and novice nuns.<br><br>If, thinking, “I’ll initiate a lawsuit,” she looks for a companion or just goes there herself, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If she tells one other person, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If she tells a second person, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>At the end of the lawsuit, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>An immediate offense:<br><br>there is an offense as soon as the misconduct is committed, and no pressing is required.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>she is sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>only the Sangha gives the trial period for that offense, sends back to the beginning, and rehabilitates—not several nuns, not an individual nun. Therefore it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>This is the name and designation of this class of offense. Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she goes there because people pull her;<br><br>if she is asking for protection;<br><br>if she tells without specifying a person;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is deranged;<br><br>if she is overwhelmed by pain;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The first offense entailing suspension is finished. [sound:ABi_SA_1.mp3]	{The precept about –making lawsuits} Should any bhikkhunī start a legal case against a householder, a householder’s son, a slave, or a worker, or even against a wandering contemplative: this bhikkhunī, as soon as she has fallen into the first act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 9	Aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ duṭṭhā dosā appatītā aññabhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñcidesaṁ lesamattaṁ upādāya pārājikena dhammena anuddhaṁseyya, “appeva nāma naṁ imamhā brahmacariyā cāveyya”nti, tato aparena samayena samanuggāhīyamānā vā asamanuggāhīyamānā vā aññabhāgiyañceva taṁ adhikaraṇaṁ hoti. Kocideso lesamatto upādinno, bhikkhunī ca dosaṁ patiṭṭhāti, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.		Matches Bu SA 9	Uses 'bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ', ends with 'paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā...'.&nbsp;&nbsp;duṭṭhā dosā appatītā,&nbsp;samanuggāhīyamānā vā asamanuggāhīyamānā	If a nun who is angry and displeased, uses an unrelated legal issue as a pretext to charge a nun with an offense entailing expulsion, aiming to make her leave the monastic life, and then after some time, whether she is questioned or not, it is clear that the legal issue is unrelated and was used as a pretext, and she admits to her ill will, she commits an offense entailing suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_9.mp3]	77	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove,<br><br>the monks Mettiya and Bhūmajaka were descending from the Vulture Peak when they saw two goats copulating.<br><br>They said to each other,<br><br>“Let’s give the he-goat the name Dabba the Mallian<br><br>and the she-goat the name Mettiyā the nun.<br><br>We can then say,<br><br>‘Previously we spoke of what we had heard,<br><br>but now we’ve seen Dabba copulating with the nun Mettiyā.’”<br><br>They then gave them those names<br><br>and told the monks,<br><br>“Previously we spoke of what we had heard,<br><br>but now we’ve seen Dabba copulating with the nun Mettiyā.”<br><br>The monks replied,<br><br>“Don’t say such things.<br><br>Venerable Dabba wouldn’t do that.”<br><br>The monks told the Buddha.<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha had the Sangha gathered and questioned Dabba:<br><br>“Dabba, do you remember doing as these monks say?”<br><br>“Sir, you know what I’m like.”<br><br>A second<br><br>and a third time the Buddha asked<br><br>the same question<br><br>and got the same response.<br><br>He then said, “Dabba, the Dabbas don’t give such evasive answers.<br><br>If it was done by you, say so;<br><br>if it wasn’t done by you, then say that.”<br><br>“Since I was born, sir, I don’t recall having sexual intercourse even in a dream, let alone when awake.”<br><br>“Well then, monks, call those monks to account.”<br><br>And the Buddha got up from his seat and entered his dwelling.<br><br>The monks then questioned Mettiya and Bhūmajaka, who told them what had happened.<br><br>The monks said,<br><br>“So did you charge Venerable Dabba with an offense entailing expulsion, using an unrelated legal issue as a pretext?”<br><br>“Yes.”<br><br>The monks of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How could Mettiya and Bhūmajaka charge Venerable Dabba with an offense entailing expulsion, using an unrelated legal issue as a pretext?”<br><br>They rebuked those monks in many ways and then told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned those monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that you did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“Foolish men, how [sound:ABi_SA_9.mp3]	{-an issue that pertains otherwise} Should any bhikkhunī, malicious, angered, displeased, using as a mere ploy an aspect of an issue that pertains otherwise, charge a bhikkhunī with a case involving defeat, (thinking), “Surely with this I may bring about her fall from the monastic life,” then regardless of whether or not she is cross-examined on a later occasion, if the issue pertains otherwise, an aspect used as a mere ploy, and the bhikkhunī confesses her anger: this bhikkhunī, also, as soon as she has fallen into the first act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 5	Bhojanapaṭiggahaṇapaṭhamasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī avassutā avassutassa purisapuggalassa hatthato khādanīyaṁ vā, bhojanīyaṁ vā sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a lustful nun eats fresh or cooked food after receiving it directly from a lustful man, then that nun too has committed an immediate offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_5.mp3]	67	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time there was a beautiful nun called Sundarīnandā.<br><br>When people saw her in the dining hall, they gave her the best food, both the donors and the recipient having lust.<br><br>Sundarīnandā ate as much as she liked,<br><br>but not so the other nuns.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Sundarīnandā, being lustful, eat either fresh or cooked food after receiving it directly from a lustful man?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Sundarīnandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could Sundarīnandā, being lustful, eat either fresh or cooked food after receiving it directly from a lustful man?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Lustful:<br><br>having lust, longing for, in love with.<br><br>Lustful:<br><br>having lust, longing for, in love with.<br><br>Man:<br><br>a human male, not a male spirit, not a male ghost, not a male animal. He understands and is capable of having lust.<br><br>Fresh food:<br><br>apart from the five cooked foods, water, and tooth cleaners, the rest is called “fresh food”.<br><br>Cooked food:<br><br>there are five kinds of cooked food: cooked grain, porridge, flour products, fish, and meat.<br><br>If she receives fresh or cooked food with the intention of eating it, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>That too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses.<br><br>An immediate offense:<br><br>there is an offense as soon as the misconduct is committed, and no pressing is required.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>she is sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If she receives water or a tooth cleaner, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If only the man has lust, and she receives fresh or cooked food with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>If she receives water or a tooth cleaner, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If both of them have lust, and she receives fresh or cooked food with the intention of eating it directly from a male spirit, a male ghost, a <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">paṇḍaka</i>, or a male animal in human form, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>If she receives water or a tooth cleaner, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If only the male being has lust, and she receives fresh or cooked food with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If she receives water or a tooth cleaner, she commits an offense of wrong conduct." If a nun pursues schism in a united Sangha or persists in taking up a legal issue conducive to schism, the nuns should correct her like this: ‘Venerable, don’t pursue schism in the united Sangha or persist in taking up a legal issue conducive to schism. Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_14.mp3]	101	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove,<br><br>Devadatta went to Kokālika, Kaṭamodakatissaka, Khaṇḍadeviyāputta, and Samuddadatta. suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called “an offense entailing suspension”.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and he perceives it as such, and he does not stop, he commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but he is unsure of it, and he does not stop, he commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but he perceives it as illegitimate, and he does not stop, he commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but he perceives it as legitimate, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but he is unsure of it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and he perceives it as such, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if he has not been pressed;<br><br>if he stops;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is deranged;<br><br>if he is overwhelmed by pain;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The training rule on schism in the Sangha, the tenth, is finished. [sound:ABi_SA_14.mp3]	{-schism of the Saṅgha} Should any bhikkhunī agitate for a schism in a Saṅgha in concord, or should she persist in taking up an issue conducive to schism, the bhikkhunīs should admonish her thus: “Do not, Venerable, agitate for a schism in a Saṅgha in concord or persist in taking up an issue conducive to schism. Let the venerable be reconciled with the Saṅgha, for a Saṅgha in concord, on complimentary terms, free from dispute, having a common recitation, dwells in peace.” And should that bhikkhunī, admonished thus by the bhikkhunīs, persist as before, the bhikkhunīs are to rebuke her up to three times so as to desist. If while being rebuked up to three times she desists, that is good. If she does not desist, then this bhikkhunī, also, as soon as she has fallen into the third act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 13.2	Pāpasamācāradutiyasikkhāpadaṁ	santi saṅghe aññāpi bhikkhuniyo evācārā evaṁsaddā evaṁsilokā bhikkhunisaṅghassa vihesikā aññamaññissā vajjappaṭicchādikā, tā saṅgho na kiñci āha		Unique to Bhikkhunī		There are other nuns in the Sangha who have such behavior, reputation, and notoriety, and who harass the Sangha of nuns and hide each other’s offenses. The Sangha says nothing to them.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_13.2.mp3]	93							[sound:ABi_SA_13.2.mp3]	There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha with the same conduct, the same reputation, the same notoriety,&nbsp;exasperating the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, hiding one another’s faults, but the Saṅgha doesn’t say anything to them.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 4	Ukkhittakaosāraṇasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena ukkhittaṁ bhikkhuniṁ dhammena vinayena satthusāsanena anapaloketvā kārakasaṅghaṁ, anaññāya gaṇassa chandaṁ osāreyya, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun, without getting permission from the Sangha that did the legal procedure and without the consent of the community, readmits a nun who has been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching and the Monastic Law and the Teacher’s instruction, then that nun too has committed an immediate offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_4.mp3]	66	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Caṇḍakāḷī was quarrelsome and argumentative, and she created legal issues in the Sangha.<br><br>But when a legal procedure was being done against her, the nun Thullanandā objected.<br><br>Soon afterwards Thullanandā went to a village on some business.<br><br>The Sangha of nuns<br><br>took the opportunity to eject Caṇḍakāḷī for not recognizing an offense.<br><br>When Thullanandā had finished her business in that village, she returned to Sāvatthī.<br><br>On her return, Caṇḍakāḷī neither prepared a seat for her, nor set out a foot stool, a foot scraper, or water for washing the feet; and she did not go out to meet her to receive her bowl and robe, nor ask whether she wanted water to drink.<br><br>Thullanandā asked her<br><br>why she was acting like this.<br><br>She replied, “That’s how it is, Venerable, when you don’t have a protector.”<br><br>“But how is it, Venerable, that you don’t have a protector?”<br><br>“When the nuns knew<br><br>that no one would speak up for me because I am not esteemed by them and I didn’t have a protector, they ejected me for not recognizing an offense.”<br><br>“They are incompetent fools. They don’t know about legal procedures or their flaws, nor what makes them fail or succeed.<br><br>But we know all these things.<br><br>We can get legal procedures done that haven’t been done, and we can get procedures that have been done overturned.” And she quickly gathered a sangha of nuns and readmitted the nun Caṇḍakāḷī.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā readmit a nun who had been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction, without first getting permission from the Sangha that did the legal procedure and without the consent of the community?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā readmit a nun who had been ejected by a unanimous Sangha in accordance with the Teaching, the Monastic Law, and the Teacher’s instruction, without first getting permission from the Sangha that did the legal procedure and without the consent of the community?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A unanimous Sangha:<br><br>those belonging to the same Buddhist sect and staying within the same monastery zone.<br><br>Who has been ejected:<br><br>who has been ejected for not recognizing an offense, for not making amends, or for not giving up a bad view.<br><br>In accordance with the Teaching and the Monastic Law:<br><br>in accordance with that Teaching, in accordance with that Monastic Law.<br><br>In accordance with the Teacher’s instruction:<br><br>in accordance with the Victor’s instruction, in accordance with the Buddha’s instruction.<br><br>Without getting permission from the Sangha that did the legal procedure:<br><br>without having asked permission of the Sangha that did the legal procedure of ejection.<br><br>Without the consent of the community:<br><br>without being aware of any consent from the community.<br><br>If, intending to readmit her, she searches for a group or establishes a monastery zone, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. After each of the first two announcements, she commits a serious offense. When the last announcement is finished, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>That too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses.<br><br>An immediate offense:<br><br>there is an offense as soon as the misconduct is committed, and no pressing is required.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>she is sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she readmits her, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she readmits her, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she readmits her, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she readmits her after getting permission from the Sangha that did the procedure;<br><br>if she readmits her with the consent of the community;<br><br>if she readmits one who is behaving properly;<br><br>if she readmits her when the Sangha that did the procedure is unavailable;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fourth offense entailing suspension is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī bhaṇḍanakārikā hoti kalahakārikā vivādakārikā bhassakārikā saṅghe [sound:ABi_SA_4.mp3]	{-restoring one suspended} Should any bhikkhunī— without having obtained permission from the Saṅgha who performed the act, without knowing the desire of the group—restore a bhikkhunī whom a Saṅgha acting in harmony, in line with the Dhamma, in line with&nbsp;the Vinaya, in line with the teacher’s instructions, has suspended: this bhikkhunī, also, as soon as she has fallen into the first act of offence, is to be (temporarily) excluded, and it entails initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha.

Unique to Bhikkhunī		If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop. If she then stops, all is well. Eteneva upāyena āvāhānipi kārāpeti, vivāhānipi kārāpeti, vāreyyānipi kārāpeti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā purāṇagaṇakiyā dhītā abhirūpā hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā. Tirogāmakā ājīvakasāvakā āgantvā taṁ gaṇakiṁ etadavocuṁ-""dehāyye, imaṁ kumārikaṁ amhākaṁ kumārakassā""ti.<br><br>Sā evamāha-""ahaṁ khvayyo, tumhe na jānāmi-‘ke vā ime kassa vā’ti. Ayañca me ekadhītikā, tirogāmo ca gantabbo, nāhaṁ dassāmī""ti.<br><br>Manussā te ājīvakasāvake etadavocuṁ-""kissa tumhe, ayyo, āgatatthā""ti? ""Idha mayaṁ, ayyo, amukaṁ nāma gaṇakiṁ dhītaraṁ yācimhā amhākaṁ kumārakassa. Sā evamāha-‘ahaṁ khvayyo, tumhe na jānāmi-ke vā ime kassa vā’ti. Ayañca me ekadhītikā, tirogāmo ca gantabbo, nāhaṁ dassāmī""ti.<br><br>""Kissa tumhe, ayyo, taṁ gaṇakiṁ dhītaraṁ yācittha? Nanu ayyo udāyī vattabbo. Ayyo udāyī dāpessatī""ti.<br><br>Atha kho te ājīvakasāvakā yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavocuṁ-""idha mayaṁ, bhante, amukaṁ nāma gaṇakiṁ dhītaraṁ yācimhā amhākaṁ kumārakassa. Sā evamāha-‘ahaṁ khvayyo, tumhe na jānāmi-ke vā ime kassa vāti. Ayañca me ekadhītikā, tirogāmo ca gantabbo, nāhaṁ dassāmī’ti. Sādhu, bhante, ayyo taṁ gaṇakiṁ dhītaraṁ dāpetu amhākaṁ kumārakassā""ti.<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yena sā gaṇakī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ gaṇakiṁ etadavoca-""kissimesaṁ dhītaraṁ na desī""ti?<br><br>""Ahaṁ khvayya, ime na jānāmi-‘ke vā ime kassa vā’ti. Ayañca me ekadhītikā, tirogāmo ca gantabbo, nāhaṁ dassāmī""ti.<br><br>""Dehimesaṁ. Ahaṁ ime jānāmī""ti.<br><br>""Sace, bhante, ayyo jānāti, dassāmī""ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā gaṇakī tesaṁ ājīvakasāvakānaṁ dhītaraṁ adāsi. Atha kho te ājīvakasāvakā taṁ kumārikaṁ netvā māsaṁyeva suṇisabhogena bhuñjiṁsu. Tato aparena dāsibhogena bhuñjanti.<br><br>Atha kho sā kumārikā mātuyā santike dūtaṁ pāhesi-""ahañhi duggatā dukkhitā, na sukhaṁ labhāmi. Māsaṁyeva maṁ suṇisabhogena bhuñjiṁsu. Tato aparena dāsibhogena bhuñjanti. Āgacchatu me, mātā, maṁ nessatū""ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā gaṇakī yena te ājīvakasāvakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te ājīvakasāvake etadavoca-""māyyo, imaṁ kumārikaṁ dāsibhogena bhuñjittha. Suṇisabhogena imaṁ kumārikaṁ bhuñjathā""ti.<br><br>Te evamāhaṁsu-""natthamhākaṁ tayā saddhiṁ āhārūpahāro, samaṇena saddhiṁ amhākaṁ āhārūpahāro, gaccha tvaṁ, na mayaṁ taṁ jānāmā""ti. Atha kho sā gaṇakī tehi ājīvakasāvakehi apasāditā punadeva sāvatthiṁ paccāgañchi.<br><br>Dutiyampi kho sā kumārikā mātuyā santike dūtaṁ pāhesi-""ahañhi duggatā dukkhitā, na sukhaṁ labhāmi. Māsaṁyeva maṁ suṇisabhogena bhuñjiṁsu. Tato aparena dāsibhogena bhuñjanti. Āgacchatu me, mātā, maṁ nessatū""ti. Atha kho sā gaṇakī yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca-""sā kira, bhante, kumārikā duggatā dukkhitā, na sukhaṁ labhati. Māsaṁyeva naṁ suṇisabhogena bhuñjiṁsu. Tato aparena dāsibhogena bhuñjanti. Vadeyyātha, bhante-‘māyyo, imaṁ kumārikaṁ dāsibhogena bhuñjittha. Suṇ<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yena te ājīvakasāvakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te ājīvakasāvake etadavoca-""māyyo, imaṁ kumārikaṁ dāsibhogena bhujjittha. Suṇisabhogena imaṁ kumārikaṁ bhuñjathā""ti.<br><br>Te evamāhaṁsu-""natthamhākaṁ tayā saddhiṁ āhārūpahāro, gaṇakiyā saddhiṁ amhākaṁ āhārūpahāro. Samaṇena bhavitabbaṁ abyāvaṭena. Samaṇo assa susamaṇo, gaccha tvaṁ, na mayaṁ taṁ jānāmā""ti. Atha kho āyasmā udāyī tehi ājīvakasāvakehi apasādito punadeva sāvatthiṁ paccāgañchi.<br><br>Tatiyampi kho sā kumārikā mātuyā santike dūtaṁ pāhesi-""ahañhi duggatā dukkhitā, na sukhaṁ labhāmi. Māsaṁyeva maṁ suṇisabhogena bhuñjiṁsu. Tato aparena dāsibhogena bhuñjanti. Āgacchatu me, mātā, maṁ nessatū""ti. Dutiyampi kho sā gaṇakī yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavoca-""sā kira, bhante, kumārikā duggatā dukkhitā, na sukhaṁ labhati. Māsaṁyeva naṁ suṇisabhogena bhuñjiṁsu. Tato aparena dāsibhogena bhuñjanti. Vadeyyātha, bhante-‘māyyo, imaṁ kumārikaṁ dāsibhogena bhuñjittha<br><br>""Paṭhamampāhaṁ tehi ājīvakasāvakehi apasādito, gaccha tvaṁ, nāhaṁ gamissāmī""ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā gaṇakī ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti-""evaṁ duggato hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ dukkhito hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ mā sukhaṁ labhatu ayyo udāyī, yathā me kumārikā duggatā dukkhitā na sukhaṁ labhati pāpikāya sassuyā pāpakena sasurena pāpakena sāmikenā""ti.<br><br>Sāpi kho kumārikā ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti-""evaṁ duggato hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ dukkhito hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ mā sukhaṁ labhatu ayyo udāyī, yathāhaṁ duggatā dukkhitā na sukhaṁ labhāmi pāpikāya sassuyā pāpakena sasurena pāpakena sāmikenā""ti.<br><br>Aññāpi itthiyo asantuṭṭhā sassūhi vā sasurehi vā sāmikehi vā, tā evaṁ oyācanti-""evaṁ duggato hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ dukkhito hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ mā sukhaṁ labhatu ayyo udāyī, yathā mayaṁ duggatā dukkhitā na sukhaṁ labhāma pāpikāhi sassūhi pāpakehi sasurehi pāpakehi sāmikehī""ti.<br><br>Yā pana tā itthiyo santuṭṭhā sassūhi vā sasurehi vā sāmikehi vā tā evaṁ āyācanti-""evaṁ sukhito hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ sajjito hotu ayyo udāyī, evaṁ sukhamedho hotu ayyo udāyī, yathā mayaṁ sukhitā sajjitā sukhamedhā bhaddikāhi sassūhi bhaddakehi sasurehi bhaddakehi sāmikehī""ti.<br><br>Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū ekaccānaṁ itthīnaṁ oyācantīnaṁ ekaccānaṁ itthīnaṁ āyācantīnaṁ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti-""kathañhi nāma āyasmā udāyī sañcarittaṁ samāpajjissatī""ti.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṁ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ paṭipucchi-""saccaṁ kira tvaṁ, udāyi, sañcarittaṁ samāpajjasī""ti?<br><br>""Saccaṁ, bhagavā""ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṁ, moghapurisa, sañcarittaṁ samāpajjissasi. Netaṁ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha-<br><br>""Yo pana bhikkhu sañcarittaṁ samāpajjeyya, itthiyā vā purisamatiṁ purisassa vā itthimatiṁ, jāyattane vā jārattane vā, saṅghādiseso""ti.<br><br>Evañcidaṁ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ hoti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā dhuttā uyyāne paricārentā aññatarissā vesiyā santike dūtaṁ pāhesuṁ-""āgacchatu uyyāne paricāressāmā""ti.<br><br>Sā evamāha-""ahaṁ khvayyo, tumhe na jānāmi-‘ke vā ime kassa vā’ti. Ahañcamhi bahubhaṇḍā bahuparikkhārā, bahinagarañca gantabbaṁ. Nāhaṁ gamissāmī""ti.<br><br>Atha kho so dūto tesaṁ dhuttānaṁ etamatthaṁ ārocesi. Evaṁ vutte, aññataro puriso te dhutte etadavoca-""kissa tumhe, ayyo, etaṁ vesiṁ yācittha? Nanu ayyo udāyī vattabbo. Ayyo udāyī uyyojessatī""ti.<br><br>Evaṁ vutte, aññataro upāsako taṁ purisaṁ etadavoca-""māyyo, evaṁ avaca. Na kappati samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ evarūpaṁ kātuṁ. Nāyyo udāyī evaṁ karissatī""ti. Evaṁ vutte, ""karissati na karissatī""ti abbhutamakaṁsu.<br><br>Atha kho te dhuttā yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ etadavocuṁ-""idha mayaṁ, bhante, uyyāne paricārentā asukāya nāma vesiyā santike dūtaṁ pahiṇimhā-‘āgacchatu uyyāne paricāressāmā’ti. Sā evamāha-‘ahaṁ khvayyo, tumhe na jānāmi-ke vā ime kassa vāti, ahañcamhi bahubhaṇḍā bahuparikkhārā, bahinagarañca gantabbaṁ. Nāhaṁ gamissāmī’ti. Sādhu, bhante, ayyo taṁ vesiṁ uyyojetū""ti.<br><br>Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yena sā vesī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ vesiṁ etadavoca-""kissimesaṁ na gacchasī""ti?<br><br>""Ahaṁ khvayya, ime na jānāmi-‘ke vā ime kassa vā’ti. Ahañcamhi bahubhaṇḍā bahuparikkhārā, bahinagarañca gantabbaṁ. Nāhaṁ gamissāmī""ti.<br><br>""Gacchimesaṁ. Ahaṁ ime jānāmī""ti.<br><br>""Sace, bhante, ayyo jānāti ahaṁ gamissāmī""ti. Atha kho te dhuttā taṁ vesiṁ ādāya uyyānaṁ agamaṁsu.<br><br>Atha kho so upāsako ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti-""kathañhi nāma ayyo udāyī taṅkhaṇikaṁ sañcarittaṁ samāpajjissatī""ti.<br><br>Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tassa upāsakassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti-""kathañhi nāma āyasmā udāyī taṅkhaṇikaṁ sañcarittaṁ samāpajjissatī""ti.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ …pe… ""saccaṁ kira tvaṁ, udāyi, taṅkhaṇikaṁ sañcarittaṁ samāpajjasī""ti?<br><br>""Saccaṁ, bhagavā""ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṁ, moghapurisa, taṅkhaṇikaṁ sañcarittaṁ samāpajjissasi? Netaṁ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe… evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha-"	"Yo panāti<br><br>yo yādiso …pe…<br><br>bhikkhūti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippeto bhikkhūti.<br><br>Sañcarittaṁ samāpajjeyyāti<br><br>itthiyā vā pahito purisassa santike gacchati, purisena vā pahito itthiyā santike gacchati.<br><br>Itthiyā vā purisamatinti<br><br>purisassa matiṁ itthiyā āroceti.<br><br>Purisassa vā itthimatinti<br><br>itthiyā matiṁ purisassa āroceti.<br><br>Jāyattane vāti<br><br>jāyā bhavissasi.<br><br>Jārattane vāti<br><br>jārī bhavissasi.<br><br>Antamaso taṅkhaṇikāyapīti<br><br>muhuttikā bhavissasi.<br><br>Saṅghādisesoti<br><br>…pe… tenapi vuccati ""saṅghādiseso""ti.<br><br>Dasa itthiyo- māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sārakkhā saparidaṇḍā.<br><br>Dasa bhariyāyo- dhanakkītā chandavāsinī bhogavāsinī paṭavāsinī odapattakinī obhaṭacumbaṭā dāsī ca bhariyā ca kammakārī ca bhariyā ca dhajāhaṭā muhuttikā.<br><br>Māturakkhitā nāma<br><br>mātā rakkhati gopeti issariyaṁ kāreti vasaṁ vatteti.<br><br>Piturakkhitā nāma<br><br>pitā rakkhati gopeti issariyaṁ kāreti vasaṁ vatteti.<br><br>Mātāpiturakkhitā nāma<br><br>mātāpitaro rakkhanti gopenti issariyaṁ kārenti vasaṁ vattenti.<br><br>Bhāturakkhitā nāma<br><br>bhātā rakkhati gopeti issariyaṁ kāreti vasaṁ vatteti.<br><br>Bhaginirakkhitā nāma<br><br>bhaginī rakkhati gopeti issariyaṁ kāreti vasaṁ vatteti.<br><br>Ñātirakkhitā nāma<br><br>ñātakā rakkhanti gopenti issariyaṁ kārenti vasaṁ vattenti.<br><br>Gottarakkhitā nāma<br><br>sagottā rakkhanti gopenti issariyaṁ kārenti vasaṁ vattenti.<br><br>Dhammarakkhitā nāma<br><br>sahadhammikā rakkhanti gopenti issariyaṁ kārenti vasaṁ vattenti.<br><br>Sārakkhā nāma<br><br>gabbhepi pariggahitā hoti- mayhaṁ esāti. Antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi.<br><br>Saparidaṇḍā nāma<br><br>kehici daṇḍo ṭhapito hoti-yo itthannāmaṁ itthiṁ gacchati ettako daṇḍoti.<br><br>Dhanakkītā nāma<br><br>dhanena kiṇitvā vāseti.<br><br>Chandavāsinī nāma<br><br>piyo piyaṁ vāseti.<br><br>Bhogavāsinī nāma<br><br>bhogaṁ datvā vāseti.<br><br>Paṭavāsinī nāma<br><br>paṭaṁ datvā vāseti.<br><br>Odapattakinī nāma<br><br>udakapattaṁ āmasitvā vāseti.<br><br>Obhaṭacumbaṭā nāma<br><br>cumbaṭaṁ oropetvā vāseti.<br><br>Dāsī nāma<br><br>dāsī ceva hoti bhariyā ca.<br><br>Kammakārī nāma<br><br>kammakārī ceva hoti bhariyā ca.<br><br>Dhajāhaṭā nāma<br><br>karamarānītā vuccati.<br><br>Muhuttikā nāma<br><br>taṅkhaṇikā vuccati.<br><br>Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ māturakkhitaṁ brūhi-‘hohi kira itthannāmassa bhariyā dhanakkītā’""ti. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṁsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ piturakkhitaṁ brūhi …pe… mātāpiturakkhitaṁ brūhi … bhāturakkhitaṁ brūhi … bhaginirakkhitaṁ brūhi … ñātirakkhitaṁ brūhi … gottarakkhitaṁ brūhi … dhammarakkhitaṁ brūhi … sārakkhaṁ brūhi … saparidaṇḍaṁ brūhi-‘hohi kira itthannāmassa bhariyā dhanakkītā’""ti. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṁsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Nikkhepapadāni.<br><br>Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ māturakkhitañca piturakkhitañca brūhi-‘hotha kira itthannāmassa bhariyāyo dhanakkītā’""ti. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṁsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ māturakkhitañca mātāpiturakkhitañca …pe… māturakkhitañca bhāturakkhitañca … māturakkhitañca bhaginirakkhitañca … māturakkhitañca ñātirakkhitañca … māturakkhitañca gottarakkhitañca … māturakkhitañca dhammarakkhitañca … māturakkhitañca sārakkhañca … māturakkhitañca saparidaṇḍañca brūhi-‘hotha kira itthannāmassa bhariyāyo dhanakkītā’""ti. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṁsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Khaṇḍacakkaṁ.<br><br>Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ piturakkhitañca mātāpiturakkhitañca brūhi-‘hotha kira itthannāmassa bhariyāyo dhanakkītā’""ti. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṁsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Baddhacakkaṁ mūlaṁ saṅkhittaṁ.<br><br>(…) Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ saparidaṇḍañca māturakkhitañca brūhi-‘hotha kira itthannāmassa bhariyāyo dhanakkītā’""ti. Paṭiggaṇhāti vīmaṁsati paccāharati, āpatti saṅghādisesassa.<br><br>Puriso bhikkhuṁ pahiṇati-""gaccha, bhante, itthannāmaṁ saparidaṇḍañca piturakkhitañca …pe… saparidaṇḍañca mātāpiturakkhitañca … saparidaṇḍañca bhāturakkhitañca … saparidaṇḍañca bhaginirakkhitañca … saparidaṇḍañca ñātirakkhitañca … saparidaṇḍañca gottarakkhitañca … saparidaṇḍañca dhammarakkhitañca … saparidaṇḍañca sārakkhañca brūhi-‘hotha kira itthannāmassa bhariyāyo dhanakkītā’""ti.
