Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::4.Saṅghādisesuddeso	BI VIN PAT BI SA 6	Bhojanapaṭiggahaṇadutiyasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī evaṁ vadeyya: “kiṁ te, ayye, eso purisapuggalo karissati avassuto vā anavassuto vā, yato tvaṁ anavassutā, iṅgha, ayye, yaṁ te eso purisapuggalo deti khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā, taṁ tvaṁ sahatthā paṭiggahetvā khāda vā bhuñja vā”ti, ayampi bhikkhunī paṭhamāpattikaṁ dhammaṁ āpannā nissāraṇīyaṁ saṅghādisesaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun says, ‘Venerable, what can this man do to you, whether he has lust or not, if you’re without? Go on, venerable, receive it with your own hands and then eat whatever fresh or cooked food he gives you,’ then that nun too has committed an immediate offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_6.mp3]	70	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time there was a beautiful nun called Sundarīnandā.<br><br>When people saw her in the dining hall, they were affected by lust, and they gave her the best food.<br><br>Being afraid of wrongdoing, Sundarīnandā did not receive it.<br><br>The nun next to her said,<br><br>“Why didn’t you receive it, Venerable?”<br><br>“Because they have lust.”<br><br>“But do you have lust?”<br><br>“No.”<br><br>“What can this man do to you, whether he has lust or not, when you’re without it?<br><br>Go on, Venerable, receive it with your own hands, and eat whatever fresh or cooked food he gives you.”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could a nun say,<br><br>‘What can this man do to you, whether he has lust or not, when you’re without it?<br><br>Go on, Venerable, receive it with your own hands, and eat whatever fresh or cooked food he gives you’?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that a nun said this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could a nun say this?”<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Says:<br><br>if she urges her on, saying, “Venerable, what can this man do to you, whether he has lust or not, if you’re without? Go on, Venerable, receive it with your own hands and then eat whatever fresh or cooked food he gives you,” then she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If, because of her statement, the other nun receives fresh or cooked food with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>At the end of the meal, she commits an offense entailing suspension.<br><br>That too:<br><br>this is said with reference to the preceding offenses.<br><br>An immediate offense:<br><br>there is an offense as soon as the misconduct is committed, and no pressing is required.<br><br>Entailing sending away:<br><br>she is sent away from the Sangha.<br><br>Suspension:<br><br>… Therefore, too, it is called an offense entailing suspension.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If she urges her on to receive water or a tooth cleaner, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If, because of her statement, the other nun receives it with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If, when only the male being has lust, she urges her on to eat fresh or cooked food received directly from a male spirit, a male ghost, a <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">paṇḍaka</i>, or a male animal in human form, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If, because of her statement, the other nun receives it with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>At the end of the meal, she commits a serious offense.<br><br>If she urges her on to receive water or a tooth cleaner, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If, because of her statement, the other nun receives it with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct."	There is no offense:<br><br>if she urges her on, knowing that he has no lust;<br><br>if she urges her on, thinking that she is not receiving because of anger;<br><br>if she urges her on, thinking that she is not receiving because of compassion for the family;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The sixth offense entailing suspension is finished. [sound:ABi_SA_6.mp3]	{-2nd about accepting food} Should any bhikkhunī say, “What does it matter to you whether this man is lusting or not, when you are not lusting? Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun walks to the next inhabited area by herself or crosses a river by herself or spends the night apart by herself or lags behind her companions by herself, then that nun too has committed an immediate offense entailing sending away and suspension.	Saṅghādisesuddeso		[sound:Bi_SA_3.mp3]	63	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a nun who was a pupil of Bhaddā Kāpilānī had an argument with the nuns and then went to her relatives’ village.<br><br>Not seeing her pupil anywhere, Bhaddā Kāpilānī asked the nuns, “Where’s so-and-so? Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun asks for one thing and then for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_4.mp3]	134	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nun Thullanandā was sick.<br><br>A lay follower went to her and asked,<br><br>“Venerable, what’s wrong with you? There is no offense:<br><br>if she asks for both at the same time;<br><br>if she can show a benefit in asking;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fourth training rule is finished. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::5.Nissaggiya pācittiyā::1 Patta Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI NP 2	Akālacīvarabhājanasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṁ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun determines out-of-season robe-cloth as ‘in-season’, and then distributes it, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_2.mp3]	130	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time, after completing the rainy-season residence in a village monastery, a number of nuns were traveling to Sāvatthī. They were perfect in conduct and deportment, but poorly dressed in shabby robes.<br><br>Some lay followers who saw them thought,<br><br>“These nuns are perfect in conduct and deportment, but poorly dressed in shabby robes; they must’ve been robbed,” and they gave out-of-season robe-cloth to the Sangha of nuns.<br><br>Because they had performed the robe-making ceremony, the nun Thullanandā<br><br>determined it as in-season robe-cloth, and then distributed it.<br><br>The lay followers asked those nuns whether<br><br>they had obtained any robe-cloth.<br><br>They replied that they hadn’t<br><br>and told them what had happened.<br><br>Those lay followers then complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā determine out-of-season robe-cloth as ‘in-season’, and then distribute it?”<br><br>The nuns heard the complaints of those lay followers,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā do this?”<br><br>Those nuns then told the monks,<br><br>who in turn told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Out-of-season robe-cloth:<br><br>for one who has not participated in the robe-making ceremony, it is robe-cloth given during the eleven months. For one who has participated in the robe-making ceremony, it is robe-cloth given during the seven months. Also, if it is given in the robe season, but the cloth is designated, it is called “out-of-season robe-cloth”.<br><br>If she distributes it after determining the out-of-season robe-cloth as “in-season”, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When she gets it, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>The robe-cloth should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it’s to be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1/en/brahmali#2.1.21"">Bi Np 1:2.1.21</a>–Bi Np 1:2.1.43, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>… ‘Venerables, this out-of-season robe-cloth, which I distributed after determining it as “in-season”, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should give …<br><br>‘I give this robe-cloth back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is out-of-season robe-cloth and she perceives it as such, and she distributes it after determining it as “in-season”, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is out-of-season robe-cloth, but she is unsure of it, and she distributes it after determining it as “in-season”, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is out-of-season robe-cloth, but she perceives it as in-season robe-cloth, and she distributes it after determining it as “in-season”, there is no offense.<br><br>If it is in-season robe-cloth, but she perceives it as out-of-season robe-cloth, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is in-season robe-cloth, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is in-season robe-cloth and she perceives it as such, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if she distributes out-of-season robe-cloth that she perceives as in-season;<br><br>if she distributes in-season robe-cloth that she perceives as in-season;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The second training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		When a personal requisite is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>The first subchapter on almsbowls.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_10.mp3]	140	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Thullanandā was a why,<br><br>and she replied, “I have neither donor, nor worker.”<br><br>Then, after collecting voluntary contributions for the yard of Thullanandā’s dwelling, the people gave the collected requisites to Thullanandā.<br><br>But even though she had asked for them, Thullanandā exchanged those requisites for tonics, which she then used.<br><br>When the people found out about this, they complained and criticized her,<br><br>“When personal requisites are designated for a specific purpose and were asked for, how could the nun Thullanandā exchange them for something else?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“When personal requisites are designated for a specific purpose and were asked for, how could the nun Thullanandā exchange them for something else?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun :<br><br>The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A requisite is designated for a specific purpose:<br><br>it was given for a specific purpose.<br><br>Personal:<br><br>belonging to an individual nun, not to the Sangha, not to a group.<br><br>Was asked for:<br><br>that she herself had asked for.<br><br>Exchanges it for something else:<br><br>if, apart from the purpose for which it was given, she exchanges it for something else, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When she gets it, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>It should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it’s to be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1/en/brahmali#2.1.21"">Bi Np 1:2.1.21</a>–Bi Np 1:2.1.43, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>‘Venerables, this thing, which I got in exchange for a personal requisite that was designated for a specific purpose and had been asked for, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should give …<br><br>‘I give this back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is for a specific purpose and she perceives that it is, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is for a specific purpose, but she is unsure of it, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is for a specific purpose, but she does not perceive that it is, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>When she receives in return what had been relinquished, it is to be used in accordance with the intention of the donors.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, but she perceives that it is, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, and she does not perceive that it is, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if she uses the remainder;<br><br>if she uses it after getting permission from the owners;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The tenth training rule is finished. Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_8.mp3]	138	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns staying in the yard belonging to a certain association were weak because of a lack of congee.<br><br>Then, after collecting voluntary contributions to supply the nuns with congee, that association stored the ingredients in a shop. They then went to the nuns and said,<br><br>“Venerables, congee ingredients are stored in such-and-such a shop. Please have someone get rice from there, have congee cooked, and then eat it.”<br><br>But the nuns exchanged those ingredients for tonics, which they then used.<br><br>When that association found out about this, they complained and criticized them,<br><br>“When collective ingredients are designated for a specific purpose, how could the nuns exchange them for something else?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nuns did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“When collective ingredients are designated for a specific purpose, how could the nuns exchange them for something else?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A requisite is designated for a specific purpose:<br><br>it was given for a specific purpose.<br><br>Collective:<br><br>belonging to a group, not to the Sangha, not to an individual nun.<br><br>Exchanges it for something else:<br><br>if, apart from the purpose for which it was given, she exchanges it for something else, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When she gets it, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>It should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it’s to be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1/en/brahmali#2.1.21"">Bi Np 1:2.1.21</a>–Bi Np 1:2.1.43, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>‘Venerables, this thing, which I got in exchange for a collective requisite that was designated for a specific purpose, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should give …<br><br>‘I give this back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is for a specific purpose and she perceives that it is, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is for a specific purpose, but she is unsure of it, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is for a specific purpose, but she does not perceive that it is, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>When she receives in return what had been relinquished, it is to be used in accordance with the intention of the donors.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, but she perceives that it is, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, and she does not perceive that it is, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if she uses the remainder;<br><br>if she uses it after getting permission from the owners;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The eighth training rule is finished. Venerables, these thirty rules on relinquishment and confession come up for recitation.<br><br>1. If a nun collects almsbowls, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>2. If a nun determines out-of-season robe-cloth as ‘in-season’, and then distributes it, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>3. If a nun trades robes with a nun and then says, ‘Here’s your robe; give me that robe of mine. That which is yours is yours, and that which is mine is mine. Give me that, and take back what’s yours;’ and she just takes it or has it taken, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>4. If a nun asks for one thing and then for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>5. If a nun gets one thing in exchange and then something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>6. When a requisite belonging to the Sangha is designated for a specific purpose, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>7. When a requisite belonging to the Sangha is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>8. When a collective requisite is designated for a specific purpose, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>9. When a collective requisite is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>10. When a personal requisite is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>The first subchapter on almsbowls.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_0-10.mp3]	141							[sound:ABi_NP_0-10.mp3]	Now, Venerables, these thirty matters entailing confession with forfeiture come up for recitation.<br><br>1. {The precept about -a bowl hoard} Should any bhikkhunī make a bowl hoard (have more than one bowl in her possession), it is to be forfeited and confessed. [See Bhikkhus’ N.P. 21]<br><br>2. {-distributing out-of-season robe-cloth} Should any bhikkhunī, having determined an out-of-season robe- cloth to be an in-season robe-cloth, distribute it, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>3. {-exchanging a robe} Should any bhikkhunī, having exchanged robe-cloth with another bhikkhunī, later say to her, “Here, Venerable. This is your robe-cloth. Bring me that robe-cloth of mine. What was yours is still yours. What was mine is still mine. Bring me that one of mine. Take yours back,” and then snatch it back or have it snatched back, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>4. {-asking for another} Should any bhikkhunī, having had one thing asked for, (then send it back and) have another thing asked for, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>5. {-getting another in exchange} Should any bhikkhunī, having had one thing bought, (then send it back and) have another thing bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>6. {-1st about exchanging a Saṅgha belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, using a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for the Saṅgha, have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>7. {-2nd Saṅgha belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for the Saṅgha, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>8. {-1st about exchanging a group belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, using a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for a group, have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>9. {-2nd group belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for a group, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>10. {-exchanging something belonging to an individual} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for an individual, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>Part One: The Bowl Chapter

Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_3.mp3]	133	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Thullanandā was using a robe she had received after trading with another nun.<br><br>But the other nun folded up the robe she had received and put it aside.<br><br>Thullanandā then said to her,<br><br>“Venerable, where’s that robe that I traded with you?”<br><br>She brought out the robe and showed it to her,<br><br>and Thullanandā said,<br><br>“Here’s your robe and give me that robe of mine. That which is yours is yours and that which is mine is mine. Give me that and take back what’s yours.” And she just took it.<br><br>That nun then told the nuns what had happened.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā trade a robe with a nun and then take it back?”<br><br>Those nuns then told the monks,<br><br>who in turn told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā trade a robe with a nun and then take it back?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>With a nun:<br><br>with another nun.<br><br>Robes:<br><br>one of the six kinds of robe-cloth, but not smaller than what can be assigned to another.<br><br>Trades:<br><br>much with little or little with much.<br><br>Just takes it:<br><br>if she just takes it herself, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>Has it taken:<br><br>if she asks another, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If she only asks once, then even if the other takes back many, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>The robe-cloth should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it’s to be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1/en/brahmali#2.1.21"">Bi Np 1:2.1.21</a>–Bi Np 1:2.1.43, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>… ‘Venerables, this robe-cloth, which I took back after trading it with a nun, is to be relinquished. [sound:ABi_NP_3.mp3]	{-exchanging a robe} Should any bhikkhunī, having exchanged robe-cloth with another bhikkhunī, later say to her, “Here, Venerable. This is your robe-cloth. Bring me that robe-cloth of mine. What was yours is still yours. What was mine is still mine. Bring me that one of mine. Take yours back,” and then snatch it back or have it snatched back, it is to be forfeited and confessed.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::5.Nissaggiya pācittiyā::1 Patta Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI NP 7	Dutiyasaṅghikacetāpanasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		When a requisite belonging to the Sangha is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_7.mp3]	137	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the lay followers collected voluntary contributions to supply the Sangha of nuns with robes. They stored the requisites in a cloth merchant’s shop, and then went to the nuns and said,<br><br>“Venerables, requisites to be used for robes are stored in such-and-such a cloth merchant’s shop. Please have someone get cloth from there and share it out.”<br><br>But even though they had asked for them, the nuns exchanged those requisites for tonics, which they then used.<br><br>When the lay followers found out about this, they complained and criticized them,<br><br>“When requisites belonging to the Sangha are designated for a specific purpose and were asked for, how could the nuns exchange them for something else?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nuns did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“When requisites belonging to the Sangha are designated for a specific purpose and were asked for, how could the nuns exchange them for something else?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A requisite is designated for a specific purpose:<br><br>it was given for a specific purpose.<br><br>Belonging to the Sangha:<br><br>belonging to the Sangha, not to a group, not to an individual nun.<br><br>Was asked for:<br><br>that she herself had asked for.<br><br>Exchanges it for something else:<br><br>if, apart from the purpose for which it was given, she exchanges it for something else, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When she gets it, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>It should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it’s to be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1/en/brahmali#2.1.21"">Bi Np 1:2.1.21</a>–Bi Np 1:2.1.43, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>‘Venerables, this thing, which I got in exchange for a requisite belonging to the Sangha that was designated for a specific purpose and had been asked for, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should give …<br><br>‘I give this back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is for a specific purpose and she perceives that it is, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is for a specific purpose, but she is unsure of it, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is for a specific purpose, but she does not perceive that it is, and she exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>When she receives in return what had been relinquished, it is to be used in accordance with the intention of the donors.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, but she perceives that it is, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not for a specific purpose, and she does not perceive that it is, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if she uses the remainder;<br><br>if she uses it after getting permission from the owners;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The seventh training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena upāsakā bhikkhunisaṅghassa cīvaratthāya chandakaṁ saṅgharitvā aññatarassa pāvārikassa ghare parikkhāraṁ nikkhipitvā bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“amukassa, ayye, pāvārikassa ghare cīvaratthāya parikkhāro nikkhitto, tato cīvaraṁ āharāpetvā bhājethā”ti.<br><br>Bhikkhuniyo tena ca parikkhārena sayampi yācitvā bhesajjaṁ cetāpetvā paribhuñjiṁsu.<br><br>Upāsakā jānitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo aññadatthikena parikkhārena …pe…<br><br>bhikkhunīti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.<br><br>Aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikenāti<br><br>aññassatthāya dinnena.<br><br>Saṅghikenāti<br><br>saṅghassa, na gaṇassa, na ekabhikkhuniyā.<br><br>Saññācikenāti<br><br>sayaṁ yācitvā.<br><br>Aññaṁ cetāpeyyāti<br><br>yaṁatthāya dinnaṁ taṁ ṭhapetvā aññaṁ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṁ.<br><br>Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṁ [sound:ABi_NP_7.mp3]	{-2nd Saṅgha belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for the Saṅgha, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::5.Nissaggiya pācittiyā::1 Patta Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI NP 5	Aññacetāpana sikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun gets one thing in exchange and then something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_5.mp3]	135	"At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nun Thullanandā was sick.<br><br>A lay follower went to her and asked,<br><br>“I hope you’re bearing up, Venerable, I hope you’re getting better?”<br><br>“I’m not bearing up, and I’m not getting better.”<br><br>“We’ll deposit a <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">kahāpaṇa</i> coin in such-and-such a shop. Please get whatever you wish from there.”<br><br>Thullanandā then said to a trainee nun,<br><br>“Go to such-and-such a shop and bring back a <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">kahāpaṇa</i>’s worth of oil.”<br><br>That trainee nun did just that and gave it to Thullanandā.<br><br>Thullanandā said,<br><br>“I don’t need oil; I need ghee.”<br><br>The trainee nun returned to the shopkeeper and said,<br><br>“It seems the nun doesn’t need oil, but ghee. Here’s your oil; please give me ghee.”<br><br>“Venerable, if we were to take back goods that have been sold, when would our goods be sold?<br><br>When oil is bought, oil is taken away. Buying ghee, you receive that, and you’ll take that away.”<br><br>The trainee nun started to cry.<br><br>The nuns asked her<br><br>why,<br><br>and she told them what had happened.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā get one thing in exchange and then something else?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā get one thing in exchange and then something else?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:"	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Gets one thing in exchange:<br><br>whatever she gets in exchange.<br><br>Then something else:<br><br>apart from that thing, if she gets something else in exchange, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When she gets it, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>It should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it’s to be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np1/en/brahmali#2.1.21"">Bi Np 1:2.1.21</a>–Bi Np 1:2.1.43, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>… ‘Venerables, this thing, which I got in exchange, having first gotten something else in exchange, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should give …<br><br>‘I give this back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is something else and she perceives it as such, and she gets that in exchange, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is something else, but she is unsure of it, and she gets that in exchange, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is something else, but she does not perceive it as such, and she gets that in exchange, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is not something else, but she perceives it as such, and she gets that in exchange, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not something else, but she is unsure of it, and she gets that in exchange, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is not something else, and she does not perceive it as such, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if she gets both in exchange at the same time;<br><br>if she can show a benefit in doing the exchange;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fifth training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti.<br><br>Atha kho aññataro upāsako yena thullanandā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā thullanandaṁ bhikkhuniṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“kacci, ayye, khamanīyaṁ kacci yāpanīyan”ti?<br><br>“Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyan”ti.<br><br>“Amukassa, ayye, āpaṇikassa ghare kahāpaṇaṁ nikkhipissāmi, tato yaṁ iccheyyāsi taṁ āharāpeyyāsī”ti.<br><br>Thullanandā bhikkhunī aññataraṁ sikkhamānaṁ āṇāpesi—<br><br>“gaccha, sikkhamāne, amukassa āpaṇikassa gharā kahāpaṇassa telaṁ āharā”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā sikkhamānā tassa āpaṇikassa gharā kahāpaṇassa telaṁ āharitvā thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā adāsi.<br><br>Thullanandā bhikkhunī evamāha—<br><br>“na me, sikkhamāne, telena attho, sappinā me attho”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā sikkhamānā yena so āpaṇiko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ āpaṇikaṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“na kira, āvuso, ayyāya telena attho, sappinā attho, handa te telaṁ, sappiṁ me dehī”ti.<br><br>“Sace mayaṁ, ayye, vikkītaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ puna ādiyissāma, kadā amhākaṁ bhaṇḍaṁ vikkāyissati.<br><br>Telassa kayena telaṁ haṭaṁ, sappissa kayaṁ āhara, sappiṁ harissasī”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā sikkhamānā rodantī aṭṭhāsi.<br><br>Bhikkhuniyo taṁ sikkhamānaṁ etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“kissa tvaṁ, sikkhamāne, rodasī”ti?<br><br>Atha kho sā sikkhamānā bhikkhunīnaṁ etamatthaṁ ārocesi.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpessatī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpetī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpessati.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Yā panāti<br><br>yā yādisā …pe…<br><br>bhikkhunīti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.<br><br>Aññaṁ cetāpetvāti<br><br>yaṁ kiñci cetāpetvā.<br><br>Aññaṁ cetāpeyyāti<br><br>taṁ ṭhapetvā aññaṁ cetāpeti, payoge dukkaṭaṁ.<br><br>Paṭilābhena nissaggiyaṁ hoti.<br><br>Nissajjitabbaṁ saṅghassa vā gaṇassa vā ekabhikkhuniyā vā.<br><br>Evañca pana, bhikkhave, nissajjitabbaṁ.<br><br>…pe…<br><br>“idaṁ me, ayye, aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpitaṁ nissaggiyaṁ, imāhaṁ saṅghassa nissajjāmī”ti …pe…<br><br>dadeyyāti …pe…<br><br>dadeyyunti …pe…<br><br>ayyāya dammīti.<br><br>Aññe aññasaññā aññaṁ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>Aññe vematikā aññaṁ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>Aññe anaññasaññā aññaṁ cetāpeti, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>Anaññe aññasaññā anaññaṁ cetāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Anaññe vematikā anaññaṁ cetāpeti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Anaññe anaññasaññā anāpatti. There is no offense:<br><br>if she uses the remainder;<br><br>if she uses it after getting permission from the owners;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The sixth training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		When a collective requisite is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::5.Nissaggiya pācittiyā::1 Patta Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI NP 1	Pattasannicayasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī pattasannicayaṁ kareyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.		Matches Bu NP 21	Differs: 'pattasannicayaṁ kareyya' vs 'atirekapatto dhāretabbo'.	If a nun collects almsbowls, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Pattavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_1.mp3]	129	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns from the group of six had collected a large number of almsbowls.<br><br>When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized those nuns,<br><br>“How can the nuns collect a large number of bowls? Will they start up as bowl merchants or set up a bowl shop?”<br><br>The nuns heard the complaints of those people,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized those nuns,<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six collect bowls?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nuns from the group of six do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six collect bowls?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>An almsbowl:<br><br>there are two kinds of bowls: the iron bowl and the ceramic bowl.<br><br>And there are three sizes of bowls: the large bowl, the medium bowl, and the small bowl.<br><br>The large bowl:<br><br>it takes half an <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">āḷhaka</i> measure of boiled rice, a fourth part of fresh food, and a suitable amount of curry.<br><br>The medium bowl:<br><br>it takes a <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">nāḷika</i> measure of boiled rice, a fourth part of fresh food, and a suitable amount of curry.<br><br>The small bowl:<br><br>it takes a <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">pattha</i> measure of boiled rice, a fourth part of fresh food, and a suitable amount of curry.<br><br>Anything larger than this is not a bowl, nor anything smaller.<br><br>Collects:<br><br>almsbowls that have neither been determined nor assigned to another.<br><br>Entailing relinquishment:<br><br>entailing relinquishment at dawn.<br><br>The bowl should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual nun.<br><br>“And, monks, it should relinquished like this.<br><br>After approaching the Sangha, that nun should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the senior nuns. She should then squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘Venerables, this almsbowl, which I have kept for more than one day, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.’<br><br>After relinquishing it, she is to confess the offense.<br><br>The confession should be received by a competent and capable nun.<br><br>The relinquished bowl is then to be given back:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>This almsbowl, which was to be relinquished by the nun so-and-so, has been relinquished to the Sangha.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should give this bowl back to nun so-and-so.’<br><br>Or: after approaching several nuns, that nun should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the senior nuns. She should then squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘Venerables, this almsbowl, which I have kept for more than one day, is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to you.’<br><br>After relinquishing it, she is to confess the offense.<br><br>The confession should be received by a competent and capable nun.<br><br>The relinquished bowl is then to be given back:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask you to listen.<br><br>This almsbowl, which was to be relinquished by the nun so-and-so, has been relinquished to you.<br><br>If the Venerables are ready, you should give this bowl back to nun so-and-so.’<br><br>Or: after approaching a single nun, that nun should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘This almsbowl, which I have kept for more than one day, is to be relinquished.<br><br>I relinquish it to you.’<br><br>After relinquishing it, she is to confess the offense.<br><br>The confession should be received by that nun.<br><br>The relinquished bowl is then to be given back:<br><br>‘I give this almsbowl back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is more than one day and she perceives it as more, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is more than one day, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is more than one day, but she perceives it as less, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been determined, but she perceives that it has, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been assigned to another, but she perceives that it has, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been given away, but she perceives that it has, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been not lost, but she perceives that it has …<br><br>If it has not been destroyed, but she perceives that it has …<br><br>If it has not been broken, but she perceives that it has …<br><br>If it has not been stolen, but she perceives that it has, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If she uses an almsbowl that should be relinquished without first relinquishing it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than one day, but she perceives it as more, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than one day, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than one day and she perceives it as less, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if, before dawn, it has been determined, assigned to another, given away, lost, destroyed, broken, stolen, or taken on trust;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>Soon afterwards the nuns from the group of six did not give back a relinquished bowl.<br><br>They told the Buddha.<br><br>“Monks, a relinquished almsbowl should be given back.<br><br>If a nun doesn’t give it back, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”<br><br>The first training rule is finished. Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Cīvaravaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_12.mp3]	143	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Thullanandā was a learned reciter, and she was confident and skilled at giving teachings.<br><br>On one occasion when the weather was warm, King Pasenadi of Kosala put on an expensive linen cloak and went to Thullanandā. "There is no offense:<br><br>if she carries out an exchange for one worth at most two-and-a-half <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">kaṁsa</i> coins;<br><br>if she carries out an exchange for one worth less than two-and-a-half <i lang=""pi"" translate=""no"">kaṁsa</i> coins;<br><br>if it is from relatives;<br><br>if it is from those who have given an invitation;<br><br>if it is for the benefit of someone else;<br><br>if it is by means of her own property;<br><br>if she gets one in exchange that has little value from someone who wants to exchange one of great value;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The twelfth training rule is finished." When her robe is finished and the robe season has ended, a nun should keep an extra robe for ten days at the most.<br>If she keeps it longer than that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Cīvaravaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_13.mp3]	144	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Vesālī at the Gotamaka Shrine,<br><br>he allowed the three robes for the monks.<br><br>When they heard about this, the monks from the group of six went to the village in one set of three robes, stayed in the monastery in another set, and went to bathe in yet another set.<br><br>The monks of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the monks from the group of six keep extra robes?”<br><br>After rebuking those monks in many ways, they told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that you do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“Foolish men, how can you do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:<br><br>‘If a monk keeps an extra robe, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.’”<br><br>In this way the Buddha laid down this training rule for the monks.<br><br>Soon afterwards Venerable Ānanda was offered an extra robe.<br><br>He wanted to give it to Venerable Sāriputta<br><br>who was staying at Sāketa.<br><br>Knowing that the Buddha had laid down a rule against having extra robes, Ānanda thought,<br><br>“What should I do now?”<br><br>He told the Buddha, who said,<br><br>“How long is it, Ānanda, before Sāriputta returns?”<br><br>“Nine or ten days.”<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, you should keep an extra robe for ten days at the most.<br><br>And so, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>When his robe is finished:<br><br>the monk has made a robe; or the robe-cloth has been lost, destroyed, or burned; or his expectation of receiving further robe-cloth is disappointed.<br><br>The robe season has ended:<br><br>it has ended according to one of the eight key phrases or the Sangha has ended it.<br><br>For ten days at the most:<br><br>it should be kept ten days at a maximum.<br><br>An extra robe:<br><br>it has not been determined nor assigned to another.<br><br>Robe:<br><br>one of the six kinds of robe-cloth, but not smaller than what can be assigned to another.<br><br>If he keeps it longer than that, it becomes subject to relinquishment:<br><br>it becomes subject to relinquishment at dawn on the eleventh day.<br><br>The robe-cloth should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual.<br><br>“And, monks, it should be relinquished like this.<br><br>After approaching the Sangha, that monk should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the senior monks. He should then squat on his heels, raise his joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘Venerables, this robe-cloth, which I have kept over ten days, is to be relinquished.<br><br>I relinquish it to the Sangha.’<br><br>After relinquishing it, he should confess the offense.<br><br>The confession should be received by a competent and capable monk.<br><br>The relinquished robe-cloth is then to be given back:<br><br>‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>This robe-cloth, which was to be relinquished by monk so-and-so, has been relinquished to the Sangha.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should give this robe-cloth back to monk so-and-so.’<br><br>Or: after approaching several monks, that monk should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the senior monks. He should then squat on his heels, raise his joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘Venerables, this robe-cloth, which I have kept over ten days, is to be relinquished.<br><br>I relinquish it to you.’<br><br>After relinquishing it, he should confess the offense.<br><br>The confession should be received by a competent and capable monk.<br><br>The relinquished robe-cloth is then to be given back:<br><br>‘Please, venerables, I ask you to listen.<br><br>This robe-cloth, which was to be relinquished by monk so-and-so, has been relinquished to you.<br><br>If the venerables are ready, you should give this robe-cloth back to monk so-and-so.’<br><br>Or: after approaching a single monk, that monk should arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, squat on his heels, raise his joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘This robe-cloth, which I have kept over ten days, is to be relinquished.<br><br>I relinquish it to you.’<br><br>After relinquishing it, he should confess the offense.<br><br>The confession should be received by that monk.<br><br>The relinquished robe-cloth is then to be given back:<br><br>‘I give this robe-cloth back to you.’”<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is more than ten days and he perceives it as more, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is more than ten days, but he is unsure of it, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is more than ten days, but he perceives it as less, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been determined, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been assigned to another, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been given away, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been lost, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been destroyed, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been burned, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been stolen, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If he uses robe-cloth that should be relinquished without first relinquishing it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than ten days, but he perceives it as more, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than ten days, but he is unsure of it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than ten days and he perceives it as less, there is no offense.	There is no offense:<br><br>if within ten days it has been determined, assigned to another, given away, lost, destroyed, burned, stolen, or taken on trust;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>Soon afterwards the monks from the group of six did not give back relinquished robe-cloth.<br><br>They told the Buddha.<br><br>“Monks, relinquished robe-cloth should be given back.<br><br>If you don’t give it back, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”<br><br>The training rule on the robe season, the first, is finished. [sound:ABi_NP_13.mp3]	{-kaṭhina} When a bhikkhunī has finished her robe- making and the frame is destroyed (her kaṭhina privileges are in abeyance), she is to keep an extra robe- cloth ten days at most. Beyond that, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [1]

Matches Bu NP 10	Uses 'bhikkhuniṁ', 'ayye' instead of 'bhante', 'ayyā' instead of 'āyasmā',&nbsp;ayyaṁ instead of&nbsp;āyasmantaṃ,&nbsp;Tāya&nbsp;bhikkhuniyā,&nbsp;panāyyāya instead of&nbsp;pan'āyasmato, kāci&nbsp;veyyāvaccakarā,&nbsp;cīvaratthikāya,&nbsp;bhikkhuniyo, bhikkhuniyā veyyāvaccakarā&nbsp;niddisitabbā&nbsp;ārāmikā&nbsp;vā upāsikā, esā, saññattā sā, upasaṅkamatāyyā, codetabbā&nbsp;sāretabbā, codayamānā sārayamānā, tuṇhībhūtāya, tuṇhībhūtā uddissa tiṭṭhamānā, uttari vāyamamānā, yatassā, tassā bhikkhuniyā	If a king, a king’s employee, a brahmin, or a householder sends a robe fund for a nun by messenger, saying, ‘Buy robe-cloth with this robe fund and give it to nun so-and-so,’ and the messenger goes to that nun and says, ‘Venerable, I have brought a robe fund for you. Please receive it,’ then that nun should reply, ‘We don’t receive robe funds, but we do receive allowable robe-cloth at the right time.’ If that messenger says, ‘Is there anyone who provides services for you?’ the nun, if she needs robe-cloth, should point out a monastery worker or a lay follower and say, ‘They provide services for the nuns.’ If the messenger instructs that service provider and then returns to the nun and says, ‘Venerable, I have instructed the service provider you pointed out. Please go to them at the right time and they’ll give you robe-cloth,’ then, if that nun needs robe-cloth, she should go to that service provider and prompt them and remind them two or three times, saying, ‘I need robe-cloth.’ If she then gets robe-cloth, all is well. If she does not get it, she should stand in silence for it at most six times. If she then gets robe-cloth, all is well. If she makes any further effort and then gets robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. If she does not get robe-cloth, she should go to the owners of that robe fund, or send a message, saying, ‘That nun hasn’t received any benefit from the robe fund you sent for her. Please recover what’s yours, or it might perish.’ This is the proper procedure.<br><br>The second subchapter on robes. I would like you to use the robe-cloth.”<br><br>When Upananda did not say anything to that lay follower,<br><br>that government official sent him a second message<br><br>saying the same thing.<br><br>When Upananda still did not say anything to that lay follower,<br><br>that government official sent him a third message.<br><br>At that time the householder association had made an agreement that whoever came late to a meeting would be fined fifty coins. There is no offense:<br><br>if he prompts three times and stands six times;<br><br>if he prompts less than three times and stands less than six times;<br><br>if it is given without prompting;<br><br>if the owners prompt and then it is given;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The training rule on kings is finished. [sound:ABi_NP_20.mp3]	{-the king} In case a king, a royal official, a brahmin or a householder sends a robe fund for a bhikkhunī via a messenger: “Purchase a robe with this robe fund and supply the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with a robe.” If the messenger approaches the bhikkhunī and says: “This robe fund is for the venerable. May the venerable accept this robe fund.” Then the bhikkhunī is to tell the messenger: “We do not accept robe funds, friend. We accept robes at the right time.” If the messenger says to the bhikkhunī: “Does the venerable have a steward?” Then, if the bhikkhunī desires a robe, she may indicate a steward, either a monastery attendant or a lay follower: “That, sir, is the bhikkhunīs’ steward.” If the messenger, having instructed the steward, goes to the bhikkhunī and says: “I have instructed the steward the venerable indicated. May the venerable go and she (the steward) will supply you with a robe in-season.” Then the bhikkhunī, desiring a robe and approaching the steward, may prompt and remind her 2 or 3 times: “I have need of a robe.” Should (the steward) produce the robe after being prompted and reminded 2 or 3 times, that is good. If she does not produce the robe, (the bhikkhunī) should stand in silence 4, 5, or 6 times at most for that purpose. Should (the steward) produce the robe after (the bhikkhunī) has stood in silence for the purpose 4, 5, or 6 times at most, that is good. If she should not produce the robe, but she produces the robe after (the bhikkhunī) has tried further, it is to be forfeited and confessed. If she should not produce (the robe), then the bhikkhunī herself should go to the place from which the robe fund was brought, or a messenger should be sent (to say), “The robe fund that you, Venerable sirs, sent for the sake of the bhikkhunī has given no benefit to the bhikkhunī at all. May you be united with what is yours. May what is yours not be lost.” This is the proper course here. [10]<br><br>Part Two: The Robe-cloth Chapter

When her robe is finished and the robe season has ended, if out-of-season robe-cloth is offered to a nun, she may receive it if she wishes. If she receives it, she should quickly make a robe. If there is not enough cloth, but she is expecting more, she should keep it at most one month to make up the lack. If she keeps it longer than that, then even if she expects more cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Cīvaravaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_15.mp3]	150	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a monk had been given robe-cloth outside the robe season.<br><br>While he was making the robe, he realized there was not enough cloth.<br><br>Lifting it up, he smoothed it out again and again.<br><br>While walking about the dwellings, the Buddha saw that monk acting in this way.<br><br>He went up to him and said,<br><br>“What are you doing, monk?”<br><br>“Sir, I’ve been given this out-of-season robe-cloth,<br><br>but it’s not enough to make a robe.<br><br>That’s why I lift it up and smooth it out again and again.”<br><br>“Are you expecting to receive more cloth?”<br><br>“I am.”<br><br>Soon afterwards the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, I allow you to keep out-of-season robe-cloth if you are expecting to receive more.”<br><br>When they heard about this, some monks kept out-of-season robe-cloth for more than a month,<br><br>keeping them in bundles on a bamboo robe rack.<br><br>While walking about the dwellings, Venerable Ānanda saw that robe-cloth,<br><br>and he asked the monks,<br><br>“Whose cloth is this?”<br><br>“It’s our out-of-season robe-cloth, which we’re keeping because we’re expecting more.”<br><br>“But how long have you kept it?”<br><br>“More than a month.”<br><br>Venerable Ānanda complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can these monks keep out-of-season robe-cloth for more than a month?”<br><br>After rebuking those monks in many ways, Venerable Ānanda told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned the monks:<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that there are monks who do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can those foolish men keep out-of-season robe-cloth for more than a month?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>When his robe is finished:<br><br>the monk has made a robe; or the robe-cloth has been lost, destroyed, or burned; or his expectation of receiving further robe-cloth is disappointed.<br><br>The robe season has ended:<br><br>it has ended according to one of the eight key phrases or the Sangha has ended it.<br><br>Out-of-season robe-cloth:<br><br>for one who has not participated in the robe-making ceremony, it is robe-cloth given during the eleven months.<br><br>for one who has participated in the robe-making ceremony, it is robe-cloth given during the seven months.<br><br>Also, if it is given in the robe season, but the cloth is designated, it is called “out-of-season robe-cloth”.<br><br>If it is offered:<br><br>If it is offered by a sangha, by a group, by a relative, or by a friend, or if it is rags, or if he got it by means of his own property.<br><br>If he wishes:<br><br>if he desires, he may receive it.<br><br>If he receives it, he should quickly make a robe:<br><br>it should be made within ten days.<br><br>If there is not enough cloth:<br><br>if there is not enough cloth when the robe is being made.<br><br>He should keep it at most one month:<br><br>he should keep it one month at a maximum.<br><br>To make up the lack:<br><br>for the purpose of making up the lack.<br><br>But he is expecting more:<br><br>he is expecting more from a sangha, from a group, from a relative, or from a friend, or he is expecting to get rags, or he is expecting to get it by means of his own property.<br><br>If he keeps it longer than that, then even if he expects more cloth:<br><br>if he is given the expected robe-cloth on the same day as he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be made into a robe within ten days.<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth the day after he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be made into a robe within ten days.<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth two days after …<br><br>three days after …<br><br>eighteen days after …<br><br>… nineteen days after he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be made into a robe within ten days.<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth twenty days after he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be made into a robe within nine days.<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth twenty-one days after he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be made into a robe within eight days. …<br><br>twenty-two days after …<br><br>twenty-seven days after …<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth twenty-eight days after he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be made into a robe within one day.<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth twenty-nine days after he was given the original robe-cloth, it must be determined, assigned to another, or given away on that very day.<br><br>If he does not determine it, assign it to another, or give it away, it becomes subject to relinquishment at dawn on the thirtieth day.<br><br>The robe-cloth should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual.<br><br>“And, monks, it should be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-np1#3.2.5"">Bu NP 1:3.2.5</a>–3.2.29, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>‘Venerables, this out-of-season robe-cloth, which I have kept for more than a month, is to be relinquished.<br><br>I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should give …<br><br>‘I give this robe-cloth back to you.’”<br><br>If he is given the expected robe-cloth, but it is different from the robe-cloth originally given to him, and there are days remaining, he does not have to make a robe if he does not want to.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is more than a month and he perceives it as more, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is more than a month, but he is unsure of it, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it is more than a month, but he perceives it as less, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been determined, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been assigned to another, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been given away, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been lost, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been destroyed, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been burned, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If it has not been stolen, but he perceives that it has, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If he uses robe-cloth that should be relinquished without first relinquishing it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than a month, but he perceives it as more, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than a month, but he is unsure of it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is less than a month and he perceives it as less, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if within a month it has been determined, assigned to another, given away, lost, destroyed, burned, stolen, or taken on trust;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The third training rule on the robe season, the third, is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno akālacīvaraṁ uppannaṁ hoti.<br><br>Tassa taṁ cīvaraṁ kayiramānaṁ [sound:ABi_NP_15.mp3]	{-out-of-season robe-cloth} When a bhikkhunī has finished her robe-making and the frame is destroyed: If out-of-season robe-cloth accrues to her, she may accept it if she so desires. Once she accepts it, she is to make it up immediately. If it should not be enough,&nbsp;she may lay it aside for a month at most if she has an expectation for filling the lack. Should she keep it beyond that, even when there is an expectation (for further cloth), it is to be forfeited and confessed. [3]	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::5.Nissaggiya pācittiyā::2 Cīvara Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI NP 18	Paṭhamaupakkhaṭasikkhāpadaṁ	Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa aññātakassa gahapatissa vā gahapatāniyā vā cīvaracetāpannaṁ upakkhaṭaṁ hoti: “iminā cīvaracetāpannena cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarena acchādessāmī”ti. Tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “sādhu vata, maṁ āyasmā iminā cīvaracetāpannena evarūpaṁ vā evarūpaṁ vā cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā acchādehī”ti kalyāṇakamyataṁ upādāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.		Matches Bu NP 8	Uses 'bhikkhuniṁ',&nbsp;cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā	If a male or female householder has set aside a robe fund for an unrelated nun, thinking, ‘With this robe fund I will buy robe-cloth and give it to nun so-and-so;’ and if that nun, without first being invited, goes to them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘Please use this robe fund to buy such-and-such robe-cloth and then give it to me,’ and she does so because she wants something fine, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Cīvaravaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_18.mp3]	159	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a certain man said to his wife,<br><br>“I’m going to give robe-cloth to Venerable Upananda.”<br><br>An alms-collecting monk heard that man making that statement.<br><br>He then went to Upananda the Sakyan and said,<br><br>“Upananda, you have much merit.<br><br>In such-and-such a place I heard a man tell his wife<br><br>that he’s going to give you robe-cloth.”<br><br>“He’s my supporter.”<br><br>Upananda then went to that man and said,<br><br>“Is it true that you want to give me robe-cloth?”<br><br>“Yes,<br><br>that’s just what I was thinking.”<br><br>“If that’s the case, give me such-and-such robe-cloth.<br><br>For what’s the point of giving robe-cloth that I won’t use?”<br><br>That man complained and criticized him,<br><br>“These Sakyan monastics have great desires. They’re not content.<br><br>It’s no easy matter to give them robe-cloth.<br><br>How could Venerable Upananda come to me and say what kind of robe-cloth he wants without first being invited by me to do so?”<br><br>The monks heard the complaints of that man,<br><br>and the monks of few desires complained and criticized him,<br><br>“How could Venerable Upananda go to a householder and say what kind of robe-cloth he wants without first being invited to do so?”<br><br>After rebuking him in many ways, they told the Buddha. Soon afterwards he had the Sangha gathered and questioned Upananda:<br><br>“Is it true, Upananda, that you did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>“Is he a relative of yours?”<br><br>“No.”<br><br>“Foolish man, people who are unrelated don’t know what’s appropriate and inappropriate, what’s good and bad, in dealing with each other.<br><br>And still you did this.<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	"<b>Definitions</b><br><br>For a monk:<br><br>for the benefit of a monk; making a monk the object of consideration, one wants to give to him.<br><br>Unrelated:<br><br>anyone who is not a descendant of one’s male ancestors going back eight generations, either on the mother’s side or on the father’s side.<br><br>A male householder:<br><br>any man who lives at home.<br><br>A female householder:<br><br>any woman who lives at home.<br><br>A robe fund:<br><br>money, gold, a pearl, a gem, a coral, a crystal, cloth, thread, or cotton wool.<br><br>With this robe fund:<br><br>with that which is at one’s disposal.<br><br>I will buy:<br><br>having traded.<br><br>I will give:<br><br>I will donate.<br><br>If that monk:<br><br>the monk the robe fund has been set aside for.<br><br>Without first being invited:<br><br>he or she has not said beforehand: “Venerable, what kind of robe-cloth do you need? What kind of robe-cloth can I buy for you?”<br><br>Goes to them:<br><br>having gone to their house or having gone wherever.<br><br>Specifies the kind of robe-cloth he wants:<br><br>please make it long or wide or closely woven or soft.<br><br>This robe fund:<br><br>that which is at one’s disposal.<br><br>Such-and-such:<br><br>long or wide or closely woven or soft.<br><br>To buy:<br><br>having traded.<br><br>Give:<br><br>donate.<br><br>Because he wants something fine:<br><br>wanting something good, wanting something expensive.<br><br>If that lay person buys robe-cloth that is long, wide, closely woven, or soft because of the monk’s statement, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When he gets the robe-cloth, it becomes subject to relinquishment.<br><br>The robe-cloth should be relinquished to a sangha, a group, or an individual.<br><br>“And, monks, it should be relinquished like this.<br><br>(To be expanded as in <a href=""https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-np1#3.2.5"">Bu NP 1:3.2.5</a>–3.2.29, with appropriate substitutions.)<br><br>‘Venerables, this robe-cloth, which I received after going to an unrelated householder and saying what kind of robe-cloth I wanted without first being invited, is to be relinquished.<br><br>I relinquish it to the Sangha.’ …<br><br>the Sangha should give …<br><br>you should them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth he wants, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If the householder is unrelated, but the monk is unsure of it, and, without perceives them as related, and, without first being invited, he goes to them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth he wants, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>If the householder is related, but the monk perceives them as unrelated, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the householder is related, but the monk is unsure of it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the householder is related and the monk perceives them as such, there is no offense."	There is no offense:<br><br>if it is from relatives;<br><br>if it is from those who have given an invitation;<br><br>if it is for the benefit of another;<br><br>if it is by means of his own property;<br><br>if the householder wishes to buy something expensive, but the monk has them buy something inexpensive;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The training rule on what is set aside, the eighth, is finished. [sound:ABi_NP_18.mp3]	{-1st on setting up a robe fund} In case a man or woman householder prepares a robe fund for the sake of an unrelated bhikkhunī, thinking. “Having purchased a robe with this robe fund, I will supply the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with a robe”: If the bhikkhunī, not previously invited, approaching (the householder) should make a stipulation with regard to the robe, saying, “It would be good indeed, sir, if you supplied me (with a robe),” having purchased a robe of such-and-such a sort with this robe fund—out of a desire for something fine—it is to be forfeited and confessed.
