Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::04 Tuvaṭṭa Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 37	Antoraṭṭhasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun goes wandering without a group of travelers where it is considered risky and dangerous within her own country, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Tuvaṭṭavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_37.mp3]	253	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns went wandering without a group of travelers where it was considered risky and dangerous within their own country.<br><br>Scoundrels raped them.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns go wandering without a group of travelers where it’s considered risky and dangerous within their own country?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Within her own country:<br><br>in the country where she is living.<br><br>Risky:<br><br>a place has been seen along that road where criminals are camping, eating, standing, sitting, or lying down.<br><br>Dangerous:<br><br>criminals have been seen along that road, injuring, robbing, or beating people.<br><br>Without a group of travelers:<br><br>in the absence of a group of travelers.<br><br>Goes wandering:<br><br>when the villages are a chicken’s flight apart, then for every next village she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>When it is an uninhabited area, a wilderness, then for every six kilometers she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she travels with a group;<br><br>if she travels where it is safe and free from danger;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The seventh training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ caranti.<br><br>Dhuttā dūsenti.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ carissantī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ carantī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ carissanti.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Yā panāti<br><br>yā yādisā …pe…<br><br>bhikkhunīti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.<br><br>Antoraṭṭheti<br><br>yassa vijite viharati, tassa raṭṭhe.<br><br>Sāsaṅkaṁ nāma<br><br>tasmiṁ magge corānaṁ niviṭṭhokāso dissati, bhuttokāso dissati, ṭhitokāso dissati, nisinnokāso dissati, nipannokāso dissati.<br><br>Sappaṭibhayaṁ nāma<br><br>tasmiṁ magge corehi manussā hatā dissanti, viluttā dissanti, ākoṭitā dissanti.<br><br>Asatthikā nāma<br><br>vinā satthena.<br><br>Cārikaṁ careyyāti<br><br>kukkuṭasampāte gāme gāmantare gāmantare āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Agāmake araññe addhayojane addhayojane āpatti pācittiyassa.	Anāpatti—<br><br>satthena saha gacchati,<br><br>kheme appaṭibhaye gacchati,<br><br>āpadāsu,<br><br>ummattikāya,<br><br>ādikammikāyāti.<br><br>Sattamasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.	[sound:ABi_PC_37.mp3]	{-within a territory} Should any bhikkhunī, without joining a caravan of merchants, set out within the local king’s territory on a journey considered dubious and risky, it is to be confessed.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::04 Tuvaṭṭa Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 32	Ekattharaṇatuvaṭṭanasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭeyyuṁ, pācittiyaṁ.		Kd15/Cv5: 19.2.9-11 “You shouldn’t lie down on the same sheet, lie down under the same cover, or lie down both on the same sheet and under the same cover,&nbsp;if you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”		If two nuns lie down on the same sheet and under the same cover, they commit an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Tuvaṭṭavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_32.mp3]	245	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>two nuns were lying down on the same sheet and under the same cover.<br><br>When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can two nuns lie down on the same sheet and under the same cover? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”<br><br>The nuns heard the complaints of those people,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns do this?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>Two:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nuns:<br><br>fully ordained is what is meant.<br><br>If two lie down on the same sheet and under the same cover:<br><br>if they spread out just the one and cover themselves with just the one, they commit an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is the same sheet and the same cover, and they perceive them as such, and they lie down, they commit an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is the same sheet and the same cover, but they are unsure of it, and they lie down, they commit an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is the same sheet and the same cover, but they perceive them as different, and they lie down, they commit an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is the same sheet but different covers, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is different sheets but the same cover, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is different sheets and different covers, but they perceive them as the same, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is different sheets and different covers, but they are unsure of it, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is different sheets and different covers, and they perceive them as such, there is no offense.	There is no offense:<br><br>if they make a partition and then lie down;<br><br>if they are insane;<br><br>if they are the first offenders.<br><br>The second training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭenti.<br><br>Manussā vihāracārikaṁ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭessanti, seyyathāpi gihiniyo kāmabhoginiyo”ti.<br><br>Assosuṁ kho bhikkhuniyo tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭessantī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭentī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭessanti.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Yā panāti<br><br>yā yādisā …pe…<br><br>bhikkhuniyoti<br><br>upasampannāyo vuccanti.<br><br>Dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭeyyunti<br><br>taññeva attharitvā taññeva pārupanti, āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe ekattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā tuvaṭṭenti, āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe vematikā tuvaṭṭenti, āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Ekattharaṇapāvuraṇe nānattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā tuvaṭṭenti, āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Ekattharaṇe nānāpāvuraṇe, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Nānattharaṇe ekapāvuraṇe, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Nānattharaṇapāvuraṇe ekattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Nānattharaṇapāvuraṇe vematikā, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Nānattharaṇapāvuraṇe nānattharaṇapāvuraṇasaññā, anāpatti.	Anāpatti—<br><br>vavatthānaṁ dassetvā nipajjanti,<br><br>ummattikānaṁ,<br><br>ādikammikānanti.<br><br>Dutiyasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.	[sound:ABi_PC_32.mp3]	{-sharing one blanket} Should two bhikkhunīs share a single blanket or sleeping mat, it is to be confessed.

Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::04 Tuvaṭṭa Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 33	Aphāsukaraṇasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sañcicca aphāsuṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun intentionally makes a nun ill at ease, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Tuvaṭṭavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_33.mp3]	246	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Thullanandā was a learned reciter, and she was confident and skilled at giving teachings.<br><br>Bhaddā Kāpilānī, too, was a learned reciter who was confident and skilled at giving teachings, and she was respected for her excellence.<br><br>Because of this, people visited Bhaddā Kāpilānī first and then Thullanandā.<br><br>Overcome by jealousy, Thullanandā thought,<br><br>“These ones, who are supposedly contented and have few desires, who are supposedly secluded and not socializing, are always persuading and convincing people.” And in front of Bhaddā Kāpilānī, she walked back and forth, stood, sat down, and lay down, and she recited and had others recite, and she rehearsed.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā intentionally make Bhaddā Kāpilānī ill at ease?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A nun:<br><br>another nun.<br><br>Intentionally:<br><br>knowing, perceiving, having intended, having decided, she transgresses.<br><br>Makes ill at ease:<br><br>if, without asking permission, but thinking, “In this way she will be ill at ease,” she walks back and forth in front of her, or she stands, sits down, or lies down in front of her, or she recites, has others recite, or rehearses in front of her, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If the other person is fully ordained, and she perceives her as such, and she intentionally makes her ill at ease, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If the other person is fully ordained, but she is unsure of it, and she intentionally makes her ill at ease, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If the other person is fully ordained, but she does not perceive her as such, and she intentionally makes her ill at ease, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, and she intentionally makes her ill at ease, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, but she perceives her as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, and she does not perceive her as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if, after asking permission and not desiring to make her ill at ease, she walks back and forth in front of her, or she stands, sits down, or lies down in front of her, or she recites, has others recite, or rehearses in front of her;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The third training rule is finished. uḷārasambhāvitā”ti bhaddaṁ kāpilāniṁ paṭhamaṁ payirupāsitvā, pacchā thullanandaṁ bhikkhuniṁ payirupāsanti.<br><br>Thullanandā bhikkhunī issāpakatā—<br><br>“imā kira appicchā santuṭṭhā pavivittā asaṁsaṭṭhā yā imā saññattibahulā viññattibahulā viharantī”ti bhaddāya kāpilāniyā purato caṅkamatipi tiṭṭhatipi nisīdatipi seyyampi kappeti uddisatipi uddisāpetipi sajjhāyampi karoti.<br><br>Yā tā I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. Pācittiyā	Cittāgāravaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_44.mp3]	261	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nuns were providing services for householders.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns provide services for householders?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Services for a householder:<br><br>if she cooks congee, a meal, or fresh food for a householder, or she washes a wrap garment or a turban for them, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if it is a congee drink;<br><br>if it is a meal for the Sangha;<br><br>if it is to venerate a shrine;<br><br>if she cooks congee, a meal, or fresh food for her own service-provider, or she washes a wrap garment or a turban for them;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fourth training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun spins yarn, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Cittāgāravaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_43.mp3]	260	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nuns from the group of six were spinning yarn.<br><br>When people walking about the dwellings saw this, they complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the nuns spin yarn? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”<br><br>The nuns heard the complaints of those people,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six spin yarn?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that those nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Yarn:<br><br>there are six kinds of yarn:<br><br>linen, cotton, silk, wool, sunn hemp, and hemp.<br><br>Spins:<br><br>if she spins it herself, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every pull, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she spins yarn that has already been spun;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The third training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun goes wandering without relinquishing her lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Cittāgāravaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_48.mp3]	267	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nun Thullanandā went wandering without first relinquishing her lodging.<br><br>Soon afterwards her lodging caught fire.<br><br>Some nuns said,<br><br>“Come, Venerables, let’s remove her things.”<br><br>But others replied,<br><br>“No, let’s things?”<br><br>“No, we didn’t.”<br><br>Thullanandā complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How could the nuns not remove the contents when a lodging is burning?”<br><br>But the nuns of few desires rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Lodging:<br><br>one with a door is what is meant.<br><br>Goes wandering without relinquishing:<br><br>if she crosses the boundary of an enclosed lodging without first relinquishing it to a nun, a trainee nun, or a novice nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she goes beyond the vicinity of an unenclosed lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it has not been relinquished, and she perceives that it has not, and she goes, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it has not been relinquished, but she is unsure of it, and she goes, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it has not been relinquished, but she perceives that it has, and she goes, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she does not relinquish a lodging without a door, and then goes, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it has been relinquished, but she perceives that it has not, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it has been relinquished, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it has been relinquished, and she perceives that it has, there is no offense.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she relinquishes it and then goes;<br><br>if there is an obstacle;<br><br>if she searches, but is unable to find anyone to relinquish it to;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The eighth training rule is finished. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::05 Cittāgāra Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 45	Adhikaraṇasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā: “ehāyye, imaṁ adhikaraṇaṁ vūpasamehī”ti vuccamānā: “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vūpasameyya, na vūpasamāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If, when a nun is requested by a nun to resolve a legal issue, she agrees, but then neither resolves it nor makes any effort to resolve it, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Cittāgāravaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_45.mp3]	264	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a certain nun went to the nun Thullanandā and said,<br><br>“Please come, Venerable, and resolve this legal issue.”<br><br>Thullanandā agreed,<br><br>but then neither resolved it nor made any effort to do so.<br><br>That nun told the nuns what had happened.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā<br><br>agree to resolve a legal issue, but then neither resolve it nor make any effort to do so?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā acted like this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā act like this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>By a nun:<br><br>by another nun.<br><br>A legal issue:<br><br>there are four kinds of legal issues: legal issues arising from disputes, legal issues arising from accusations, legal issues arising from offenses, legal issues arising from business.<br><br>To resolve a legal issue:<br><br>to make a decision on a legal issue.<br><br>Then, if there were no obstacles:<br><br>when there is no obstacle.<br><br>Neither resolves it:<br><br>she does not resolve it herself.<br><br>Nor makes any effort to resolve it:<br><br>she does not ask anyone else.<br><br>If, thinking, “I’ll neither resolve it nor make any effort to resolve it,” then, by the mere fact of abandoning her duty, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If the other person is fully ordained, and she perceives her as such, and she neither resolves the legal issue nor makes any effort to resolve it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If the other person is fully ordained, but she is unsure of it, and she neither resolves the legal issue nor makes any effort to resolve it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If the other person is fully ordained, but she does not perceive her as such, and she neither resolves the legal issue nor makes any effort to resolve it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, and she neither resolves the legal issue nor makes any effort to resolve it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, but she perceives her as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If the other person is not fully ordained, and she does not perceive her as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if there is an obstacle;<br><br>if she searches, but is unable to find anyone to settle it;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fifth training rule is finished. If a nun, knowing that there are monks in a monastery, enters it without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>52. If a nun abuses or reviles a monk, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>53. If a furious nun reviles the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>54. If a nun, who has been invited to a meal, refuses an offer to eat more, and then eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>55. If a nun keeps a family to herself, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>56. If a nun spends the rainy-season residence in a monastery without monks, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>57. If a nun who has completed the rainy-season residence does not invite correction from both Sanghas in regard to three things—what has been seen, heard, or suspected—she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>58. If a nun does not go to the instruction or to a formal meeting of the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>59. Every half-month a nun should seek two things from the Sangha of monks: asking it about the observance day and going to it for the instruction. If she lets the half-month pass, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>60. If a nun, alone with a man, without getting permission from the Sangha or a group, has an abscess or a wound situated on the lower part of her body ruptured by him, or split open, washed, anointed, bandaged, or unwrapped by him, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The sixth subchapter on monasteries.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_51-60.mp3]	283							[sound:ABi_PC_51-60.mp3]	51. {-entering a monastery} Should any bhikkhunī, without asking permission, knowingly enter a monastery containing a bhikkhu, it is to be confessed. [See Bk’ Pāc. 23]<br><br>52. {-insulting a bhikkhu} Should any bhikkhunī revile or insult a bhikkhu, it is to be confessed.<br><br>53. {-insult group} Should any bhikkhunī, in a fit of temper, revile a group (of bhikkhunīs), it is to be confessed.<br><br>54. {-being invited} Should any bhikkhunī, having eaten and turned down an offer (of further food), chew or consume staple or non-staple food (elsewhere), it is to be confessed. [See Bhikkhus’ Pācittiya 35]<br><br>55. {-being stingy with families} Should any bhikkhunī be stingy with regard to families (of supporters), it is to be confessed.<br><br>56. {-residence with no bhikkhu} Should any bhikkhunī spend the rains retreat in a dwelling where there are no bhikkhus (nearby), it is to be confessed.<br><br>57. {-not inviting} Should any bhikkhunī, having completed the rains retreat, not invite (criticism) from both Communities with regard to three matters—what they have seen, heard, or suspected (her of doing)—it is to be confessed.<br><br>58. {-ovāda} Should any bhikkhunī not go for the ovāda or for the (meetings which define) communion (the uposatha and pavāraṇā), it is to be confessed.<br><br>59. {-requesting the ovāda} Every half-month a bhikkhunī should request two things from the Bhikkhu Saṅgha: the asking of the date of the uposatha and the approaching for the ovāda. In excess of that (half-month), it is to be confessed.<br><br>60. {-lower part of body} Should any bhikkhunī, without having informed a Saṅgha or a group (of bhikkhunīs), alone with a man have a boil or scar that has appeared on the lower part of her body (between the navel and the knees) burst or cut open or cleaned or smeared with a salve or bandaged or unbandaged, it is to be confessed.<br><br>Part Six: The Monastery Chapter

Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_52.mp3]	272	At one time when the Buddha was staying  in the hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood near Vesālī,<br><br>Venerable Upāli’s preceptor, Venerable Kappita, was staying in a charnel ground.<br><br>At that time the leader of the nuns from the group of six had just died.<br><br>They took her to that charnel ground, cremated her near Venerable Kappita’s dwelling, and made a stupa. They then went there to cry.<br><br>Venerable Kappita was disturbed by the noise, and so he demolished the stupa and scattered the rubble.<br><br>The nuns from the group of six thought,<br><br>“Kappita has demolished our Venerable’s stupa; let’s kill him,” and they laid a plan.<br><br>A certain nun told Venerable Upāli what was happening,<br><br>and he in turn told Venerable Kappita.<br><br>Venerable Kappita then left his dwelling and went into hiding.<br><br>Soon afterwards the nuns from the group of six went to his dwelling<br><br>and crushed it with rocks and lumps of earth. When they thought he was dead, they left.<br><br>The following morning Venerable Kappita robed up, took his bowl and robe, and entered Vesālī for almsfood.<br><br>When the nuns from the group of six saw him,<br><br>they said,<br><br>“Kappita is alive! training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure reviles him, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she abuses or reviles someone who is not fully ordained, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If he is not fully ordained, but she perceives him as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If he is not fully ordained, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If he is not fully ordained, and she does not perceive him as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she is aiming at something beneficial;<br><br>if she is aiming at giving a teaching;<br><br>if she is aiming at giving an instruction;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The second training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a furious nun reviles the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_53.mp3]	273	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nun Caṇḍakāḷī was quarrelsome and argumentative, and she created legal issues in the Sangha.<br><br>But when a legal procedure was being done against her, the nun Thullanandā objected.<br><br>Soon afterwards when Thullanandā went to a village on some business,<br><br>the Sangha of nuns<br><br>took the opportunity to eject Caṇḍakāḷī for not recognizing an offense.<br><br>When Thullanandā had finished her business, she returned to Sāvatthī.<br><br>As she was approaching, Caṇḍakāḷī neither prepared a seat for her, nor set out a foot stool, a foot scraper, or water for washing the feet;<br><br>and she did not go out to meet her to receive her bowl and robe or to ask whether she wanted water to drink.<br><br>Thullanandā asked her<br><br>why she was acting like this.<br><br>She replied, “That’s how it is, Venerable, when one doesn’t have a protector.”<br><br>“But how is it, Venerable, that you don’t have a protector?”<br><br>“When these nuns knew<br><br>that no one would speak up for me because I am not esteemed by them and I didn’t have a protector, they ejected me for not recognizing an offense.”<br><br>“They are incompetent fools! They don’t understand legal procedures, nor what makes them fail or succeed.” And being furious, she reviled the community.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could Venerable Thullanandā revile the community because she is furious?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could the nun Thullanandā do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Furious:<br><br>angry is what is meant.<br><br>The community:<br><br>the Sangha of nuns is what is meant.<br><br>Reviles:<br><br>if she reviles them, saying, “They are incompetent fools. They don’t understand legal procedures, nor what makes them fail or succeed,” she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she reviles several nuns, a single nun, or someone who is not fully ordained, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she is aiming at something beneficial;<br><br>if she is aiming at giving a teaching;<br><br>if she is aiming at giving an instruction;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The third training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī bhaṇḍanakārikā hoti kalahakārikā vivādakārikā bhassakārikā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārikā.<br><br>Thullanandā bhikkhunī tassā kamme karīyamāne paṭikkosati.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena thullanandā bhikkhunī gāmakaṁ agamāsi kenacideva karaṇīyena.<br><br>Atha kho bhikkhunisaṅgho—<br><br>“thullanandā bhikkhunī pakkantā”ti caṇḍakāḷiṁ bhikkhuniṁ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipi.<br><br>Thullanandā bhikkhunī gāmake taṁ karaṇīyaṁ tīretvā punadeva sāvatthiṁ paccāgacchi.<br><br>Caṇḍakāḷī bhikkhunī thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā āgacchantiyā neva āsanaṁ paññapesi na pādodakaṁ pādapīṭhaṁ pādakaṭhalikaṁ upanikkhipi;<br><br>na paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṁ paṭiggahesi na pānīyena āpucchi.<br><br>Thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍakāḷiṁ bhikkhuniṁ etadavoca—<br><br>“kissa tvaṁ, ayye, mayi āgacchantiyā neva āsanaṁ paññapesi na pādodakaṁ pādapīṭhaṁ pādakaṭhalikaṁ upanikkhipi;<br><br>“Evañhetaṁ, ayye, hoti yathā taṁ anāthāyā”ti.<br><br>“Kissa pana tvaṁ, ayye, anāthā”ti?<br><br>“Imā maṁ, ayye, bhikkhuniyo—<br><br>‘ayaṁ anāthā appaññātā, natthi imissā kāci pativattā’ti, āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṁsū”ti.<br><br>“bālā etā abyattā etā netā jānanti kammaṁ vā kammadosaṁ vā kammavipattiṁ vā kammasampattiṁ vā”ti, caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāsi.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma ayyā thullanandā caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāsissatī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāsatī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, thullanandā bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāsissati.<br><br>Netaṁ, adhippetā bhikkhunīti.<br><br>Caṇḍīkatā nāma<br><br>kodhanā vuccati.<br><br>Gaṇo nāma<br><br>bhikkhunisaṅgho vuccati.<br><br>Paribhāseyyāti<br><br>“bālā etā abyattā etā netā jānanti kammaṁ vā kammadosaṁ vā kammavipattiṁ vā kammasampattiṁ vā”ti paribhāsati, āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Sambahulā bhikkhuniyo vā ekaṁ bhikkhuniṁ vā anupasampannaṁ vā paribhāsati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.	Anāpatti—<br><br>atthapurekkhārāya,<br><br>dhammapurekkhārāya,<br><br>anusāsanipurekkhārāya,<br><br>ummattikāya,<br><br>ādikammikāyāti.<br><br>Tatiyasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.	[sound:ABi_PC_53.mp3]	{-insult group} Should any bhikkhunī, in a fit of temper, revile a group (of bhikkhunīs), it is to be confessed.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::06 Ārāma Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 59	Ovādūpasaṅkamanasikkhāpadaṁ	Anvaddhamāsaṁ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā uposathapucchakañca ovādūpasaṅkamanañca. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā pācittiyaṁ.		Garudhamma 3:&nbsp;Each fortnight the nuns should expect two things from the community of monks:the date of the sabbath, and visiting for advice.	Garudhamma 3: Anvaḍḍhamāsaṁ&nbsp;bhikkhuniyā&nbsp;bhikkhusaṅghato&nbsp;dve&nbsp;dhammā&nbsp;paccāsīsitabbā uposathapucchakañca,&nbsp;ovādūpasaṅkamanañca.	Every half-month a nun should seek two things from the Sangha of monks: asking it about the observance day and going to it for the instruction. If she lets the half-month pass, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_59.mp3]	279	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns did not enquire about the observance day nor ask for the instruction.<br><br>The monks complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the nuns not enquire about the observance day nor ask for the instruction?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that the nuns don’t do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can the nuns not do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>Every half-month:<br><br>every observance day.<br><br>The observance day:<br><br>there are two observance days: the fourteenth and the fifteenth day of the lunar half-month.<br><br>The instruction:<br><br>the eight important principles.<br><br>If she thinks, “I won’t enquire about the observance day, nor ask for the instruction,” then by the mere fact of abandoning her duty, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if there is an obstacle;<br><br>if she searches for a companion nun, but does not find one;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The ninth training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchanti ovādampi na yācanti.<br><br>Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchissanti ovādampi na yācissantī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchanti ovādampi na yācantī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo uposathampi na pucchissanti ovādampi na yācissanti.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Anvaddhamāsanti<br><br>anuposathikaṁ.<br><br>Uposatho nāma<br><br>dve uposathā— cātuddasiko ca pannarasiko ca.<br><br>Ovādo nāma<br><br>aṭṭha garudhammā.<br><br>“Uposathampi na pucchissāmi ovādampi na yācissāmī”ti dhuraṁ nikkhittamatte āpatti pācittiyassa.	Anāpatti—<br><br>sati antarāye,<br><br>pariyesitvā dutiyikaṁ bhikkhuniṁ na labhati,<br><br>gilānāya,<br><br>āpadāsu,<br><br>ummattikāya,<br><br>ādikammikāyāti.<br><br>Navamasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.	[sound:ABi_PC_59.mp3]	{-requesting the ovāda} Every half-month a bhikkhunī should request two things from the Bhikkhu Saṅgha: the asking of the date of the uposatha and the approaching for the ovāda. In excess of that (half-month), it is to be confessed.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::06 Ārāma Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 55	Kulamaccharinīsikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī kulamaccharinī assa, pācittiyaṁ.		Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun keeps a family to herself, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_55.mp3]	275	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a certain nun there was walking for almsfood along a street. She then went to a certain family where she sat down on the prepared seat.<br><br>The people there gave her a meal and said,<br><br>“Venerable, other nuns may come too.”<br><br>Then that nun thought,<br><br>“What can I do so that other nuns don’t come?” And she went up to other nuns and said,<br><br>“Venerables, in such-and-such a place there are malicious dogs, a fierce ox, and it’s muddy.<br><br>Don’t go there.”<br><br>Another nun, too, went to that family while walking for almsfood along that street. She sat down on the prepared seat<br><br>and the people there gave her a meal. They then asked her,<br><br>“Venerable, why don’t the nuns come here?”<br><br>And she told them what had happened.<br><br>People complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How can a nun keep a family to herself?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that a nun acted like this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could a nun act like this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A family:<br><br>there are four kinds of families: the aristocratic family, the brahmin family, the merchant family, the worker family.<br><br>Keeps for herself:<br><br>if she thinks, “What can I do so that other nuns don’t come?” and she then speaks disparagingly about that family to the nuns, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she speaks disparagingly about that family to the nuns, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she is not keeping a family to herself, but describes the drawbacks as they are;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fifth training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sāvatthiyaṁ aññatarissā visikhāya piṇḍāya caramānā yena aññataraṁ kulaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.<br><br>Atha kho te manussā taṁ bhikkhuniṁ bhojetvā etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“aññāpi, ayye, bhikkhuniyo āgacchantū”ti.<br><br>Atha kho sā bhikkhunī—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo nāgaccheyyun”ti, bhikkhuniyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca—<br><br>“amukasmiṁ, ayye, okāse vāḷā sunakhā caṇḍo balibaddo cikkhallo okāso.<br><br>Mā kho tattha agamitthā”ti.<br><br>Aññatarāpi bhikkhunī tassā visikhāya piṇḍāya caramānā yena taṁ kulaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.<br><br>Atha kho te manussā taṁ bhikkhuniṁ bhojetvā etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“kissa, ayye, bhikkhuniyo na āgacchantī”ti?<br><br>Atha kho sā bhikkhunī tesaṁ manussānaṁ etamatthaṁ ārocesi.<br><br>Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhunī kulaṁ maccharāyissatī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī kulaṁ maccharāyatī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī kulaṁ maccharāyissati.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Yā panāti<br><br>yā yādisā …pe…<br><br>bhikkhunīti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.<br><br>Kulaṁ nāma<br><br>cattāri kulāni— khattiyakulaṁ, brāhmaṇakulaṁ, vessakulaṁ, suddakulaṁ.<br><br>Maccharinī assāti<br><br>“kathaṁ bhikkhuniyo nāgaccheyyun”ti bhikkhunīnaṁ santike kulassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsati, āpatti pācittiyassa.<br><br>Kulassa vā santike bhikkhunīnaṁ avaṇṇaṁ bhāsati, āpatti pācittiyassa.	Anāpatti—<br><br>kulaṁ na maccharāyantī santaṁyeva ādīnavaṁ ācikkhati,<br><br>ummattikāya,<br><br>ādikammikāyāti.<br><br>Pañcamasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.	[sound:ABi_PC_55.mp3]	{-being stingy with families} Should any bhikkhunī be stingy with regard to families (of supporters), it is to be confessed.

Bhikkhu Pācittiya 23	Yo&nbsp;pana&nbsp;bhikkhu&nbsp;bhikkhunupassayaṁ&nbsp;upasaṅkamitvā&nbsp;bhikkhuniyo&nbsp;ovadeyya,&nbsp;pācittiyaṁ.	If a nun, knowing that there are monks in a monastery, enters it without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_51.mp3]	271	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a number of monks dressed only in sarongs were making robes in a certain village monastery.<br><br>Nuns entered that monastery without asking permission and approached those monks.<br><br>The monks complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns enter a monastery without asking permission?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns did that?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do that?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:<br><br>‘If a nun enters a monastery without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.’”<br><br>In this way the Buddha laid down this training rule for the nuns.<br><br>Soon afterwards those monks left that monastery.<br><br>But even though the nuns had heard that the monks had left, they did not go there.<br><br>Soon the monks returned.<br><br>When the nuns heard that this was the case, they asked permission and then entered that monastery.<br><br>They approached the monks and bowed down to them.<br><br>The monks then said to them, “Sisters, why didn’t you sweep the monastery, or put out water for drinking or water for washing?”<br><br>“The Buddha has laid down a training rule that we may not enter a monastery without asking permission.<br><br>That’s why we didn’t do it.”<br><br>They told the Buddha. Soon afterwards the Buddha had the Sangha gathered and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, when a monk is available, a nun should enter a monastery only after asking permission.<br><br>And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:<br><br>‘If a nun, when a monk is available, enters a monastery without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.’”<br><br>In this way the Buddha laid down this training rule for the nuns.<br><br>After leaving that monastery once more, the monks returned yet again.<br><br>Thinking that the monks were still away, the nuns entered the monastery without asking permission.<br><br>The nuns became anxious, thinking,<br><br>“We have entered a monastery without asking permission, even though a monk was available. And the Buddha has laid down a training rule against this.<br><br>Could it be that we have committed an offense entailing confession?”<br><br>They told the Buddha.<br><br>Soon afterwards he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Knowing:<br><br>she knows it by herself or others have told her or they have told her.<br><br>There are monks in a monastery:<br><br>even where monks stay at the foot of a tree.<br><br>Enters it without asking permission:<br><br>if she crosses the boundary of an enclosed monastery without asking permission of a monk or a novice monk or a monastery worker, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she enters the vicinity of an unenclosed monastery, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If there are monks in a monastery, and she perceives that there are, and she enters it without asking permission of an available monk, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If there are monks in a monastery, but she is unsure of it, and she enters it without asking permission of an available monk, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If there are monks in a monastery, but she does not perceive that there are, and she enters it without asking permission of an available monk, there is no offense.<br><br>If there are no monks in a monastery, but she perceives that there are, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If there are no monks in a monastery, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If there are no monks in a monastery, and she does not perceive that there are, there is no offense.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she enters after asking permission of an available monk;<br><br>if, when there is no available monk, she enters without asking permission;<br><br>if she goes while looking at the head of a nun in front of her;<br><br>if she is going to where the nuns have gathered;<br><br>if a path goes through the monastery;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The first training rule is finished. anāpucchā ārāmaṁ pavisitvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṁsu.<br><br>Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo anāpucchā ārāmaṁ pavisissantī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::06 Ārāma Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 54	Pavāritasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī nimantitā vā pavāritā vā khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.		Matchs Bu PC 35	Yo&nbsp;pana&nbsp;bhikkhu&nbsp;bhuttāvī&nbsp;pavārito	If a nun, who has been invited to a meal, refuses an offer to eat more, and then eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_54.mp3]	274	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a certain brahmin had invited the nuns for a meal.<br><br>When the nuns had finished and refused an invitation to eat more, they went to their respective families, where some ate and others got almsfood and left.<br><br>Soon afterwards that brahmin said this to his neighbors,<br><br>“I have satisfied the nuns. Come, and I’ll satisfy you, too.”<br><br>“How could you satisfy us?<br><br>Those nuns who were invited by you came to our houses, where some ate and others got almsfood and left.”<br><br>That brahmin complained and criticized those nuns,<br><br>“How could they eat in our house and afterwards eat elsewhere? Am I not able to give them as much as they want?”<br><br>The nuns heard the complaints of that brahmin,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How could nuns finish their meal, refuse an invitation to eat more, and then eat elsewhere?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How could nuns act in this way?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Refuses an offer to eat more:<br><br>refuses an offer to eat any of the five cooked foods.<br><br>Refuses an invitation to eat more:<br><br>eating is seen, cooked food is seen, it is brought forward within arm’s reach, a refusal is seen.<br><br>Fresh food:<br><br>apart from the five cooked foods, congee, the post-midday tonics, the seven-day tonics, and the lifetime tonics,<br><br>the rest is called “fresh food”.<br><br>Cooked food:<br><br>there are five kinds of cooked food: cooked grain, porridge, flour products, fish, and meat.<br><br>If she receives it with the intention of eating it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If she has refused an offer, and she perceives that she has, and she eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she has refused an offer, but she is unsure of it, and she eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she has refused an offer, but she does not perceive that she has, and she eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she receives post-midday tonics, seven-day tonics, or lifetime tonics for the purpose of food, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>For every mouthful, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. …	There is no offense:<br><br>if she has refused an offer to eat more, but not an invitation;<br><br>if she drinks congee;<br><br>if she eats more after getting permission from the person who invited her;<br><br>if, when there is a reason, she uses post-midday tonics, seven-day tonics, or lifetime tonics;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fourth training rule is finished. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::06 Ārāma Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 56	Abhikkhukāvāsasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ vaseyya, pācittiyaṁ.		"Garudhamma 2:&nbsp;<span style=""color: rgb(238, 238, 238); background-color: rgb(65, 65, 65);"">A nun should not commence the rainy season residence in a monastery without monks.</span>"	Na&nbsp;bhikkhuniyā&nbsp;abhikkhuke&nbsp;āvāse&nbsp;vassaṁ&nbsp;upagantabbaṁ.	If a nun spends the rainy-season residence in a monastery without monks, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_56.mp3]	276	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time a number of nuns who had completed the rainy-season residence in a village monastery went to Sāvatthī.<br><br>The nuns there asked them,<br><br>“Venerables, where did you spend the rains residence?<br><br>We hope the instruction was effective?”<br><br>“There were no monks there.<br><br>So how could the instruction be effective?”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How could nuns spend the rains residence in a monastery without monks?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How could nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>A monastery without monks:<br><br>she is not able to go to the instruction or to a formal meeting of the community.<br><br>If she thinks, “I’ll stay here for the rainy-season residence,” and she prepares a dwelling, sets out water for drinking and water for washing, and sweeps the yard, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>At dawn, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if the monks who entered the rainy-season residence there depart or disrobe or die or join another group;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The sixth training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo gāmakāvāse vassaṁvuṭṭhā sāvatthiṁ agamaṁsu.<br><br>Bhikkhuniyo tā bhikkhuniyo etadavocuṁ—<br><br>“katthāyyāyo vassaṁvuṭṭhā?<br><br>Kacci ovādo iddho ahosī”ti?<br><br>“Natthayye, tattha bhikkhū;<br><br>kuto ovādo iddho bhavissatī”ti.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma bhikkhuniyo abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ vasissantī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ vasantī”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ vasissanti.<br><br>Netaṁ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyo imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddisantu—	Yā panāti<br><br>yā yādisā …pe…<br><br>bhikkhunīti<br><br>…pe… ayaṁ imasmiṁ atthe adhippetā bhikkhunīti.<br><br>Abhikkhuko nāma āvāso<br><br>na sakkā hoti ovādāya vā saṁvāsāya vā gantuṁ.<br><br>“Vassaṁ vasissāmī”ti senāsanaṁ paññapeti pānīyaṁ paribhojanīyaṁ upaṭṭhapeti pariveṇaṁ sammajjati, āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Saha aruṇuggamanā āpatti pācittiyassa. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::06 Ārāma Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 57	Apavāraṇāsikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī vassaṁvuṭṭhā ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi na pavāreyya diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, pācittiyaṁ.		Garudhamma 4:&nbsp;After completing the rainy season residence the nuns should invite admonition from the communities of both monks and nuns in regard to anything that wasseen, heard, or suspected.	Garudhamma 4: Vassaṁvuṭṭhāya&nbsp;bhikkhuniyā&nbsp;ubhatosaṅghe&nbsp;tīhi&nbsp;ṭhānehi&nbsp;pavāretabbaṁ—diṭṭhena&nbsp;vā&nbsp;sutena&nbsp;vā&nbsp;parisaṅkāya&nbsp;vā.	If a nun who has completed the rainy-season residence does not invite correction from both Sanghas in regard to three things—what has been seen, heard, or suspected—she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_57.mp3]	277	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time a number of nuns who had completed the rainy-season residence in a village monastery went to Sāvatthī.<br><br>The nuns there asked them,<br><br>“Venerables, where did you spend the rains residence?<br><br>Where did you invite the Sangha of monks for correction?”<br><br>“We didn’t invite the Sangha of monks for correction.”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How could nuns who have completed the rains residence not invite the Sangha of monks for correction?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns didn’t do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How could nuns not do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Who has completed the rainy-season residence:<br><br>who has completed the first three or the last three months of the rainy-season residence.<br><br>If she thinks, “I won’t invite correction from both Sanghas in regard to three things—what has been seen, heard, or suspected,” then by the mere fact of abandoning her duty, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if there is an obstacle;<br><br>if she searches, but does not find anyone to invite for correction;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The seventh training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun, alone with a man, without getting permission from the Sangha or a group, has an abscess or a wound situated on the lower part of her body ruptured by him, or split open, washed, anointed, bandaged, or unwrapped by him, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The sixth subchapter on monasteries.	Pācittiyā	Ārāmavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_60.mp3]	282	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>a certain nun was alone with a man, when she had him rupture an abscess growing on the lower part of her body.<br><br>When he tried to rape her,<br><br>she cried out.<br><br>The nuns rushed up and asked her why.<br><br>And she told them what had happened.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized her,<br><br>“How could a nun be alone with a man and have him rupture an abscess growing on the lower part of her body?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that a nun did this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked her …<br><br>“How could a nun do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>The lower part of the body:<br><br>below the navel and above the knees.<br><br>Situated:<br><br>situated there.<br><br>An abscess:<br><br>any kind of abscess.<br><br>A wound:<br><br>any kind of sore.<br><br>Without getting permission:<br><br>without having asked permission.<br><br>The Sangha:<br><br>the Sangha of nuns is what is meant.<br><br>A group:<br><br>several nuns is what is meant.<br><br>A man:<br><br>a human male, not a male spirit, not a male ghost, not a male animal. He understands and is capable of raping.<br><br>With:<br><br>together.<br><br>Alone:<br><br>just the man and the nun.<br><br>If she tells him, “Rupture it,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When it has been ruptured, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she tells him, “Split it open,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When it has been split open, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she tells him, “Wash it,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When it has been washed, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she tells him, “Anoint it,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When it has been anointed, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she tells him, “Bandage it,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When it has been bandaged, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If she tells him, “Unwrap it,” she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When it has been unwrapped, she commits an offense entailing confession.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she gets permission and then has it ruptured, split open, washed, anointed, bandaged, or unwrapped;<br><br>if she has a female companion who understands;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The tenth training rule is finished.<br><br>The sixth subchapter on monasteries is finished. There is no offense:<br><br>if she gives the full admission to a woman who is breastfeeding, but she does not perceive her as such;<br><br>if she gives the full admission to a woman who is not breastfeeding, and she does not perceive her as such;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The second training rule is finished. Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Gabbhinivaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_66.mp3]	289	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns were giving the full admission to married girls who were more than twelve years old, but who had not trained for two years in the six rules.<br><br>They were ignorant and incompetent, and they did not know what was allowable and what was not.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns give the full admission to married girls who are more than twelve years old, but who haven’t trained for two years in the six rules?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …”<br><br>After rebuking them … he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, approval is required for a married girl who is more than twelve years old to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>And the approval is to be given like this.<br><br>After approaching the Sangha of nuns, that married girl who is more than twelve years old should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the nuns. She should then squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘Venerables, I, so-and-so, a married girl who is more than twelve years old, am training under Venerable so-and-so. I ask the Sangha for approval to train for two years in the six rules.’<br><br>And she should ask a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>A competent and capable nun should then inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The married girl so-and-so, who is more than twelve years old and training under Venerable so-and-so, is asking the Sangha for approval to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should give approval to the married girl so-and-so, who is more than twelve years old, to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>The married girl so-and-so, who is more than twelve years old and training under Venerable so-and-so, is asking the Sangha for approval to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>The Sangha gives approval to the married girl so-and-so, who is more than twelve years old, to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>Any nun who approves of giving approval to the married girl so-and-so, who is more than twelve years old, to train in the six rules for two years should remain silent.<br><br>Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>The Sangha has given approval to the married girl so-and-so, who is more than twelve years old, to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I’ll remember it thus.’<br><br>That married girl, who is more than twelve years old, should be told to say this:<br><br>‘I undertake to abstain from killing living beings for two years without transgression. …<br><br>I undertake to abstain from eating at the wrong time for two years without transgression.’”<br><br>Then, after rebuking those nuns in many ways, the Buddha spoke in dispraise of being difficult to support …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Who is more than twelve years old:<br><br>who has reached twelve years of age.<br><br>A married girl:<br><br>one who has gone to the place of a man is what is meant.<br><br>Two years:<br><br>two twelve-month periods.<br><br>Who has not trained:<br><br>the training has not been given to her, or the training has been given to her, but she has failed in it.<br><br>Gives the full admission:<br><br>gives the full ordination.<br><br>If, intending to give the full admission, she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she establishes a monastery zone, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, the preceptor commits an offense entailing confession,<br><br>and the group and the teacher commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she gives the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old and who has trained in the six rules for two years;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The sixth training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṁ gihigataṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṁ vuṭṭhāpenti.<br><br>Tā bālā honti abyattā na jānanti kappiyaṁ vā akappiyaṁ vā.<br><br>Yā tā bhikkhuniyo appicchā …pe… tā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma gihigatā saṅghaṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṁ yācati.<br><br>Saṅgho itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiṁ deti.<br><br>Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya paripuṇṇadvādasavassāya gihigatāya dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhāsammutiyā dānaṁ, sā tuṇhassa;<br><br>yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.<br><br>Dinnā saṅghena itthannāmāya Unique to Bhikkhunī		If a nun gives the full admission to a pregnant woman, she commits an offense entailing confession. There is no offense:<br><br>if she gives the full admission to a woman who is pregnant, but she  does not perceive her as such;<br><br>if she gives the full admission to a woman who is not pregnant, and she does not perceive her as such;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The first training rule is finished. Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::07 Gabbhini Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC 63	Paṭhamasikkhamānasikkhāpadaṁ	Yā pana bhikkhunī dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṁ sikkhamānaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.		Partial Garudhamma 6: A trainee nun who has trained in the six rules for two years should seek ordination from the communities of both monks and nuns.		If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Gabbhinivaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_63.mp3]	286	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns were giving the full admission to trainee nuns who had not trained for two years in the six rules.<br><br>They were ignorant and incompetent, and did not know what was allowable and what was not.<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns give the full admission to trainee nuns who haven’t trained for two years in the six rules?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …”<br><br>After rebuking them …<br><br>he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, approval is required for a trainee nun to train in the six rules for two years.<br><br>And it should be given like this.<br><br>After approaching the Sangha of nuns, that trainee nun should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the nuns. I’ll remember it thus.’<br><br>That trainee nun should then be told to say this:<br><br>‘I undertake to abstain from killing living beings for two years without transgression.<br><br>I undertake to abstain from stealing for two years without transgression.<br><br>I undertake to abstain from sexual activity for two years without transgression.<br><br>I undertake to abstain from lying for two years without transgression.<br><br>I undertake to abstain from alcohol, which causes heedlessness, for two years without transgression.<br><br>I undertake to abstain from eating at the wrong time for two years without transgression.’”<br><br>Then, after rebuking those nuns in many ways, the Buddha spoke in dispraise of being difficult to support …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Two years:<br><br>two twelve-month periods.<br><br>Who has not trained:<br><br>the training has not been given to her, or the training has been given to her, but she has failed in it.<br><br>Gives the full admission:<br><br>gives the full ordination.<br><br>If, intending to give the full admission, she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she establishes a monastery zone, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After the motion, she offense entailing confession,<br><br>and the group and the teacher commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she gives the full admission, she confession.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. Partial Garudhamma 6: A trainee nun who has trained in the six rules for two years should seek ordination from the communities of both monks and nuns.		If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.	Pācittiyā	Gabbhinivaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_64.mp3]	287	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns were giving the full admission to trainee nuns who had trained in the six rules for two years, but who had not been approved by the Sangha.<br><br>The nuns said,<br><br>“Come, trainee nuns, find out about this,” “Give this,” “Bring this,” “There’s need for this,” or “Make this allowable.”<br><br>But they replied,<br><br>“Venerables, we’re not trainee nuns. We’re nuns.”<br><br>The nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns give the full admission to trainee nuns who have trained for two years in the six rules, but who haven’t been approved by the Sangha?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, Sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can nuns do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …”<br><br>After rebuking them …<br><br>he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, approval is required for the full admission of a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules.<br><br>And it should be given like this.<br><br>After approaching the Sangha of nuns, that trainee nun should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder and pay respect at the feet of the nuns. She should then squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:<br><br>‘Venerables, I, the trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules under Venerable so-and-so, ask the Sangha for approval to be fully admitted.’<br><br>And she should ask a second<br><br>and a third time.<br><br>A competent and capable nun should then inform the Sangha:<br><br>‘Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>This trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained under Venerable so-and-so for two years in the six rules, is asking the Sangha for approval to be fully admitted.<br><br>If the Sangha is ready, it should give approval for the trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules, to be fully admitted.<br><br>This is the motion.<br><br>Please, Venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen.<br><br>This trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained under Venerable so-and-so for two years in the six rules, is asking the Sangha for approval to be fully admitted.<br><br>The Sangha gives approval for the trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules, to be fully admitted.<br><br>Any nun who approves of giving approval for the trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules, to be fully admitted should remain silent.<br><br>Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.<br><br>The Sangha has given approval for the trainee nun so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules, to be fully admitted.<br><br>The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I’ll remember it thus.’”<br><br>Then, after rebuking those nuns in many ways, the Buddha spoke in dispraise of being difficult to support …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>A:<br><br>whoever …<br><br>Nun:<br><br>… The nun who has been given the full ordination in unanimity by both Sanghas through a legal procedure consisting of one motion and three announcements that is irreversible and fit to stand—this sort of nun is meant in this case.<br><br>Two years:<br><br>two twelve-month periods.<br><br>Who has trained:<br><br>who has trained in the six rules.<br><br>Who has not been approved:<br><br>approval to be fully admitted has not been given though a legal procedure consisting of one motion and one announcement.<br><br>Gives the full admission:<br><br>gives the full ordination.<br><br>If, intending to give the full admission, she searches for a group, a teacher, a bowl, or a robe, or she establishes a monastery zone, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After the motion, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>After each of the first two announcements, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>When the last announcement is finished, the preceptor commits an offense entailing confession,<br><br>and the group and the teacher commit an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is a legitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as illegitimate, and she gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she perceives it as legitimate, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, but she is unsure of it, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If it is an illegitimate legal procedure, and she perceives it as such, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if she gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained in the six rules for two years and who has been approved by the Sangha;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fourth training rule is finished.
