Pācittiyā	Dhammikavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_165.mp3]	446	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>he allowed itch-covering cloths for the monks.<br><br>Knowing this, the monks from the group of six wore itch covers that were inappropriate in size.<br><br>As they were walking about, they were dragging them along, both in front and behind.<br><br>The monks of few desires complained and criticized those monks,<br><br>“How can the monks from the group of six wear such itch covers?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that you do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“Foolish men, how can you do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	<b>Definitions</b><br><br>An itch-covering cloth:<br><br>it is for the purpose of covering an itch or a boil or a running sore or a carbuncle, below the navel and above the knees.<br><br>Is having made:<br><br>making it himself or having it made, it should be made the right size.<br><br>This is the right size: four standard handspans long and two wide.<br><br>If he makes one or has one made that exceeds that, then for the effort there is an act of wrong conduct.<br><br>When he gets it, it is to be cut down, and he is then to confess an offense entailing confession.<br><br><b>Permutations</b><br><br>If he finishes what he began himself, he commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If he has others finish what he began himself, he commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If he finishes himself what was begun by others, he commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If he has others finish what was begun by others, he commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>If he makes one or has one made for the benefit of someone else, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If he gets one that was made by someone else and then uses it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct. If a nun gives her consent to legitimate legal procedures, and then criticizes them afterwards, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>158. When the Sangha is in the middle of a discussion, if a nun gets up from her seat and leaves without first giving her consent, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>159. If a nun gives out a robe as part of a unanimous Sangha and then criticizes it afterwards, saying, ‘The nuns are diverting the Sangha’s material support according to friendship,’ she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>160. If a nun diverts to an individual material support that she knows was intended for the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>161. If a nun picks up something precious or something regarded as precious, or she has it picked up, except within a monastery or inside a lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>If she picks up something precious or something regarded as precious, or she has it picked up, within a monastery or inside a lodging, she should put it aside with the thought, ‘Whoever owns it will come and get it.’ This is the proper procedure.<br><br>162. If a nun has a needle case made from bone, ivory, or horn, it is to be destroyed, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>163. If a nun is having a new bed or bench made, it is to have legs eight standard fingerbreadths long below the lowest frame. If the legs exceed that, they are to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>164. If a nun has a bed or a bench made upholstered with cotton down, it is to be stripped, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>165. If a nun is having an itch-covering cloth made, it should be made the right size. This is the right size: four standard handspans long and two wide. If it exceeds that, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>166. If a nun has a robe made that is the standard robe size or larger, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>This is the standard robe size: nine standard handspans long and six wide.<br><br>The sixteenth subchapter on legitimate correction.<br><br>Venerables, the one hundred and sixty-six rules on confession have been recited.<br>In regard to this I ask you, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A second time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A third time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>You are pure in this and therefore silent. I will remember it thus.<br><br>The hundred and sixty six offenses entailing confession are finished.	Pācittiyā	Dhammikavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC_157-166.mp3]	451							[sound:ABi_PC_157-166.mp3]	157. {-objecting to a formal act} Should any bhikkhunī, having given consent (by proxy) to a formal act carried out in accordance with the rule, later complain (about the act), it is to be confessed. [79]<br><br>158. {-going without giving consent} Should any bhikkhunī, when deliberation is being carried on in the Saṅgha, get up from her seat and leave without having given consent, it is to be confessed. [80]<br><br>159. {-worn thin} Should any bhikkhunī, (acting as part of) a Saṅgha in concord, give robe-cloth (to an individual bhikkhunī) and later complain, “The bhikkhunīs apportion the Saṅgha’s gains according to friendship,” it is to be confessed. [81]<br><br>160. {-allocation} Should any bhikkhunī knowingly divert to an individual gains that had been allocated for the Saṅgha, it is to be confessed. [82]<br><br>161. {-valuables} Should any bhikkhunī pick up or have (someone) pick up a valuable or what is considered a valuable, except within a monastery or within a dwelling, it is to be confessed. But when a bhikkhunī has picked up or had (someone) pick up a valuable or what is considered a valuable (left) in a monastery or in a dwelling, she is to keep it, (thinking,) “Whoever it belongs to will (come and) fetch it.” This is the proper course here. [84]<br><br>162. {-needle cases} Should any bhikkhunī have a needle case made of bone, ivory, or horn, it is to be broken and confessed. [86]<br><br>163. {-beds and benches} When a bhikkhunī is making a new bed or bench, it is to have legs (at most) eight fingerbreadths long, using Sugata fingerbreadths, not counting the lower edge of the frame. In excess of that it is to be cut down and confessed. [87]<br><br>164. {-upholstered with cotton} Should any bhikkhunī have a bed or bench upholstered with cotton, it (the upholstery) is to be torn off and confessed. [88]<br><br>165. {-skin-eruption cloth} When a bhikkhunī is making a skin-eruption cloth, it is to be made to the measurement. Here the standard is this: four Sugata spans in length, two spans in width. If in excess, it is to be cut down and confessed. [90]<br><br>166. {-“Nanda”} Should any bhikkhunī have a robe made the size of the Sugata robe or larger, it is to be cut down and confessed. Here, the size of the Sugata robe is this: nine spans — using the Sugata span — in length, six spans in width. This is the size of the Sugata’s Sugata robe. [92]<br><br>Part Sixteen: The In-accordance-with-the-Rule Chapter<br><br>Recited, Venerables, are the hundred and sixty-six matters entailing confession. Herein I ask the venerables: Are you pure in this? A second time I ask: Are you pure in this? For the third time I ask: Are you pure in this? The venerables are pure in this; therefore they are silent. So I remember it.<br><br>The section on confession is finished.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::6.Pācittiyā::16 Dhammika Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI PC		Ime kho panāyyāyo, chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā dhammā uddesaṁ āgacchanti.<br><br>1. Yā pana bhikkhunī lasuṇaṁ khādeyya pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>2. Yā pana bhikkhunī sambādhe lomaṁ saṁharāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>3. Talaghātake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>4. Jatumaṭṭhake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>5. Udakasuddhikaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā ādiyamānāya dvaṅgulapabbaparamaṁ ādātabbaṁ. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>6. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa bhuñjantassa pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>7. Yā pana bhikkhunī āmakadhaññaṁ viññatvā vā viññāpetvā vā bhajjitvā vā bhajjāpetvā vā koṭṭetvā vā koṭṭāpetvā vā pacitvā vā pacāpetvā vā bhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>8. Yā pana bhikkhunī uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā saṅkāraṁ vā vighāsaṁ vā tirokuṭṭe vā tiropākāre vā chaḍḍeyya vā chaḍḍāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>9. Yā pana bhikkhunī uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā saṅkāraṁ vā vighāsaṁ vā harite chaḍḍeyya vā chaḍḍāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>10. Yā pana bhikkhunī naccaṁ vā gītaṁ vā vāditaṁ vā dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Lasuṇavaggo paṭhamo.<br><br>11. Yā pana bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>12. Yā pana bhikkhunī paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>13. Yā pana bhikkhunī ajjhokāse purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>14. Yā pana bhikkhunī rathikāya vā byūhe vā siṅghāṭake vā purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā nikaṇṇikaṁ vā jappeyya dutiyikaṁ vā bhikkhuniṁ uyyojeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>15. Yā pana bhikkhunī purebhattaṁ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkameyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>16. Yā pana bhikkhunī pacchābhattaṁ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>17. Yā pana bhikkhunī vikāle kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṁ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>18. Yā pana bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṁ ujjhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>19. Yā pana bhikkhunī attānaṁ vā paraṁ vā nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>20. Yā pana bhikkhunī attānaṁ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>Andhakāravaggo dutiyo.<br><br>21. Yā pana bhikkhunī naggā nahāyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>22. Udakasāṭikaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā kārayamānāya pamāṇikā kāretabbā, tatridaṁ pamāṇaṁ, dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṁ dve vidatthiyo. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>23. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṁ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbeyya, na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṁ kareyya aññatra catūhapañcāhā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>24. Yā pana bhikkhunī pañcāhikaṁ saṅghāṭicāraṁ atikkāmeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>25. Yā pana bhikkhunī cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṁ dhāreyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>26. Yā pana bhikkhunī gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṁ antarāyaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>27. Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikaṁ cīvaravibhaṅgaṁ paṭibāheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>28. Yā pana bhikkhunī agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā samaṇacīvaraṁ dadeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>29. Yā pana bhikkhunī dubbalacīvarapaccāsāya cīvarakālasamayaṁ atikkāmeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>30. Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikaṁ kathinuddhāraṁ paṭibāheyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Naggavaggo tatiyo.<br><br>31. Yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭeyyuṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>32. Yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭeyyuṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>33. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sañcicca aphāsuṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>34. Yā pana bhikkhunī dukkhitaṁ sahajīviniṁ neva upaṭṭhaheyya, na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>35. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā upassayaṁ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍheyya vā nikkaḍḍhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>36. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṁsaṭṭhā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “māyye, saṁsaṭṭhā vihari gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenāpi, viviccāyye, vivekaññeva bhaginiyā saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Evañca pana&nbsp;sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ. No ce paṭinissajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>37. Yā pana bhikkhunī antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>38. Yā pana bhikkhunī tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>39. Yā pana bhikkhunī antovassaṁ cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>40. Yā pana bhikkhunī vassaṁvuṭṭhā cārikaṁ na pakkameyya antamaso chappañcayojanānipi, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Tuvaṭṭavaggo catuttho.<br><br>41. Yā pana bhikkhunī rājāgāraṁ vā cittāgāraṁ vā ārāmaṁ vā uyyānaṁ vā pokkharaṇiṁ vā dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>42. Yā pana bhikkhunī āsandiṁ vā pallaṅkaṁ vā paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>43. Yā pana bhikkhunī suttaṁ kanteyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>44. Yā pana bhikkhunī gihiveyyāvaccaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>45. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā: “ehāyye, imaṁ adhikaraṇaṁ vūpasamehī”ti vuccamānā: “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vūpasameyya, na vūpasamāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>46. Yā pana bhikkhunī agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā dadeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>47. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ sabhikkhukaṁ ārāmaṁ anāpucchā paviseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>52. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuṁ akkoseyya vā paribhāseyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>53. Yā pana bhikkhunī kulamaccharinī assa, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>56. Yā pana bhikkhunī abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ vaseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>57. Yā pana bhikkhunī ovādāya vā saṁvāsāya vā na gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>59. Anvaddhamāsaṁ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā uposathapucchakañca ovādūpasaṅkamanañca. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>60. Yā pana bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṁ gaṇḍaṁ vā rudhitaṁ vā anapaloketvā saṅghaṁ vā gaṇaṁ vā purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā bhedāpeyya vā phālāpeyya vā dhovāpeyya vā ālimpāpeyya vā bandhāpeyya vā mocāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Ārāmavaggo chaṭṭho.<br><br>61. Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnadvādasavassaṁ gihigataṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>66. Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṁ gihigataṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṁ saṅghena asammataṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>68. Yā pana bhikkhunī, “alaṁ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti vuccamānā, “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā sā pacchā khiyyanadhammaṁ āpajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>77. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisasaṁsaṭṭhaṁ kumārakasaṁsaṭṭhaṁ caṇḍiṁ sokāvāsaṁ sikkhamānaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>80. Yā pana bhikkhunī itthālaṅkāraṁ dhāreyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>88. Yā pana bhikkhunī gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>89. Yā pana bhikkhunī anokāsakataṁ bhikkhuṁ pañhaṁ puccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>96. Yā pana bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā gāmaṁ paviseyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.<br><br>97. Sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>98. Omasavāde pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>99. Bhikkhunipesuññe pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>100. Yā pana bhikkhunī anupasampannaṁ padaso dhammaṁ vāceyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>101. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā duṭṭhullaṁ āpattiṁ anupasampannāya āroceyya aññatra bhikkhunisammutiyā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>106. Yā pana bhikkhunī pathaviṁ khaṇeyya vā khaṇāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Musāvādavaggo dasamo.<br><br>107. Bhūtagāmapātabyatāya pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>108. Aññavādake, vihesake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>109. Ujjhāpanake, khiyyanake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>110. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghikaṁ mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā bhisiṁ vā kocchaṁ vā ajjhokāse santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṁ pakkamantī neva uddhareyya, na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṁ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>111. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghike vihāre seyyaṁ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṁ pakkamantī neva uddhareyya, na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṁ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>112. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghike vihāre jānaṁ pubbupagataṁ bhikkhuniṁ anupakhajja seyyaṁ kappeyya, “yassā sambādho bhavissati, sā pakkamissatī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>113. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ kupitā anattamanā saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍheyya vā nikkaḍḍhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>114. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṁ mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>115. Mahallakaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā vihāraṁ kārayamānāya yāva dvārakosā aggaḷaṭṭhapanāya, ālokasandhiparikammāya dvatticchadanassa pariyāyaṁ appaharite ṭhitāya adhiṭṭhātabbaṁ.<br>Tato ce uttari appaharitepi ṭhitā adhiṭṭhaheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>116. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ sappāṇakaṁ udakaṁ tiṇaṁ vā mattikaṁ vā siñceyya vā siñcāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Bhūtagāmavaggo ekādasamo.<br><br>117. Agilānāya bhikkhuniyā eko āvasathapiṇḍo bhuñjitabbo. <br>Tato ce uttari bhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>118. Gaṇabhojane aññatra samayā pācittiyaṁ. Tatthāyaṁ samayo, gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, nāvābhiruhanasamayo, mahāsamayo, samaṇabhattasamayo, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>119. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva kulaṁ upagataṁ pūvehi vā manthehi vā abhihaṭṭhuṁ pavāreyya, ākaṅkhamānāya bhikkhuniyā dvattipattapūrā paṭiggahetabbā. <br>Tato ce uttari paṭiggaṇheyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Dvattipattapūre paṭiggahetvā tato nīharitvā bhikkhunīhi saddhiṁ saṁvibhajitabbaṁ, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>120. Yā pana bhikkhunī vikāle khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>121. Yā pana bhikkhunī sannidhikārakaṁ khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>122. Yā pana bhikkhunī adinnaṁ mukhadvāraṁ āhāraṁ āhareyya aññatra udakadantaponā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>123. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ, “ehāyye, gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti tassā dāpetvā vā adāpetvā vā uyyojeyya, “gacchāyye, na me tayā saddhiṁ kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hoti, ekikāya me kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hotī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>124. Yā pana bhikkhunī sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>125. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisena saddhiṁ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>126. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā raho nisajjaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Bhojanavaggo dvādasamo.<br><br>127. Yā pana bhikkhunī nimantitā sabhattā samānā santiṁ bhikkhuniṁ anāpucchā purebhattaṁ vā pacchābhattaṁ vā kulesu cārittaṁ āpajjeyya aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatthāyaṁ samayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>128. Agilānāya bhikkhuniyā catumāsappaccayapavāraṇā sāditabbā aññatra punapavāraṇāya, aññatra niccapavāraṇāya. Tato ce uttari sādiyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>129. Yā pana bhikkhunī uyyuttaṁ senaṁ dassanāya gaccheyya aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>130. Siyā ca tassā bhikkhuniyā kocideva paccayo senaṁ gamanāya, dirattatirattaṁ tāya bhikkhuniyā senāya vasitabbaṁ. Tato ce uttari vaseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>131. Dirattatirattaṁ ce bhikkhunī senāya vasamānā uyyodhikaṁ vā balaggaṁ vā senābyūhaṁ vā anīkadassanaṁ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>132. Surāmerayapāne pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>133. Aṅgulipatodake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>134. Udake hasadhamme pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>135. Anādariye pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>136. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ bhiṁsāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Cārittavaggo terasamo.<br><br>137. Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā visibbanāpekkhā jotiṁ samādaheyya vā samādahāpeyya vā aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>138. Yā pana bhikkhunī orenaddhamāsaṁ nahāyeyya aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatthāyaṁ samayo “diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhāna”nti “vassānassa paṭhamo māso” iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo, gilānasamayo, kammasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, vātavuṭṭhisamayo, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>139. Navaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā cīvaralābhāya tiṇṇaṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṁ aññataraṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṁ ādātabbaṁ nīlaṁ vā kaddamaṁ vā kāḷasāmaṁ vā. <br>Anādā ce bhikkhunī tiṇṇaṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṁ aññataraṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṁ navaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>140. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇerassa vā sāmaṇeriyā vā sāmaṁ cīvaraṁ vikappetvā apaccuddhāraṇaṁ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>141. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā pattaṁ vā cīvaraṁ vā nisīdanaṁ vā sūcigharaṁ vā kāyabandhanaṁ vā apanidheyya vā apanidhāpeyya vā antamaso hasāpekkhāpi, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>142. Yā pana bhikkhunī sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>143. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ sappāṇakaṁ udakaṁ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>144. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ yathādhammaṁ nihatādhikaraṇaṁ punakammāya ukkoṭeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>145. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ theyyasatthena saddhiṁ saṁvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṁ paṭipajjeyya antamaso gāmantarampi, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>146. Yā pana bhikkhunī evaṁ vadeyya: <br>“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā”ti. <br>Sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: <br>“māyye evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya, <br>anekapariyāyena ayye antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti. <br>Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya. <br>Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ. <br>No ce paṭinissajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Jotivaggo catuddasamo.<br><br>147. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ tathāvādiniyā bhikkhuniyā akaṭānudhammāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissaṭṭhāya saddhiṁ sambhuñjeyya vā, saṁvaseyya vā, saha vā seyyaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>148. Samaṇuddesāpi ce evaṁ vadeyya: <br>“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā”ti. <br>Sā samaṇuddesā bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: <br>“māyye, samaṇuddese evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya, <br>anekapariyāyena ayye, samaṇuddese antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti. <br>Evañca sā samaṇuddesā bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā samaṇuddesā bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: <br>“ajjatagge te, ayye, samaṇuddese na ceva so bhagavā satthā apadisitabbo, <br>yampi caññā samaṇuddesā labhanti bhikkhunīhi saddhiṁ dirattatirattaṁ sahaseyyaṁ, sāpi te natthi, <br>cara pire, vinassā”ti. <br>Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ tathānāsitaṁ samaṇuddesaṁ upalāpeyya vā, upaṭṭhāpeyya vā, sambhuñjeyya vā, saha vā seyyaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>149. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi sahadhammikaṁ vuccamānā evaṁ vadeyya: “na tāvāhaṁ, ayye, etasmiṁ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi, yāva na aññaṁ bhikkhuniṁ byattaṁ vinayadharaṁ paripucchāmī”ti, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Sikkhamānāya, bhikkhuniyo, bhikkhuniyā aññātabbaṁ paripucchitabbaṁ paripañhitabbaṁ, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>150. Yā pana bhikkhunī pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṁ vadeyya: “kiṁ panimehi khuddānukhuddakehi sikkhāpadehi uddiṭṭhehi, yāvadeva kukkuccāya vihesāya vilekhāya saṁvattantī”ti, sikkhāpadavivaṇṇake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>151. Yā pana bhikkhunī anvaddhamāsaṁ pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṁ vadeyya: <br>“idāneva kho ahaṁ jānāmi, ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṁ uddesaṁ āgacchatī”ti, <br>tañce bhikkhuniṁ aññā bhikkhuniyo jāneyyuṁ nisinnapubbaṁ imāya bhikkhuniyā dvattikkhattuṁ pātimokkhe uddissamāne, ko pana vādo bhiyyo,<br>na ca tassā bhikkhuniyā aññāṇakena mutti atthi, yañca tattha āpattiṁ āpannā, tañca yathādhammo kāretabbo, uttari ca assā moho āropetabbo:<br>“tassā te, ayye, alābhā, tassā te dulladdhaṁ, yaṁ tvaṁ pātimokkhe uddissamāne na sādhukaṁ aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi karosī”ti, <br>idaṁ tasmiṁ mohanake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>152. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā kupitā anattamanā pahāraṁ dadeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>153. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā kupitā anattamanā talasattikaṁ uggireyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>154. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṁseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>155. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sañcicca kukkuccaṁ upadaheyya, “itissā muhuttampi aphāsu bhavissatī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>156. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṁ bhaṇḍanajātānaṁ kalahajātānaṁ vivādāpannānaṁ upassutiṁ tiṭṭheyya, “yaṁ imā bhaṇissanti, taṁ sossāmī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Diṭṭhivaggo pannarasamo.<br><br>157. Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikānaṁ kammānaṁ chandaṁ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṁ āpajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>158. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṁ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkameyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>159. Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṁ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṁ āpajjeyya, “yathāsanthutaṁ bhikkhuniyo saṅghikaṁ lābhaṁ pariṇāmentī”ti, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>160. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ saṅghikaṁ lābhaṁ pariṇataṁ puggalassa pariṇāmeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>161. Yā pana bhikkhunī ratanaṁ vā ratanasammataṁ vā aññatra ajjhārāmā vā ajjhāvasathā vā uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Ratanaṁ vā pana bhikkhuniyā ratanasammataṁ vā ajjhārāme vā ajjhāvasathe vā uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipitabbaṁ, “yassa bhavissati, so harissatī”ti, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>162. Yā pana bhikkhunī aṭṭhimayaṁ vā dantamayaṁ vā visāṇamayaṁ vā sūcigharaṁ kārāpeyya, bhedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>163. Navaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā kārayamānāya aṭṭhaṅgulapādakaṁ kāretabbaṁ sugataṅgulena aññatra heṭṭhimāya aṭaniyā. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>164. Yā pana bhikkhunī mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā tūlonaddhaṁ kārāpeyya, uddālanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>165. Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiṁ pana bhikkhuniyā kārayamānāya pamāṇikā kāretabbā, tatridaṁ pamāṇaṁ, dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṁ dve vidatthiyo. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>166. Yā pana bhikkhunī sugatacīvarappamāṇaṁ cīvaraṁ kārāpeyya, atirekaṁ vā, chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatridaṁ sugatassa sugatacīvarappamāṇaṁ, dīghaso nava vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṁ cha vidatthiyo, idaṁ sugatassa sugatacīvarappamāṇanti. <br><br>Dhammikavaggo soḷasamo.<br><br>Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā dhammā. <br>Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>dutiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>tatiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmīti. <br><br>Chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā niṭṭhitā.	Ime kho panāyyāyo, chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā dhammā uddesaṁ āgacchanti.<br><br>1. Yā pana bhikkhunī lasuṇaṁ khādeyya pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>2. Yā pana bhikkhunī sambādhe lomaṁ saṁharāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>3. Talaghātake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>4. Jatumaṭṭhake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>5. Udakasuddhikaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā ādiyamānāya dvaṅgulapabbaparamaṁ ādātabbaṁ. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>6. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa bhuñjantassa pānīyena vā vidhūpanena vā upatiṭṭheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>7. Yā pana bhikkhunī āmakadhaññaṁ viññatvā vā viññāpetvā vā bhajjitvā vā bhajjāpetvā vā koṭṭetvā vā koṭṭāpetvā vā pacitvā vā pacāpetvā vā bhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>8. Yā pana bhikkhunī uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā saṅkāraṁ vā vighāsaṁ vā tirokuṭṭe vā tiropākāre vā chaḍḍeyya vā chaḍḍāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>9. Yā pana bhikkhunī uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā saṅkāraṁ vā vighāsaṁ vā harite chaḍḍeyya vā chaḍḍāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>10. Yā pana bhikkhunī naccaṁ vā gītaṁ vā vāditaṁ vā dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Lasuṇavaggo paṭhamo.<br><br>11. Yā pana bhikkhunī rattandhakāre appadīpe purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>12. Yā pana bhikkhunī paṭicchanne okāse purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>13. Yā pana bhikkhunī ajjhokāse purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>14. Yā pana bhikkhunī rathikāya vā byūhe vā siṅghāṭake vā purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā santiṭṭheyya vā sallapeyya vā nikaṇṇikaṁ vā jappeyya dutiyikaṁ vā bhikkhuniṁ uyyojeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>15. Yā pana bhikkhunī purebhattaṁ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā āsane nisīditvā sāmike anāpucchā pakkameyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>16. Yā pana bhikkhunī pacchābhattaṁ kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā āsane abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>17. Yā pana bhikkhunī vikāle kulāni upasaṅkamitvā sāmike anāpucchā seyyaṁ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>18. Yā pana bhikkhunī duggahitena dūpadhāritena paraṁ ujjhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>19. Yā pana bhikkhunī attānaṁ vā paraṁ vā nirayena vā brahmacariyena vā abhisapeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>20. Yā pana bhikkhunī attānaṁ vadhitvā vadhitvā rodeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>Rattandhakāravaggo dutiyo.<br><br>21. Yā pana bhikkhunī naggā nahāyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>22. Udakasāṭikaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā kārayamānāya pamāṇikā kāretabbā, tatridaṁ pamāṇaṁ, dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṁ dve vidatthiyo. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>23. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṁ visibbetvā vā visibbāpetvā vā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva sibbeyya, na sibbāpanāya ussukkaṁ kareyya aññatra catūhapañcāhā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>24. Yā pana bhikkhunī pañcāhikaṁ saṅghāṭicāraṁ atikkāmeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>25. Yā pana bhikkhunī cīvarasaṅkamanīyaṁ dhāreyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>26. Yā pana bhikkhunī gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṁ antarāyaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>27. Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikaṁ cīvaravibhaṅgaṁ paṭibāheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>28. Yā pana bhikkhunī agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā samaṇacīvaraṁ dadeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>29. Yā pana bhikkhunī dubbalacīvarapaccāsāya cīvarakālasamayaṁ atikkāmeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>30. Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikaṁ kathinuddhāraṁ paṭibāheyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Naggavaggo tatiyo.<br><br>31. Yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekamañce tuvaṭṭeyyuṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>32. Yā pana bhikkhuniyo dve ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā tuvaṭṭeyyuṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>33. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sañcicca aphāsuṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>34. Yā pana bhikkhunī dukkhitaṁ sahajīviniṁ neva upaṭṭhaheyya, na upaṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>35. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā upassayaṁ datvā kupitā anattamanā nikkaḍḍheyya vā nikkaḍḍhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>36. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṁsaṭṭhā vihareyya gahapatinā vā gahapatiputtena vā, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā: “māyye, saṁsaṭṭhā vihari gahapatināpi gahapatiputtenāpi, viviccāyye, vivekaññeva bhaginiyā saṅgho vaṇṇetī”ti. Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya, yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ. No ce paṭinissajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>37. Yā pana bhikkhunī antoraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>38. Yā pana bhikkhunī tiroraṭṭhe sāsaṅkasammate sappaṭibhaye asatthikā cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>39. Yā pana bhikkhunī antovassaṁ cārikaṁ careyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>40. Yā pana bhikkhunī vassaṁvuṭṭhā cārikaṁ na pakkameyya antamaso chappañcayojanānipi, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Tuvaṭṭavaggo catuttho.<br><br>41. Yā pana bhikkhunī rājāgāraṁ vā cittāgāraṁ vā ārāmaṁ vā uyyānaṁ vā pokkharaṇiṁ vā dassanāya gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>42. Yā pana bhikkhunī āsandiṁ vā pallaṅkaṁ vā paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>43. Yā pana bhikkhunī suttaṁ kanteyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>44. Yā pana bhikkhunī gihiveyyāvaccaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>45. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā: “ehāyye, imaṁ adhikaraṇaṁ vūpasamehī”ti vuccamānā: “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vūpasameyya, na vūpasamāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>46. Yā pana bhikkhunī agārikassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā dadeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>47. Yā pana bhikkhunī āvasathacīvaraṁ anissajjetvā paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>48. Yā pana bhikkhunī āvasathaṁ anissajjitvā cārikaṁ pakkameyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>49. Yā pana bhikkhunī tiracchānavijjaṁ pariyāpuṇeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>50. Yā pana bhikkhunī tiracchānavijjaṁ vāceyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Cittāgāravaggo pañcamo.<br><br>51. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ sabhikkhukaṁ ārāmaṁ anāpucchā paviseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>52. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuṁ akkoseyya vā paribhāseyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>53. Yā pana bhikkhunī caṇḍīkatā gaṇaṁ paribhāseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>54. Yā pana bhikkhunī nimantitā vā pavāritā vā khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>55. Yā pana bhikkhunī kulamaccharinī assa, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>56. Yā pana bhikkhunī abhikkhuke āvāse vassaṁ vaseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>57. Yā pana bhikkhunī vassaṁvuṭṭhā ubhatosaṅghe tīhi ṭhānehi na pavāreyya diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>58. Yā pana bhikkhunī ovādāya vā saṁvāsāya vā na gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>59. Anvaddhamāsaṁ bhikkhuniyā bhikkhusaṅghato dve dhammā paccāsīsitabbā uposathapucchakañca ovādūpasaṅkamanañca. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>60. Yā pana bhikkhunī pasākhe jātaṁ gaṇḍaṁ vā rudhitaṁ vā anapaloketvā saṅghaṁ vā gaṇaṁ vā purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā bhedāpeyya vā phālāpeyya vā dhovāpeyya vā ālimpāpeyya vā bandhāpeyya vā mocāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Ārāmavaggo chaṭṭho.<br><br>61. Yā pana bhikkhunī gabbhiniṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>62. Yā pana bhikkhunī pāyantiṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>63. Yā pana bhikkhunī dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṁ sikkhamānaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>64. Yā pana bhikkhunī dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṁ sikkhamānaṁ saṅghena asammataṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>65. Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnadvādasavassaṁ gihigataṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>66. Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṁ gihigataṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>67. Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassaṁ gihigataṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṁ saṅghena asammataṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>68. Yā pana bhikkhunī sahajīviniṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā dve vassāni neva anuggaṇheyya na anuggaṇhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>69. Yā pana bhikkhunī vuṭṭhāpitaṁ pavattiniṁ dve vassāni nānubandheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>70. Yā pana bhikkhunī sahajīviniṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā neva vūpakāseyya na vūpakāsāpeyya antamaso chappañcayojanānipi, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Gabbhinivaggo sattamo.<br><br>71. Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnavīsativassaṁ kumāribhūtaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>72. Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇavīsativassaṁ kumāribhūtaṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu asikkhitasikkhaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>73. Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇavīsativassaṁ kumāribhūtaṁ dve vassāni chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhaṁ saṅghena asammataṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>74. Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnadvādasavassā vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>75. Yā pana bhikkhunī paripuṇṇadvādasavassā saṅghena asammatā vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>76. Yā pana bhikkhunī, “alaṁ tāva te, ayye, vuṭṭhāpitenā”ti vuccamānā, “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā sā pacchā khiyyanadhammaṁ āpajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>77. Yā pana bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṁ, “sace me tvaṁ, ayye, cīvaraṁ dassasi, evāhaṁ taṁ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vuṭṭhāpeyya, na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>78. Yā pana bhikkhunī sikkhamānaṁ, “sace maṁ tvaṁ, ayye, dve vassāni anubandhissasi, evāhaṁ taṁ vuṭṭhāpessāmī”ti vatvā sā pacchā anantarāyikinī neva vuṭṭhāpeyya, na vuṭṭhāpanāya ussukkaṁ kareyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>79. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisasaṁsaṭṭhaṁ kumārakasaṁsaṭṭhaṁ caṇḍiṁ sokāvāsaṁ sikkhamānaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>80. Yā pana bhikkhunī mātāpitūhi vā sāmikena vā ananuññātaṁ sikkhamānaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>81. Yā pana bhikkhunī pārivāsikachandadānena sikkhamānaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>82. Yā pana bhikkhunī anuvassaṁ vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>83. Yā pana bhikkhunī ekaṁ vassaṁ dve vuṭṭhāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Kumāribhūtavaggo aṭṭhamo.<br><br>84. Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā chattupāhanaṁ dhāreyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>85. Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā yānena yāyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>86. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghāṇiṁ dhāreyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>87. Yā pana bhikkhunī itthālaṅkāraṁ dhāreyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>88. Yā pana bhikkhunī gandhavaṇṇakena nahāyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>89. Yā pana bhikkhunī vāsitakena piññākena nahāyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>90. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā ummaddāpeyya vā parimaddāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>91. Yā pana bhikkhunī sikkhamānāya ummaddāpeyya vā parimaddāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>92. Yā pana bhikkhunī sāmaṇeriyā ummaddāpeyya vā parimaddāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>93. Yā pana bhikkhunī gihiniyā ummaddāpeyya vā parimaddāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>94. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa purato anāpucchā āsane nisīdeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>95. Yā pana bhikkhunī anokāsakataṁ bhikkhuṁ pañhaṁ puccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>96. Yā pana bhikkhunī asaṅkaccikā gāmaṁ paviseyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.<br><br>97. Sampajānamusāvāde pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>98. Omasavāde pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>99. Bhikkhunipesuññe pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>100. Yā pana bhikkhunī anupasampannaṁ padaso dhammaṁ vāceyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>101. Yā pana bhikkhunī anupasampannāya uttaridvirattatirattaṁ sahaseyyaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>102. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisena sahaseyyaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>103. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisassa uttarichappañcavācāhi dhammaṁ deseyya aññatra viññunā itthiviggahena, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>104. Yā pana bhikkhunī anupasampannāya uttarimanussadhammaṁ āroceyya, bhūtasmiṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>105. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā duṭṭhullaṁ āpattiṁ anupasampannāya āroceyya aññatra bhikkhunisammutiyā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>106. Yā pana bhikkhunī pathaviṁ khaṇeyya vā khaṇāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Musāvādavaggo dasamo.<br><br>107. Bhūtagāmapātabyatāya pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>108. Aññavādake, vihesake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>109. Ujjhāpanake, khiyyanake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>110. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghikaṁ mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā bhisiṁ vā kocchaṁ vā ajjhokāse santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṁ pakkamantī neva uddhareyya, na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṁ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>111. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghike vihāre seyyaṁ santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṁ pakkamantī neva uddhareyya, na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṁ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>112. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghike vihāre jānaṁ pubbupagataṁ bhikkhuniṁ anupakhajja seyyaṁ kappeyya, “yassā sambādho bhavissati, sā pakkamissatī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>113. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ kupitā anattamanā saṅghikā vihārā nikkaḍḍheyya vā nikkaḍḍhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>114. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghike vihāre uparivehāsakuṭiyā āhaccapādakaṁ mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>115. Mahallakaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā vihāraṁ kārayamānāya yāva dvārakosā aggaḷaṭṭhapanāya, ālokasandhiparikammāya dvatticchadanassa pariyāyaṁ appaharite ṭhitāya adhiṭṭhātabbaṁ.<br>Tato ce uttari appaharitepi ṭhitā adhiṭṭhaheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>116. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ sappāṇakaṁ udakaṁ tiṇaṁ vā mattikaṁ vā siñceyya vā siñcāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Bhūtagāmavaggo ekādasamo.<br><br>117. Agilānāya bhikkhuniyā eko āvasathapiṇḍo bhuñjitabbo. <br>Tato ce uttari bhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>118. Gaṇabhojane aññatra samayā pācittiyaṁ. Tatthāyaṁ samayo, gilānasamayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, nāvābhiruhanasamayo, mahāsamayo, samaṇabhattasamayo, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>119. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva kulaṁ upagataṁ pūvehi vā manthehi vā abhihaṭṭhuṁ pavāreyya, ākaṅkhamānāya bhikkhuniyā dvattipattapūrā paṭiggahetabbā. <br>Tato ce uttari paṭiggaṇheyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Dvattipattapūre paṭiggahetvā tato nīharitvā bhikkhunīhi saddhiṁ saṁvibhajitabbaṁ, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>120. Yā pana bhikkhunī vikāle khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>121. Yā pana bhikkhunī sannidhikārakaṁ khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>122. Yā pana bhikkhunī adinnaṁ mukhadvāraṁ āhāraṁ āhareyya aññatra udakadantaponā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>123. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ, “ehāyye, gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya pavisissāmā”ti tassā dāpetvā vā adāpetvā vā uyyojeyya, “gacchāyye, na me tayā saddhiṁ kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hoti, ekikāya me kathā vā nisajjā vā phāsu hotī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>124. Yā pana bhikkhunī sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>125. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisena saddhiṁ raho paṭicchanne āsane nisajjaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>126. Yā pana bhikkhunī purisena saddhiṁ ekenekā raho nisajjaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Bhojanavaggo dvādasamo.<br><br>127. Yā pana bhikkhunī nimantitā sabhattā samānā santiṁ bhikkhuniṁ anāpucchā purebhattaṁ vā pacchābhattaṁ vā kulesu cārittaṁ āpajjeyya aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatthāyaṁ samayo, cīvaradānasamayo, cīvarakārasamayo, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>128. Agilānāya bhikkhuniyā catumāsappaccayapavāraṇā sāditabbā aññatra punapavāraṇāya, aññatra niccapavāraṇāya. Tato ce uttari sādiyeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>129. Yā pana bhikkhunī uyyuttaṁ senaṁ dassanāya gaccheyya aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>130. Siyā ca tassā bhikkhuniyā kocideva paccayo senaṁ gamanāya, dirattatirattaṁ tāya bhikkhuniyā senāya vasitabbaṁ. Tato ce uttari vaseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>131. Dvirattatirattaṁ ce bhikkhunī senāya vasamānā uyyodhikaṁ vā balaggaṁ vā senābyūhaṁ vā anīkadassanaṁ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>132. Surāmerayapāne pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>133. Aṅgulipatodake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>134. Udake hasadhamme pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>135. Anādariye pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>136. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ bhiṁsāpeyya, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Cārittavaggo terasamo.<br><br>137. Yā pana bhikkhunī agilānā visibbanāpekkhā jotiṁ samādaheyya vā samādahāpeyya vā aññatra tathārūpappaccayā, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>138. Yā pana bhikkhunī orenaddhamāsaṁ nahāyeyya aññatra samayā, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatthāyaṁ samayo “diyaḍḍho māso seso gimhāna”nti “vassānassa paṭhamo māso” iccete aḍḍhateyyamāsā uṇhasamayo, pariḷāhasamayo, gilānasamayo, kammasamayo, addhānagamanasamayo, vātavuṭṭhisamayo, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>139. Navaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā cīvaralābhāya tiṇṇaṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṁ aññataraṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṁ ādātabbaṁ nīlaṁ vā kaddamaṁ vā kāḷasāmaṁ vā. <br>Anādā ce bhikkhunī tiṇṇaṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇānaṁ aññataraṁ dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṁ navaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>140. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā sikkhamānāya vā sāmaṇerassa vā sāmaṇeriyā vā sāmaṁ cīvaraṁ vikappetvā apaccuddhāraṇaṁ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>141. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā pattaṁ vā cīvaraṁ vā nisīdanaṁ vā sūcigharaṁ vā kāyabandhanaṁ vā apanidheyya vā apanidhāpeyya vā antamaso hasāpekkhāpi, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>142. Yā pana bhikkhunī sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>143. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ sappāṇakaṁ udakaṁ paribhuñjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>144. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ yathādhammaṁ nihatādhikaraṇaṁ punakammāya ukkoṭeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>145. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ theyyasatthena saddhiṁ saṁvidhāya ekaddhānamaggaṁ paṭipajjeyya antamaso gāmantarampi, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>146. Yā pana bhikkhunī evaṁ vadeyya:<br>“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā”ti.<br>Sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā:<br>“māyye evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya,<br>anekapariyāyenāyye antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti.<br>Evañca sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi yāvatatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbā tassa paṭinissaggāya.<br>Yāvatatiyañce samanubhāsiyamānā taṁ paṭinissajjeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ.<br>No ce paṭinissajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>Jotivaggo cuddasamo.<br><br>147. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ tathāvādiniyā bhikkhuniyā akaṭānudhammāya taṁ diṭṭhiṁ appaṭinissaṭṭhāya saddhiṁ sambhuñjeyya vā, saṁvaseyya vā, saha vā seyyaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>148. Samaṇuddesāpi ce evaṁ vadeyya:<br>“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā yeme antarāyikā dhammā vuttā bhagavatā, te paṭisevato nālaṁ antarāyāyā”ti.<br>Sā samaṇuddesā bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā:<br>“māyye, samaṇuddese evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya,<br>anekapariyāyenāyye, samaṇuddese antarāyikā dhammā antarāyikā vuttā bhagavatā, alañca pana te paṭisevato antarāyāyā”ti.<br>Evañca sā samaṇuddesā bhikkhunīhi vuccamānā tatheva paggaṇheyya, sā samaṇuddesā bhikkhunīhi evamassa vacanīyā:<br>“ajjatagge te, ayye, samaṇuddese na ceva so bhagavā satthā apadisitabbo,<br>yampi caññā samaṇuddesā labhanti bhikkhunīhi saddhiṁ dirattatirattaṁ sahaseyyaṁ, sāpi te natthi,<br>cara pire, vinassā”ti.<br>Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ tathānāsitaṁ samaṇuddesaṁ upalāpeyya vā, upaṭṭhāpeyya vā, sambhuñjeyya vā, saha vā seyyaṁ kappeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>149. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhunīhi sahadhammikaṁ vuccamānā evaṁ vadeyya: “na tāvāhaṁ, ayye, etasmiṁ sikkhāpade sikkhissāmi, yāva na aññaṁ bhikkhuniṁ byattaṁ vinayadharaṁ paripucchāmī”ti, pācittiyaṁ.<br>Sikkhamānāya, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā aññātabbaṁ paripucchitabbaṁ paripañhitabbaṁ, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>150. Yā pana bhikkhunī pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṁ vadeyya: “kiṁ panimehi khuddānukhuddakehi sikkhāpadehi uddiṭṭhehi, yāvadeva kukkuccāya vihesāya vilekhāya saṁvattantī”ti, sikkhāpadavivaṇṇake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>151. Yā pana bhikkhunī anvaddhamāsaṁ pātimokkhe uddissamāne evaṁ vadeyya:<br>“idāneva kho ahaṁ, ayye, jānāmi ayampi kira dhammo suttāgato suttapariyāpanno anvaddhamāsaṁ uddesaṁ āgacchatī”ti,<br>tañce bhikkhuniṁ aññā bhikkhuniyo jāneyyuṁ nisinnapubbaṁ imāya bhikkhuniyā dvattikkhattuṁ pātimokkhe uddissamāne, ko pana vādo bhiyyo,<br>na ca tassā bhikkhuniyā aññāṇakena mutti atthi, yañca tattha āpattiṁ āpannā, tañca yathādhammo kāretabbo, uttari cassā moho āropetabbo:<br>“tassā te, ayye, alābhā, tassā te dulladdhaṁ, yaṁ tvaṁ pātimokkhe uddissamāne na sādhukaṁ aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi karosī”ti,<br>idaṁ tasmiṁ mohanake pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>152. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā kupitā anattamanā pahāraṁ dadeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>153. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā kupitā anattamanā talasattikaṁ uggireyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>154. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniṁ amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṁseyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>155. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sañcicca kukkuccaṁ upadaheyya, “itissā muhuttampi aphāsu bhavissatī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>156. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhunīnaṁ bhaṇḍanajātānaṁ kalahajātānaṁ vivādāpannānaṁ upassutiṁ tiṭṭheyya, “yaṁ imā bhaṇissanti, taṁ sossāmī”ti etadeva paccayaṁ karitvā anaññaṁ, pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Diṭṭhivaggo pannarasamo.<br><br>157. Yā pana bhikkhunī dhammikānaṁ kammānaṁ chandaṁ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṁ āpajjeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>158. Yā pana bhikkhunī saṅghe vinicchayakathāya vattamānāya chandaṁ adatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkameyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>159. Yā pana bhikkhunī samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṁ datvā pacchā khīyanadhammaṁ āpajjeyya, “yathāsanthutaṁ bhikkhuniyo saṅghikaṁ lābhaṁ pariṇāmentī”ti, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>160. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ saṅghikaṁ lābhaṁ pariṇataṁ puggalassa pariṇāmeyya, pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>161. Yā pana bhikkhunī ratanaṁ vā ratanasammataṁ vā aññatra ajjhārāmā vā ajjhāvasathā vā uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā, pācittiyaṁ. <br>Ratanaṁ vā pana bhikkhuniyā ratanasammataṁ vā ajjhārāme vā ajjhāvasathe vā uggahetvā vā uggahāpetvā vā nikkhipitabbaṁ, “yassa bhavissati, so harissatī”ti, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>162. Yā pana bhikkhunī aṭṭhimayaṁ vā dantamayaṁ vā visāṇamayaṁ vā sūcigharaṁ kārāpeyya, bhedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>163. Navaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā kārayamānāya aṭṭhaṅgulapādakaṁ kāretabbaṁ sugataṅgulena aññatra heṭṭhimāya aṭaniyā. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>164. Yā pana bhikkhunī mañcaṁ vā pīṭhaṁ vā tūlonaddhaṁ kārāpeyya, uddālanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>165. Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiṁ pana bhikkhuniyā kārayamānāya pamāṇikā kāretabbā, tatridaṁ pamāṇaṁ, dīghaso catasso vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṁ dve vidatthiyo. Taṁ atikkāmentiyā chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>166. Yā pana bhikkhunī sugatacīvarappamāṇaṁ cīvaraṁ kārāpeyya, atirekaṁ vā, chedanakaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatridaṁ sugatassa sugatacīvarappamāṇaṁ, dīghaso nava vidatthiyo sugatavidatthiyā, tiriyaṁ cha vidatthiyo, idaṁ sugatassa sugatacīvarappamāṇanti. <br><br>Dhammikavaggo soḷasamo.<br><br>Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, chasaṭṭhisatā pācittiyā dhammā.<br>Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>dutiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>tatiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmīti.<br><br>Pācittiyā niṭṭhitā.			Venerables, these one hundred and sixty-six rules on confession come up for recitation.<br><br>1. If a nun eats garlic, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>2. If a nun removes hair from her private parts, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>3. If a nun slaps her genitals with the palm of her hand, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>4. If a nun uses a dildo, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>5. If a nun is cleaning herself with water, she may insert two finger joints at the most. If she goes further than that, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>6. If, when a monk is eating, a nun attends on him with drinking water or a fan, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>7. If a nun asks for or has someone else ask for raw grain, or she roasts it or has it roasted, or she pounds it or has it pounded, or she cooks it or has it cooked, and she then eats it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>8. If a nun disposes of feces or urine or trash or food scraps over a wall or over an encircling wall, or she has it disposed of in this way, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>9. If a nun disposes of feces or urine or trash or food scraps on cultivated plants, or she has it disposed of in this way, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>10. If a nun goes to see dancing or singing or music, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The first subchapter on garlic.<br><br>11. If, in the dark of the night without a lamp, a nun stands or talks alone with a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>12. If a nun stands or talks alone with a man in a concealed place, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>13. If a nun stands or talks alone with a man out in the open, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>14. If a nun stands or talks alone with a man on a street or in a cul-de-sac or at an intersection, or she whispers in his ear or dismisses her companion nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>15. If a nun visits families before the meal, sits down on a seat, and then departs without informing the owners, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>16. If a nun visits families after the meal, and then sits down or lies down on a seat without asking permission of the owners, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>17. If a nun visits families at the wrong time, puts out bedding without asking permission of the owners, or has it put out, and then sits down or lies down on it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>18. If a nun complains about someone else because of a misunderstanding and a lack of proper reflection, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>19. If a nun curses herself or someone else, referring to hell or the spiritual life, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>20. If a nun cries after repeatedly beating herself, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The second subchapter on darkness.<br><br>21. If a nun bathes naked, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>22. If a nun is having a bathing robe made, it should be made the right size. This is the right size: four standard handspans long and two wide. If it exceeds that, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>23. If a nun, after unstitching a nun’s robe or having it unstitched, neither sews it herself nor makes any effort to have someone else sew it, and there were no obstacles, then, except if it was no more than four or five days, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>24. If a nun does not move her robes for more than five days, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>25. If a nun wears a robe taken on loan, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>26. If a nun creates an obstacle for the community to get robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>27. If a nun blocks a legitimate distribution of robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>28. If a nun gives a monastic robe to a householder or a male wanderer or a female wanderer, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>29. If a nun lets the robe season expire because of an uncertain expectation of robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>30. If a nun blocks a legitimate ending of the robe season, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The third subchapter on nakedness.<br><br>31. If two nuns lie down on the same bed, they commit an offense entailing confession.<br><br>32. If two nuns lie down on the same sheet and under the same cover, they commit an offense entailing confession.<br><br>33. If a nun intentionally makes a nun ill at ease, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>34. If a nun neither nurses a suffering disciple, nor makes any effort to have someone else nurse her, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>35. If a nun gives a dwelling place to a nun, and then, in anger, throws her out or has her thrown out, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>36. If a nun is socializing with a householder or a householder’s offspring, the nuns should correct her like this: ‘Venerable, don’t socialize with householders or householders’ offspring. Be secluded, venerable. The Sangha praises seclusion for the Sisters.’ If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her stop. If she then stops, all is well. If she does not stop, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>37. If a nun goes wandering without a group of travelers where it is considered risky and dangerous within her own country, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>38. If a nun goes wandering without a group of travelers where it is considered risky and dangerous outside her own country, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>39. If a nun goes wandering during the rainy season, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>40. If a nun who has completed the rainy-season residence does not go wandering at least 65 to 80 kilometers, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The fourth subchapter on lying down.<br><br>41. If a nun visits a royal house or a gallery or a park or a garden or a lotus pond, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>42. If a nun uses a high or luxurious couch, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>43. If a nun spins yarn, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>44. If a nun provides services for a householder, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>45. If, when a nun is requested by a nun to resolve a legal issue, she agrees, but then neither resolves it nor makes any effort to resolve it, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>46. If a nun personally gives fresh or cooked food to a householder or a male wanderer or a female wanderer, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>47. If a nun does not relinquish a communal robe, but continues to use it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>48. If a nun goes wandering without relinquishing her lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>49. If a nun studies worldly subjects, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>50. If a nun teaches worldly subjects, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The fifth subchapter on galleries.<br><br>51. If a nun, knowing that there are monks in a monastery, enters it without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>52. If a nun abuses or reviles a monk, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>53. If a furious nun reviles the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>54. If a nun, who has been invited to a meal, refuses an offer to eat more, and then eats fresh or cooked food, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>55. If a nun keeps a family to herself, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>56. If a nun spends the rainy-season residence in a monastery without monks, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>57. If a nun who has completed the rainy-season residence does not invite correction from both Sanghas in regard to three things—what has been seen, heard, or suspected—she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>58. If a nun does not go to the instruction or to a formal meeting of the community, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>59. Every half-month a nun should seek two things from the Sangha of monks: asking it about the observance day and going to it for the instruction. If she lets the half-month pass, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>60. If a nun, alone with a man, without getting permission from the Sangha or a group, has an abscess or a wound situated on the lower part of her body ruptured by him, or split open, washed, anointed, bandaged, or unwrapped by him, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The sixth subchapter on monasteries.<br><br>61. If a nun gives the full admission to a pregnant woman, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>62. If a nun gives the full admission to a woman who is breastfeeding, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>63. If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>64. If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>65. If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is less than twelve years old, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>66. If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>67. If a nun gives the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old and who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>68. If a nun gives the full admission to a disciple, and then, for the next two years, neither guides her nor has her guided, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>69. If a nun does not follow the mentor who gave her the full admission for two years, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>70. If a nun gives the full admission to a disciple, and then neither sends her away nor has her sent away at least 65 to 80 kilometers, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The seventh subchapter on pregnant women.<br><br>71. If a nun gives the full admission to an unmarried woman who is less than twenty years old, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>72. If a nun gives the full admission to an unmarried woman who is more than twenty years old, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>73. If a nun gives the full admission to an unmarried woman who is more than twenty years old and who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>74. If a nun who has less than twelve years of seniority gives the full admission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>75. If a nun who has twelve years of seniority gives the full admission without approval from the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>76. If a nun is told, ‘Venerable, you’ve given enough full admissions for now,’ and she consents, saying, ‘Fine,’ but then criticizes it afterwards, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>77. If a nun tells a trainee nun, ‘If you give me a robe, venerable, I’ll give you the full admission,’ but she then neither gives her the full admission nor makes any effort to have her fully admitted, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>78. If a nun tells a trainee nun, ‘If you follow me for two years, venerable, I’ll give you the full admission,’ but she then neither gives her the full admission nor makes any effort to have her fully admitted, then, if there were no obstacles, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>79. If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who is socializing with men and boys and who is temperamental and difficult to live with, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>80. If a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has not been given permission by her parents or her husband, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>81. If, when a given consent has expired, a nun gives the full admission to a trainee nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>82. If a nun gives full admission every year, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>83. If a nun gives the full admission to two women in the same year, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The eighth subchapter on unmarried women.<br><br>84. If a nun who is not sick uses a sunshade and sandals, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>85. If a nun who is not sick travels in a vehicle, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>86. If a nun wears a hip ornament, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>87. If a nun wears jewelry, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>88. If a nun bathes with scents and colors, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>89. If a nun bathes with scented sesame paste, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>90. If a nun has a nun massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>91. If a nun has a trainee nun massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>92. If a nun has a novice nun massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>93. If a nun has a female householder massage her or rub her, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>94. If a nun sits down on a seat in front of a monk without asking permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>95. If a nun asks a question of a monk who has not given her permission, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>96. If a nun enters an inhabited area without wearing her chest wrap, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The ninth subchapter on sunshades and sandals.<br><br>97. If a nun lies in full awareness, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>98. If a nun speaks abusively, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>99. If a nun engages in malicious talebearing between nuns, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>100. If a nun instructs a person who is not fully ordained to memorize the Teaching, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>101. If a nun lies down more than two or three nights in the same sleeping place as a woman who is not fully ordained, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>102. If a nun lies down in the same sleeping place as a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>103. If a nun gives a teaching of more than five or six sentences to a man, except in the presence of a woman who understands, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>104. If a nun truthfully tells a person who is not fully ordained of a superhuman quality, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>105. If a nun tells a person who is not fully ordained about a nun’s grave offense, except if the nuns have agreed, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>106. If a nun digs the earth or has it dug, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The tenth subchapter on lying.<br><br>107. If a nun destroys a plant, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>108. If a nun speaks evasively or harasses, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>109. If a nun complains or criticizes, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>110. If a nun takes a bed, a bench, a mattress, or a stool belonging to the Sangha and puts it out in the open or has it put out in the open, and she then departs without putting it away, having it put away, or informing anyone, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>111. If a nun puts out bedding in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, or has it put out, and she then departs without putting it away, having it put away, or informing anyone, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>112. If, in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, a nun arranges her sleeping place in a way that encroaches on a nun that she knows arrived there before her, with the intention that anyone who feels crowded will leave, and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>113. If a nun, in anger, throws a nun out of a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, or has her thrown out, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>114. If a nun sits down or lies down on a bed or a bench with detachable legs on an upper story in a dwelling belonging to the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>115. When a nun is building a large dwelling, then standing where there are no cultivated plants, she may apply two or three layers of roofing material, taking it as far as the doorcase and using it for fixing the door and for treating the window openings.<br>If she applies more than that, even if she stands where there are no cultivated plants, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>116. If a nun pours water that she knows contains living beings onto grass or clay, or has it poured, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The eleventh subchapter on plants.<br><br>117. If a nun who is not sick eats more than one almsmeal at a public guesthouse,<br>she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>118. If a nun eats in a group, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>These are the appropriate occasions: she is sick; it is the robe-giving season; it is a time of making robes; she is traveling; she is on a boat; it is a big occasion; it is a meal given by a monastic.<br><br>119. If a nun goes to a family and is invited to take cookies or crackers, she may accept two or three bowlfuls if she wishes.<br>If she accepts more than that, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>If she accepts two or three bowlfuls, she should take it away and share it with the nuns. This is the proper procedure.<br><br>120. If a nun eats fresh or cooked food at the wrong time, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>121. If a nun eats fresh or cooked food that she has stored, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>122. If a nun eats food that has not been given, except for water and tooth cleaners, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>123. If a nun says to a nun, ‘Come, let’s go to the village or town for alms,’ and then, whether she has had food given to her or not, sends her away, saying, ‘Go away, I’m not comfortable talking or sitting with you, but only if I talk and sit by myself,’ and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>124. If a nun sits down intruding on a lustful couple, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>125. If a nun sits down in private on a concealed seat with a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>126. If a nun sits down in private alone with a man, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The twelfth subchapter on eating.<br><br>127. If a nun who has been invited to a meal visits families beforehand or afterwards without informing an available nun, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>These are the appropriate occasions: it is the robe-giving season; it is a time of making robes.<br><br>128. A nun who is not sick may accept an invitation to ask for requisites for four months. If she accepts one beyond that limit, except if it is a further invitation or a permanent invitation, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>129. If a nun goes to see an army, except if there is a suitable reason, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>130. If that nun has a reason for going to the army, she may stay with the army for two or three nights. If she stays longer than that, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>131. If a nun who is staying with an army for two or three nights goes to a battle, a troop review, a massing of the army, or a troop inspection, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>132. If a nun drinks this or that kind of alcoholic drink, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>133. If a nun tickles someone, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>134. If a nun plays in water, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>135. If a nun is disrespectful, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>136. If a nun scares a nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The thirteenth subchapter on visiting.<br><br>137. If a nun who is not sick lights a fire to warm herself, or has one lit, except if there is a suitable reason, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>138. If a nun bathes at intervals of less than a half-month, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>These are the appropriate occasions: it is the two-and-a-half-month period of summer and the fever season, comprising the last one-and-a-half months of summer and the first month of the rainy season; she is sick; she is working; she is traveling; there is wind and rain.<br><br>139. When a nun gets a new robe, she should apply one of three kinds of stains: blue-green, mud color, or dark brown. If<br>a nun uses a new robe without applying any of the three kinds of stains, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>140. If a nun herself assigns the ownership of a robe to a monk, a nun, a trainee nun, a novice monk, or a novice nun, and she then uses it without the other first relinquishing it, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>141. If a nun hides a nun’s bowl, robe, sitting mat, needle case, or belt, or she has it hidden, even just for a laugh, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>142. If a nun intentionally kills a living being, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>143. If a nun uses water that she knows contains living beings, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>144. If a nun reopens a legal issue that she knows has been legitimately settled, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>145. If a nun knowingly travels by arrangement with a group of thieves, even just to the next inhabited area, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>146. If a nun says,<br>‘As I understand the Buddha’s Teaching, the things he calls obstacles are unable to obstruct one who indulges in them,’<br>then the nuns should correct her like this:<br>‘No, venerable, don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for it’s not good to misrepresent the Buddha. The Buddha would never say such a thing.<br>In many discourses the Buddha has declared the obstacles to be obstructive and how they obstruct one who indulges in them.’<br>If that nun continues as before, the nuns should press her up to three times to make her give up that view.<br>If she then gives it up, all is well.<br>If she does not, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The fourteenth subchapter on fire.<br><br>147. If a nun lives, does formal meetings, or shares a sleeping place with a nun who she knows is saying such things, who has not made amends according to the rule, and who has not given up that view, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>148. Also if a novice nun says,<br>‘As I understand the Buddha’s Teaching, the things he calls obstacles are unable to obstruct one who indulges in them,’<br>then the nuns should correct her like this:<br>‘No, don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for it’s not good to misrepresent the Buddha. The Buddha would never say such a thing.<br>In many discourses the Buddha has declared the obstacles to be obstructive and how they obstruct one who indulges in them.’<br>If that novice nun continues as before, she should be told:<br>‘From today on you may not refer to the Buddha as your teacher.<br>And, unlike other novices, you can no longer share a sleeping place with the nuns for two or three nights.<br>Go! Away with you!’<br>If a nun befriends that novice nun, or she is attended on by her, lives with her, or shares a sleeping place with her, even though she knows that she has been expelled in this way, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>149. If a nun, when legitimately corrected by the nuns, says, ‘I won’t practice this training rule until I’ve questioned a nun who is an expert on the Monastic Law,’ she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>A nun who is training should understand, should question, should enquire. This is the proper procedure.<br><br>150. When the Monastic Code is being recited, if a nun says, ‘What’s the point of reciting these minor training rules, when they just lead to anxiety, oppression, and annoyance?’ then in disparaging the training rules, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>151. During the half-monthly recitation of the Monastic Code, a nun might say,<br>‘Just now did I find out that this rule too has come down in the Monastic Code, is included in the Monastic Code, and comes up for recitation every half-month.’<br>If other nuns know that that nun has previously sat through at least two or three recitations of the Monastic Code, then that nun<br>is not let off because of ignorance, and she is to be dealt with according to the rule. Further, she should be charged with deception:<br>‘It’s a loss for you that you don’t pay proper attention during the recitation of the Monastic Code.’<br>And for the act of deception, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>152. If a nun hits a nun in anger, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>153. If a nun raises a hand in anger against a nun, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>154. If a nun groundlessly charges a nun with an offense entailing suspension, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>155. If a nun intentionally makes a nun anxious, thinking, ‘In this way she will be ill at ease at least for a moment,’ and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>156. If a nun eavesdrops on nuns who are arguing and disputing, thinking, ‘I’ll hear what they say,’ and she does so only for this reason and no other, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>The fifteenth subchapter on view.<br><br>157. If a nun gives her consent to legitimate legal procedures, and then criticizes them afterwards, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>158. When the Sangha is in the middle of a discussion, if a nun gets up from her seat and leaves without first giving her consent, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>159. If a nun gives out a robe as part of a unanimous Sangha and then criticizes it afterwards, saying, ‘The nuns are diverting the Sangha’s material support according to friendship,’ she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>160. If a nun diverts to an individual material support that she knows was intended for the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>161. If a nun picks up something precious or something regarded as precious, or she has it picked up, except within a monastery or inside a lodging, she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>If she picks up something precious or something regarded as precious, or she has it picked up, within a monastery or inside a lodging, she should put it aside with the thought, ‘Whoever owns it will come and get it.’ This is the proper procedure.<br><br>162. If a nun has a needle case made from bone, ivory, or horn, it is to be destroyed, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>163. If a nun is having a new bed or bench made, it is to have legs eight standard fingerbreadths long below the lowest frame. If the legs exceed that, they are to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>164. If a nun has a bed or a bench made upholstered with cotton down, it is to be stripped, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>165. If a nun is having an itch-covering cloth made, it should be made the right size. This is the right size: four standard handspans long and two wide. If it exceeds that, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br><br>166. If a nun has a robe made that is the standard robe size or larger, it is to be cut down, and she commits an offense entailing confession.<br>This is the standard robe size: nine standard handspans long and six wide.<br><br>The sixteenth subchapter on legitimate correction.<br><br>Venerables, the one hundred and sixty-six rules on confession have been recited.<br>In regard to this I ask you, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A second time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A third time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>You are pure in this and therefore silent. I will remember it thus.<br><br>The hundred and sixty six offenses entailing confession are finished.	Pācittiyā	Dhammikavaggo	[sound:Bi_PC.mp3]	452							[sound:ABi_PC.mp3]	Now, Venerables, these hundred and sixty-six matters entailing confession come up for recitation.<br><br>1. {The precept about -garlic} Should any bhikkhunī eat garlic, it is to be confessed. [See Cv.V.34.1]<br><br>2. {-hair on the body} Should any bhikkhunī have the hair in the tight places (armpits and pelvic areas) removed, it is to be confessed. [See Cv.V.27.4]<br><br>3. {-slapping} (Genital) slapping (even to the extent of consenting to a blow with a lotus-leaf) is to be confessed.<br><br>4. {-a dildo} (The insertion of) a dildo is to be confessed.<br><br>5. {-water ablution} When a bhikkhunī is giving herself an ablution, it is to be given only to the depth of two finger joints (and using no more than two fingers). Beyond that, it is to be confessed.
