If a nun takes, has someone else take, or consents to gold, silver, or money being deposited for her, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>22. If a nun engages in various kinds of trades involving money, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>23. If a nun engages in various kinds of barter, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>24. If a nun exchanges an almsbowl with fewer than five mends for a new almsbowl, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br>That nun should relinquish that almsbowl to a gathering of nuns.<br>She should then be given the last almsbowl belonging to that gathering:<br>‘Nun, this bowl is yours. Keep it until it breaks.’ This is the proper procedure.<br><br>25. After being received, the tonics allowable for sick nuns—that is, ghee, butter, oil, honey, and syrup—should be used from storage for at most seven days.<br>If one uses them longer than that, one commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>26. If a nun herself gives a robe to a nun, but then, in anger, takes it back or has it taken back, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>27. If a nun herself asks for thread, and then has weavers weave her robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>28. If a male or female householder is having robe-cloth woven by weavers for an unrelated nun and, without first being invited, that nun goes to those weavers and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘This robe-cloth that you are weaving for me, make it long and wide; make it closely woven, well-woven, well-stretched, well-scraped, and well-combed, and perhaps I will even give you a small gift,’ then, in saying that and afterwards giving them a small gift, even a bit of almsfood, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>29. When there are ten days left to the Kattika full moon that ends the first rainy-season residence and a haste-cloth is given to a nun, she may receive it if she regards it as urgent. She may then store it until the end of the robe season.<br>If she stores it beyond that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>30. If a nun diverts to herself material support that she knows was intended for the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>The third subchapter on gold and silver.<br><br>Venerables, the thirty rules on relinquishment and confession have been recited.<br>In regard to this I ask you, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A second time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A third time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>You are pure in this and therefore silent. I will remember it thus.<br><br>The thirty&nbsp;offenses entailing relinquishment and confession are finished.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Jātarūpavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP_21-30.mp3]	204							[sound:ABi_NP_21-30.mp3]	21. {-money} Should any bhikkhunī take gold and silver, or have it taken, or consent to its being deposited (near her), it is to be forfeited and confessed. [18]<br><br>22. {-monetary exchange} Should any bhikkhunī engage in various types of monetary exchange, it (the income) is to be forfeited and confessed. [19]<br><br>23. {-bartering} Should any bhikkhunī engage in various types of trade, (the article) is to be forfeited and confessed. [20]<br><br>24. {-less than five mends} Should a bhikkhunī with an alms bowl having less than five mends exchange it for another new bowl, it is to be forfeited and confessed. The bowl is to be forfeited by the bhikkhunī to the assembly of bhikkhunīs. That assembly of bhikkhunīs’ final bowl should be presented to the bhikkhunī (saying): “This, bhikkhuni, is your bowl. It is to be kept until broken.” This is the proper procedure here. [22]<br><br>25. {-medicine} There are these tonics to be taken by sick bhikkhunīs: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, sugar / molasses. Having been received, they are to be used from storage seven days at most. Beyond that, they are to be forfeited and confessed. [23]<br><br>26. {-snatching robes} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself given a robe-cloth to a bhikkhunī, and then being angered and displeased, snatch it back or have it snatched back, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [25]<br><br>27. {-requesting thread} Should any bhikkhunī, having requested thread, have a robe woven by weavers, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [26]<br><br>28. {-greater about weavers} In case a man or woman householder unrelated to a bhikkhunī has weavers weave robe-cloth for her, and if the bhikkhunī without previous invitation should approach the weavers and make stipulations for the cloth, saying: “This cloth, friends, is to be woven for me. Make it long, broad, tightly woven, well woven, well spread, well scraped, well smoothed, and perhaps I may gave you a little something.” And should the bhikkhunī, having said that, give them a little something, even a bit of alms food, it (the cloth) is to be forfeited and confessed. [27]<br><br>29. {-special robes} Ten days prior to the third-month Kattika full moon, should robe-cloth offered in urgency accrue to a bhikkhunī, she is to accept it if she regards it as offered in urgency. Once she has accepted it, she may keep it throughout the robe-season. Beyond that, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [28]<br><br>30. {-allocation} Should any bhikkhunī knowingly divert to herself gains that had been intended for a Saṅgha, they are to be forfeited and confessed. [30]<br><br>Part Three: The Gold and Silver Chapter<br><br>Recited, Venerables, are the thirty matters entailing confession with forfeiture. Herein I ask the venerables: Are you pure in this? A second time I ask: Are you pure in this? A third time I ask: Are you pure in this? The venerables are pure in this; therefore they are silent. So I remember it.<br><br>The section on confession with forfeiture is finished.	
Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::5.Nissaggiya pācittiyā::3 Jātarūpa Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI NP		Ime kho panāyyāyo tiṁsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā uddesaṁ āgacchanti.<br><br>1. Yā pana bhikkhunī pattasannicayaṁ kareyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>2. Yā pana bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṁ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>3. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā saddhiṁ cīvaraṁ parivattetvā sā pacchā evaṁ vadeyya: “handāyye, tuyhaṁ cīvaraṁ, āhara metaṁ cīvaraṁ, yaṁ tuyhaṁ tuyhamevetaṁ, yaṁ mayhaṁ mayhamevetaṁ, āhara metaṁ cīvaraṁ, sakaṁ paccāharā”ti acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>4. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṁ viññāpetvā aññaṁ viññāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>5. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>6. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>7. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>8. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>9. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>10. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Pattavaggo paṭhamo.<br><br>11. Garupāvuraṇaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā cetāpentiyā catukkaṁsaparamaṁ cetāpetabbaṁ. Tato ce uttari cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>12. Lahupāvuraṇaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā cetāpentiyā aḍḍhateyyakaṁsaparamaṁ cetāpetabbaṁ. Tato ce uttari cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>13. Niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṁ bhikkhuniyā ubbhatasmiṁ kathine dasāhaparamaṁ atirekacīvaraṁ dhāretabbaṁ. <br>Taṁ atikkāmentiyā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>14. Niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṁ bhikkhuniyā ubbhatasmiṁ kathine ekarattampi ce bhikkhunī ticīvarena vippavaseyya, aññatra bhikkhunisammutiyā nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>15. Niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṁ bhikkhuniyā ubbhatasmiṁ kathine bhikkhuniyā paneva akālacīvaraṁ uppajjeyya, ākaṅkhamānāya bhikkhuniyā taṁ paṭiggahetabbaṁ, paṭiggahetvā khippameva kāretabbaṁ, no cassa pāripūri, māsaparamaṁ tāya bhikkhuniyā taṁ cīvaraṁ nikkhipitabbaṁ ūnassa pāripūriyā satiyā paccāsāya. Tato ce uttari nikkhipeyya satiyāpi paccāsāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>16. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññātakaṁ gahapatiṁ vā gahapatāniṁ vā cīvaraṁ viññāpeyya aññatra samayā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatthāyaṁ samayo acchinnacīvarā vā hoti bhikkhunī, naṭṭhacīvarā vā, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>17. Tañce aññātako gahapati vā gahapatānī vā bahūhi cīvarehi abhihaṭṭhuṁ pavāreyya, santaruttaraparamaṁ tāya bhikkhuniyā tato cīvaraṁ sāditabbaṁ. <br>Tato ce uttari sādiyeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>18. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa aññātakassa gahapatissa vā gahapatāniyā vā cīvaracetāpannaṁ upakkhaṭaṁ hoti: “iminā cīvaracetāpannena cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarena acchādessāmī”ti. Tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “sādhu vata, maṁ āyasmā iminā cīvaracetāpannena evarūpaṁ vā evarūpaṁ vā cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā acchādehī”ti kalyāṇakamyataṁ upādāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>19. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa ubhinnaṁ aññātakānaṁ gahapatīnaṁ vā gahapatānīnaṁ vā paccekacīvaracetāpannāni upakkhaṭāni honti: “imehi mayaṁ paccekacīvaracetāpannehi paccekacīvarāni cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarehi acchādessāmā”ti. Tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “sādhu vata maṁ āyasmanto imehi paccekacīvaracetāpannehi evarūpaṁ vā evarūpaṁ vā cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā acchādetha ubhova santā ekenā”ti kalyāṇakamyataṁ upādāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>20. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa rājā vā rājabhoggo vā brāhmaṇo vā gahapatiko vā dūtena cīvaracetāpannaṁ pahiṇeyya: “iminā cīvaracetāpannena cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarena acchādehī”ti. So ce dūto taṁ bhikkhuniṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya: “idaṁ kho, ayye, ayyaṁ uddissa cīvaracetāpannaṁ ābhataṁ, paṭiggaṇhātu āyyā cīvaracetāpanna”nti. Tāya bhikkhuniyā so dūto evamassa vacanīyo: “na kho mayaṁ, āvuso, cīvaracetāpannaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma, cīvarañca kho mayaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma kālena kappiya”nti. So ce dūto taṁ bhikkhuniṁ evaṁ vadeyya: “atthi panāyyāya, kāci veyyāvaccakarā”ti, cīvaratthikāya, bhikkhuniyo, bhikkhuniyā veyyāvaccakarā&nbsp;niddisitabbā&nbsp;ārāmikā&nbsp;vā upāsikā&nbsp;vā: “esā&nbsp;kho, āvuso, bhikkhunīnaṁ veyyāvaccakarā”ti. So ce dūto taṁ veyyāvaccakaraṁ saññāpetvā taṁ bhikkhuniṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya: “yaṁ kho, ayye, ayyā veyyāvaccakaraṁ niddisi, saññattā sā&nbsp;mayā, upasaṅkamatāyyā kālena, cīvarena taṁ acchādessatī”ti. Cīvaratthikāya, bhikkhuniyo, bhikkhuniyā veyyāvaccakarā&nbsp;upasaṅkamitvā dvattikkhattuṁ codetabbā&nbsp;sāretabbā: “attho me, āvuso, cīvarenā”ti, dvattikkhattuṁ codayamānā sārayamānā taṁ cīvaraṁ abhinipphādeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, no ce abhinipphādeyya, catukkhattuṁ pañcakkhattuṁ chakkhattuparamaṁ tuṇhībhūtāya uddissa ṭhātabbaṁ, catukkhattuṁ pañcakkhattuṁ chakkhattuparamaṁ tuṇhībhūtā uddissa tiṭṭhamānā taṁ cīvaraṁ abhinipphādeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ. Tato ce uttari vāyamamānā taṁ cīvaraṁ abhinipphādeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. No ce abhinipphādeyya, yatassā cīvaracetāpannaṁ ābhataṁ, tattha sāmaṁ vā gantabbaṁ, dūto vā pāhetabbo: “yaṁ kho tumhe āyasmanto bhikkhuniṁ uddissa cīvaracetāpannaṁ pahiṇittha, na taṁ tassā bhikkhuniyā kiñci atthaṁ anubhoti, yuñjantāyasmanto sakaṁ, mā vo sakaṁ vinassā”ti, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci. <br><br>Cīvaravaggo dutiyo.<br><br>21. Yā pana bhikkhunī jātarūparajataṁ uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā upanikkhittaṁ vā sādiyeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>22. Yā pana bhikkhunī nānappakārakaṁ rūpiyasaṁvohāraṁ samāpajjeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>23. Yā pana bhikkhunī nānappakārakaṁ kayavikkayaṁ samāpajjeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>24. Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnapañcabandhanena pattena aññaṁ navaṁ pattaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tāya bhikkhuniyā so patto bhikkhuniparisāya nissajjitabbo, <br>yo ca tassā bhikkhuniparisāya pattapariyanto, so tassā bhikkhuniyā padātabbo: <br>“ayaṁ te bhikkhuni patto yāvabhedanāya dhāretabbo”ti, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>25. Yāni kho pana tāni gilānānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ paṭisāyanīyāni bhesajjāni, seyyathidaṁ: sappi navanītaṁ telaṁ madhu phāṇitaṁ, tāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaparamaṁ sannidhikārakaṁ paribhuñjitabbāni. <br>Taṁ atikkāmentiyā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>26. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sāmaṁ cīvaraṁ datvā kupitā anattamanā acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>27. Yā pana bhikkhunī sāmaṁ suttaṁ viññāpetvā tantavāyehi cīvaraṁ vāyāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>28. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa aññātako gahapati vā gahapatānī vā tantavāyehi cīvaraṁ vāyāpeyya, tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā tantavāye upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “idaṁ kho āvuso cīvaraṁ maṁ uddissa viyyati, āyatañca karotha, vitthatañca appitañca suvītañca suppavāyitañca suvilekhitañca suvitacchitañca karotha, appeva nāma mayampi āyasmantānaṁ kiñcimattaṁ anupadajjeyyāmā”ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī vatvā kiñcimattaṁ anupadajjeyya antamaso piṇḍapātamattampi, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>29. Dasāhānāgataṁ kattikatemāsikapuṇṇamaṁ bhikkhuniyā paneva accekacīvaraṁ uppajjeyya, accekaṁ maññamānāya bhikkhuniyā paṭiggahetabbaṁ, paṭiggahetvā yāva cīvarakālasamayaṁ nikkhipitabbaṁ. <br>Tato ce uttari nikkhipeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>30. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ saṅghikaṁ lābhaṁ pariṇataṁ attano pariṇāmeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Jātarūpavaggo&nbsp;tatiyo.<br><br>Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, tiṁsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā. <br>Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>dutiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>tatiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā, <br>parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmīti. <br><br>Tiṁsa&nbsp;nissaggiyapācittiyā niṭṭhitā.	Ime kho panāyyāyo tiṁsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā uddesaṁ āgacchanti.<br><br>1. Yā pana bhikkhunī pattasannicayaṁ kareyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>2. Yā pana bhikkhunī akālacīvaraṁ “kālacīvara”nti adhiṭṭhahitvā bhājāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>3. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā saddhiṁ cīvaraṁ parivattetvā sā pacchā evaṁ vadeyya: “handāyye, tuyhaṁ cīvaraṁ, āhara metaṁ cīvaraṁ, yaṁ tuyhaṁ tuyhamevetaṁ, yaṁ mayhaṁ mayhamevetaṁ, āhara metaṁ cīvaraṁ, sakaṁ paccāharā”ti acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>4. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṁ viññāpetvā aññaṁ viññāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>5. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññaṁ cetāpetvā aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>6. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>7. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena saṅghikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>8. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>9. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena mahājanikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>10. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññadatthikena parikkhārena aññuddisikena puggalikena saññācikena aññaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Pattavaggo paṭhamo.<br><br>11. Garupāvuraṇaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā cetāpentiyā catukkaṁsaparamaṁ cetāpetabbaṁ. Tato ce uttari cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>12. Lahupāvuraṇaṁ pana bhikkhuniyā cetāpentiyā aḍḍhateyyakaṁsaparamaṁ cetāpetabbaṁ. Tato ce uttari cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>13. Niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṁ bhikkhuniyā ubbhatasmiṁ kathine dasāhaparamaṁ atirekacīvaraṁ dhāretabbaṁ. <br>Taṁ atikkāmentiyā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>14. Niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṁ bhikkhuniyā ubbhatasmiṁ kathine ekarattampi ce bhikkhunī ticīvarena vippavaseyya, aññatra bhikkhunisammutiyā nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>15. Niṭṭhitacīvarasmiṁ bhikkhuniyā ubbhatasmiṁ kathine bhikkhuniyā paneva akālacīvaraṁ uppajjeyya, ākaṅkhamānāya bhikkhuniyā paṭiggahetabbaṁ, paṭiggahetvā khippameva kāretabbaṁ, no cassa pāripūri, māsaparamaṁ tāya bhikkhuniyā taṁ cīvaraṁ nikkhipitabbaṁ ūnassa pāripūriyā satiyā paccāsāya. Tato ce uttari nikkhipeyya satiyāpi paccāsāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>16. Yā pana bhikkhunī aññātakaṁ gahapatiṁ vā gahapatāniṁ vā cīvaraṁ viññāpeyya aññatra samayā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tatthāyaṁ samayo acchinnacīvarā vā hoti bhikkhunī, naṭṭhacīvarā vā, ayaṁ tattha samayo.<br><br>17. Tañce aññātako gahapati vā gahapatānī vā bahūhi cīvarehi abhihaṭṭhuṁ pavāreyya, santaruttaraparamaṁ tāya bhikkhuniyā tato cīvaraṁ sāditabbaṁ. <br>Tato ce uttari sādiyeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>18. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa aññātakassa gahapatissa vā gahapatāniyā vā cīvaracetāpannaṁ upakkhaṭaṁ hoti: “iminā cīvaracetāpannena cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarena acchādessāmī”ti. Tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “sādhu vata, maṁ āyasmā iminā cīvaracetāpannena evarūpaṁ vā evarūpaṁ vā cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā acchādehī”ti kalyāṇakamyataṁ upādāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>19. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa ubhinnaṁ aññātakānaṁ gahapatīnaṁ vā gahapatānīnaṁ vā paccekacīvaracetāpannāni upakkhaṭāni honti: “imehi mayaṁ paccekacīvaracetāpannehi paccekacīvarāni cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarehi acchādessāmā”ti. Tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “sādhu vata maṁ āyasmanto imehi paccekacīvaracetāpannehi evarūpaṁ vā evarūpaṁ vā cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā acchādetha ubhova santā ekenā”ti kalyāṇakamyataṁ upādāya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>20. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa rājā vā rājabhoggo vā brāhmaṇo vā gahapatiko vā dūtena cīvaracetāpannaṁ pahiṇeyya: “iminā cīvaracetāpannena cīvaraṁ cetāpetvā itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ cīvarena acchādehī”ti. So ce dūto taṁ bhikkhuniṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya: “idaṁ kho, ayye, ayyaṁ uddissa cīvaracetāpannaṁ ābhataṁ, paṭiggaṇhātāyyā cīvaracetāpanna”nti. Tāya bhikkhuniyā so dūto evamassa vacanīyo: “na kho mayaṁ, āvuso, cīvaracetāpannaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma, cīvarañca kho mayaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma kālena kappiya”nti. So ce dūto taṁ bhikkhuniṁ evaṁ vadeyya: “atthi panāyyāya, koci veyyāvaccakaro”ti, cīvaratthikāya, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā veyyāvaccakaro niddisitabbo ārāmiko vā upāsako vā: “eso kho, āvuso, bhikkhunīnaṁ veyyāvaccakaro”ti. So ce dūto taṁ veyyāvaccakaraṁ saññāpetvā taṁ bhikkhuniṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya: “yaṁ kho, ayye, ayyā veyyāvaccakaraṁ niddisi, saññatto so mayā, upasaṅkamatāyyā kālena, cīvarena taṁ acchādessatī”ti. Cīvaratthikāya, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā veyyāvaccakaro upasaṅkamitvā dvattikkhattuṁ codetabbo sāretabbo: “attho me, āvuso, cīvarenā”ti, dvattikkhattuṁ codayamānā sārayamānā taṁ cīvaraṁ abhinipphādeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, no ce abhinipphādeyya, catukkhattuṁ pañcakkhattuṁ chakkhattuparamaṁ tuṇhībhūtāya uddissa ṭhātabbaṁ, catukkhattuṁ pañcakkhattuṁ chakkhattuparamaṁ tuṇhībhūtā uddissa tiṭṭhamānā taṁ cīvaraṁ abhinipphādeyya, iccetaṁ kusalaṁ. Tato ce uttari vāyamamānā taṁ cīvaraṁ abhinipphādeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. No ce abhinipphādeyya, yatassā cīvaracetāpannaṁ ābhataṁ, tattha sāmaṁ vā gantabbaṁ, dūto vā pāhetabbo: “yaṁ kho tumhe āyasmanto bhikkhuniṁ uddissa cīvaracetāpannaṁ pahiṇittha, na taṁ tassā bhikkhuniyā kiñci atthaṁ anubhoti, yuñjantāyasmanto sakaṁ, mā vo sakaṁ vinassā”ti, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>Cīvaravaggo dutiyo.<br><br>21. Yā pana bhikkhunī jātarūparajataṁ uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā upanikkhittaṁ vā sādiyeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>22. Yā pana bhikkhunī nānappakārakaṁ rūpiyasaṁvohāraṁ samāpajjeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>23. Yā pana bhikkhunī nānappakārakaṁ kayavikkayaṁ samāpajjeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>24. Yā pana bhikkhunī ūnapañcabandhanena pattena aññaṁ navaṁ pattaṁ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br>Tāya bhikkhuniyā so patto bhikkhuniparisāya nissajjitabbo, <br>yo ca tassā bhikkhuniparisāya pattapariyanto, so tassā bhikkhuniyā padātabbo: <br>“ayaṁ te bhikkhuni patto yāvabhedanāya dhāretabbo”ti, ayaṁ tattha sāmīci.<br><br>25. Yāni kho pana tāni gilānānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ paṭisāyanīyāni bhesajjāni, seyyathidaṁ: sappi navanītaṁ telaṁ madhu phāṇitaṁ, tāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaparamaṁ sannidhikārakaṁ paribhuñjitabbāni. <br>Taṁ atikkāmentiyā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>26. Yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuniyā sāmaṁ cīvaraṁ datvā kupitā anattamanā acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>27. Yā pana bhikkhunī sāmaṁ suttaṁ viññāpetvā tantavāyehi cīvaraṁ vāyāpeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>28. Bhikkhuniṁ paneva uddissa aññātako gahapati vā gahapatānī vā tantavāyehi cīvaraṁ vāyāpeyya, tatra cesā bhikkhunī pubbe appavāritā tantavāye upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṁ āpajjeyya: “idaṁ kho āvuso cīvaraṁ maṁ uddissa viyyati, āyatañca karotha, vitthatañca appitañca suvītañca suppavāyitañca suvilekhitañca suvitacchitañca karotha, appeva nāma mayampi āyasmantānaṁ kiñcimattaṁ anupadajjeyyāmā”ti, evañca sā bhikkhunī vatvā kiñcimattaṁ anupadajjeyya antamaso piṇḍapātamattampi, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>29. Dasāhānāgataṁ kattikatemāsikapuṇṇamaṁ bhikkhuniyā paneva accekacīvaraṁ uppajjeyya, accekaṁ maññamānāya bhikkhuniyā paṭiggahetabbaṁ, paṭiggahetvā yāva cīvarakālasamayaṁ nikkhipitabbaṁ. <br>Tato ce uttari nikkhipeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ.<br><br>30. Yā pana bhikkhunī jānaṁ saṅghikaṁ lābhaṁ pariṇataṁ attano pariṇāmeyya, nissaggiyaṁ pācittiyaṁ. <br><br>Jātarūparajatavaggo&nbsp;tatiyo.<br><br>Uddiṭṭhā kho, ayyāyo, tiṁsa nissaggiyā pācittiyā dhammā.<br>Tatthāyyāyo pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>dutiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>tatiyampi pucchāmi, kaccittha parisuddhā,<br>parisuddhetthāyyāyo, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmīti.<br><br>Nissaggiyapācittiyā niṭṭhitā.			Venerables, these thirty rules on relinquishment and confession come up for recitation.<br><br>1. If a nun collects almsbowls, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>2. If a nun determines out-of-season robe-cloth as ‘in-season’, and then distributes it, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>3. If a nun trades robes with a nun and then says, ‘Here’s your robe; give me that robe of mine. That which is yours is yours, and that which is mine is mine. Give me that, and take back what’s yours;’ and she just takes it or has it taken, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>4. If a nun asks for one thing and then for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>5. If a nun gets one thing in exchange and then something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>6. When a requisite belonging to the Sangha is designated for a specific purpose, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>7. When a requisite belonging to the Sangha is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>8. When a collective requisite is designated for a specific purpose, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>9. When a collective requisite is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>10. When a personal requisite is designated for a specific purpose and was asked for, if a nun exchanges it for something else, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>The first subchapter on almsbowls.<br><br>11. If a nun carries out an exchange to get a heavy cloak, it is to be worth at most four kaṁsa coins. If she gets one in exchange that is worth more than that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>12. If a nun carries out an exchange to get a light cloak, it is to be worth at most two-and-a-half kaṁsa coins. If she gets one in exchange that is worth more than that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>13. When her robe is finished and the robe season has ended, a nun should keep an extra robe for ten days at the most.<br>If she keeps it longer than that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>14. When her robe is finished and the robe season has ended, if a nun stays apart from her three robes even for a single day, except if the nuns have agreed, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>15. When her robe is finished and the robe season has ended, if out-of-season robe-cloth is offered to a nun, she may receive it if she wishes. If she receives it, she should quickly make a robe. If there is not enough cloth, but she is expecting more, she should keep it at most one month to make up the lack. If she keeps it longer than that, then even if she expects more cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>16. If a nun asks an unrelated male or female householder for a robe, except on an appropriate occasion, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br>These are the appropriate occasions: her robes are stolen or her robes are lost.<br><br>17. If an unrelated male or female householder invites that nun to take many robes, she should accept at most one sarong and one upper robe.<br>If she accepts more than that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>18. If a male or female householder has set aside a robe fund for an unrelated nun, thinking, ‘With this robe fund I will buy robe-cloth and give it to nun so-and-so;’ and if that nun, without first being invited, goes to them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘Please use this robe fund to buy such-and-such robe-cloth and then give it to me,’ and she does so because she wants something fine, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>19. If two male or female householders have set aside separate robe funds for an unrelated nun, thinking, ‘With these separate robe funds we’ll buy separate robe-cloths and give them to nun so-and-so;’ and if that nun, without first being invited, goes to them and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘Please put these separate robe funds together to buy such-and-such robe-cloth and then give it to me,’ and she does so because she wants something fine, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>20. If a king, a king’s employee, a brahmin, or a householder sends a robe fund for a nun by messenger, saying, ‘Buy robe-cloth with this robe fund and give it to nun so-and-so,’ and the messenger goes to that nun and says, ‘Venerable, I have brought a robe fund for you. Please receive it,’ then that nun should reply, ‘We don’t receive robe funds, but we do receive allowable robe-cloth at the right time.’ If that messenger says, ‘Is there anyone who provides services for you?’ the nun, if she needs robe-cloth, should point out a monastery worker or a lay follower and say, ‘They provide services for the nuns.’ If the messenger instructs that service provider and then returns to the nun and says, ‘Venerable, I have instructed the service provider you pointed out. Please go to them at the right time and they’ll give you robe-cloth,’ then, if that nun needs robe-cloth, she should go to that service provider and prompt them and remind them two or three times, saying, ‘I need robe-cloth.’ If she then gets robe-cloth, all is well. If she does not get it, she should stand in silence for it at most six times. If she then gets robe-cloth, all is well. If she makes any further effort and then gets robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession. If she does not get robe-cloth, she should go to the owners of that robe fund, or send a message, saying, ‘That nun hasn’t received any benefit from the robe fund you sent for her. Please recover what’s yours, or it might perish.’ This is the proper procedure.<br><br>The second subchapter on robes.<br><br>21. If a nun takes, has someone else take, or consents to gold, silver, or money being deposited for her, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>22. If a nun engages in various kinds of trades involving money, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>23. If a nun engages in various kinds of barter, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>24. If a nun exchanges an almsbowl with fewer than five mends for a new almsbowl, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br>That nun should relinquish that almsbowl to a gathering of nuns.<br>She should then be given the last almsbowl belonging to that gathering:<br>‘Nun, this bowl is yours. Keep it until it breaks.’ This is the proper procedure.<br><br>25. After being received, the tonics allowable for sick nuns—that is, ghee, butter, oil, honey, and syrup—should be used from storage for at most seven days.<br>If one uses them longer than that, one commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>26. If a nun herself gives a robe to a nun, but then, in anger, takes it back or has it taken back, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>27. If a nun herself asks for thread, and then has weavers weave her robe-cloth, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>28. If a male or female householder is having robe-cloth woven by weavers for an unrelated nun and, without first being invited, that nun goes to those weavers and specifies the kind of robe-cloth she wants, saying, ‘This robe-cloth that you are weaving for me, make it long and wide; make it closely woven, well-woven, well-stretched, well-scraped, and well-combed, and perhaps I will even give you a small gift,’ then, in saying that and afterwards giving them a small gift, even a bit of almsfood, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>29. When there are ten days left to the Kattika full moon that ends the first rainy-season residence and a haste-cloth is given to a nun, she may receive it if she regards it as urgent. She may then store it until the end of the robe season.<br>If she stores it beyond that, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>30. If a nun diverts to herself material support that she knows was intended for the Sangha, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.<br><br>The third subchapter on gold and silver.<br><br>Venerables, the thirty rules on relinquishment and confession have been recited.<br>In regard to this I ask you, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A second time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>A third time I ask, ‘Are you pure in this?’<br>You are pure in this and therefore silent. I will remember it thus.<br><br>The thirty&nbsp;offenses entailing relinquishment and confession are finished.	Nissaggiya pācittiyā	Jātarūpavaggo	[sound:Bi_NP.mp3]	205							[sound:ABi_NP.mp3]	Now, Venerables, these thirty matters entailing confession with forfeiture come up for recitation.<br><br>1. {The precept about -a bowl hoard} Should any bhikkhunī make a bowl hoard (have more than one bowl in her possession), it is to be forfeited and confessed. [See Bhikkhus’ N.P. 21]<br><br>2. {-distributing out-of-season robe-cloth} Should any bhikkhunī, having determined an out-of-season robe- cloth to be an in-season robe-cloth, distribute it, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>3. {-exchanging a robe} Should any bhikkhunī, having exchanged robe-cloth with another bhikkhunī, later say to her, “Here, Venerable. This is your robe-cloth. Bring me that robe-cloth of mine. What was yours is still yours. What was mine is still mine. Bring me that one of mine. Take yours back,” and then snatch it back or have it snatched back, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>4. {-asking for another} Should any bhikkhunī, having had one thing asked for, (then send it back and) have another thing asked for, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>5. {-getting another in exchange} Should any bhikkhunī, having had one thing bought, (then send it back and) have another thing bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>6. {-1st about exchanging a Saṅgha belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, using a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for the Saṅgha, have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>7. {-2nd Saṅgha belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for the Saṅgha, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>8. {-1st about exchanging a group belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, using a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for a group, have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>9. {-2nd group belonging} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for a group, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>10. {-exchanging something belonging to an individual} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself asked for a fund intended for one purpose, dedicated to one purpose for an individual, use it to have something else bought, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>Part One: The Bowl Chapter<br><br>11. {-heavy cloth} When a bhikkhunī is asking for a heavy cloth, one worth four bronzes at most may be asked for. If she asks for more than that, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>12. {-light cloth} When a bhikkhunī is asking for a light cloth, one worth two and a half bronzes at most may be asked for. If she asks for more than that, it is to be forfeited and confessed.<br><br>13. {-kaṭhina} When a bhikkhunī has finished her robe- making and the frame is destroyed (her kaṭhina privileges are in abeyance), she is to keep an extra robe- cloth ten days at most. Beyond that, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [1]<br><br>14. {-the “storehouse”} When a bhikkhunī has finished her robe-making and the frame is destroyed: If she dwells apart from (any of) her three robes even for one night — unless authorized by the bhikkhunīs—it is to be forfeited and confessed. [2]<br><br>15. {-out-of-season robe-cloth} When a bhikkhunī has finished her robe-making and the frame is destroyed: If out-of-season robe-cloth accrues to her, she may accept it if she so desires. Once she accepts it, she is to make it up immediately. If it should not be enough,&nbsp;she may lay it aside for a month at most if she has an expectation for filling the lack. Should she keep it beyond that, even when there is an expectation (for further cloth), it is to be forfeited and confessed. [3]<br><br>16. {-asking a non-relative} Should any bhikkhunī ask for robe-cloth from a man or woman householder unrelated to her, except at the proper occasion, it is to be forfeited and confessed. Here the proper occasion is this: The bhikkhunī’s robe has been stolen or destroyed. This is the proper occasion in this case. [6]<br><br>17. {-accepting more than that} If that unrelated man or woman householder presents the bhikkhunī with many robes (pieces of robe-cloth), she is to accept at most (enough for) an upper and an under robe. If she accepts more than that, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [7]<br><br>18. {-1st on setting up a robe fund} In case a man or woman householder prepares a robe fund for the sake of an unrelated bhikkhunī, thinking. “Having purchased a robe with this robe fund, I will supply the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with a robe”: If the bhikkhunī, not previously invited, approaching (the householder) should make a stipulation with regard to the robe, saying, “It would be good indeed, sir, if you supplied me (with a robe),” having purchased a robe of such-and-such a sort with this robe fund—out of a desire for something fine—it is to be forfeited and confessed. [8]<br><br>19. {-2nd on setting up a robe fund} In case two householders —men or women—prepare separate robe funds for the sake of a bhikkhunī unrelated to them, thinking, “Having purchased separate robes with these separate robe funds of ours, we will supply the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with robes”: If the bhikkhunī, not previously invited, approaching (them) should make a stipulation with regard to the robe, saying, “It would be good indeed, sirs, if you supplied me (with a robe), having purchased a robe of such-and-such a sort with these separate robe funds, the two (funds) together for one (robe),” out of desire for something fine, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [9]<br><br>20. {-the king} In case a king, a royal official, a brahmin or a householder sends a robe fund for a bhikkhunī via a messenger: “Purchase a robe with this robe fund and supply the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with a robe.” If the messenger approaches the bhikkhunī and says: “This robe fund is for the venerable. May the venerable accept this robe fund.” Then the bhikkhunī is to tell the messenger: “We do not accept robe funds, friend. We accept robes at the right time.” If the messenger says to the bhikkhunī: “Does the venerable have a steward?” Then, if the bhikkhunī desires a robe, she may indicate a steward, either a monastery attendant or a lay follower: “That, sir, is the bhikkhunīs’ steward.” If the messenger, having instructed the steward, goes to the bhikkhunī and says: “I have instructed the steward the venerable indicated. May the venerable go and she (the steward) will supply you with a robe in-season.” Then the bhikkhunī, desiring a robe and approaching the steward, may prompt and remind her 2 or 3 times: “I have need of a robe.” Should (the steward) produce the robe after being prompted and reminded 2 or 3 times, that is good. If she does not produce the robe, (the bhikkhunī) should stand in silence 4, 5, or 6 times at most for that purpose. Should (the steward) produce the robe after (the bhikkhunī) has stood in silence for the purpose 4, 5, or 6 times at most, that is good. If she should not produce the robe, but she produces the robe after (the bhikkhunī) has tried further, it is to be forfeited and confessed. If she should not produce (the robe), then the bhikkhunī herself should go to the place from which the robe fund was brought, or a messenger should be sent (to say), “The robe fund that you, Venerable sirs, sent for the sake of the bhikkhunī has given no benefit to the bhikkhunī at all. May you be united with what is yours. May what is yours not be lost.” This is the proper course here. [10]<br><br>Part Two: The Robe-cloth Chapter<br><br>21. {-money} Should any bhikkhunī take gold and silver, or have it taken, or consent to its being deposited (near her), it is to be forfeited and confessed. [18]<br><br>22. {-monetary exchange} Should any bhikkhunī engage in various types of monetary exchange, it (the income) is to be forfeited and confessed. [19]<br><br>23. {-bartering} Should any bhikkhunī engage in various types of trade, (the article) is to be forfeited and confessed. [20]<br><br>24. {-less than five mends} Should a bhikkhunī with an alms bowl having less than five mends exchange it for another new bowl, it is to be forfeited and confessed. The bowl is to be forfeited by the bhikkhunī to the assembly of bhikkhunīs. That assembly of bhikkhunīs’ final bowl should be presented to the bhikkhunī (saying): “This, bhikkhuni, is your bowl. It is to be kept until broken.” This is the proper procedure here. [22]<br><br>25. {-medicine} There are these tonics to be taken by sick bhikkhunīs: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, sugar / molasses. Having been received, they are to be used from storage seven days at most. Beyond that, they are to be forfeited and confessed. [23]<br><br>26. {-snatching robes} Should any bhikkhunī, having herself given a robe-cloth to a bhikkhunī, and then being angered and displeased, snatch it back or have it snatched back, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [25]<br><br>27. {-requesting thread} Should any bhikkhunī, having requested thread, have a robe woven by weavers, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [26]<br><br>28. {-greater about weavers} In case a man or woman householder unrelated to a bhikkhunī has weavers weave robe-cloth for her, and if the bhikkhunī without previous invitation should approach the weavers and make stipulations for the cloth, saying: “This cloth, friends, is to be woven for me. Make it long, broad, tightly woven, well woven, well spread, well scraped, well smoothed, and perhaps I may gave you a little something.” And should the bhikkhunī, having said that, give them a little something, even a bit of alms food, it (the cloth) is to be forfeited and confessed. [27]<br><br>29. {-special robes} Ten days prior to the third-month Kattika full moon, should robe-cloth offered in urgency accrue to a bhikkhunī, she is to accept it if she regards it as offered in urgency. Once she has accepted it, she may keep it throughout the robe-season. Beyond that, it is to be forfeited and confessed. [28]<br><br>30. {-allocation} Should any bhikkhunī knowingly divert to herself gains that had been intended for a Saṅgha, they are to be forfeited and confessed. [30]<br><br>Part Three: The Gold and Silver Chapter<br><br>Recited, Venerables, are the thirty matters entailing confession with forfeiture. Herein I ask the venerables: Are you pure in this? A second time I ask: Are you pure in this? A third time I ask: Are you pure in this? The venerables are pure in this; therefore they are silent. So I remember it.<br><br>The section on confession with forfeiture is finished.

Pali Bhikkhunī Patimokkha Memorizing for Bhikkhunī::8.Sekhiyā::1 Parimaṇḍala Vagga	BI VIN PAT BI SK 1 2	Parimaṇḍalasikkhāpadaṁ	1. Parimaṇḍalaṁ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā.<br><br>2. Parimaṇḍalaṁ pārupissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā.	1. {Parimaṇḍalasikkhāpadaṁ} Parimaṇḍalaṁ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā.<br><br>2. {Parimaṇḍalasikkhāpadaṁ} Parimaṇḍalaṁ pārupissāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā.			1. ‘I will wear my sarong evenly all around,’ this is how you should train.<br><br>2. ‘I will wear my upper robe evenly all around,’ this is how you should train.	Sekhiyā	Parimaṇḍalavaggo	[sound:Bi_SK_1_2.mp3]	467	At one time when the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery,<br><br>the nuns from the group of six were wearing their sarongs hanging down in front and behind.<br><br>People complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns wear their sarongs hanging down in front and behind? They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!”<br><br>The nuns heard the complaints of those people,<br><br>and the nuns of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six wear their sarongs hanging down in front and behind?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that those nuns do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“How can the nuns from the group of six do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	‘“I will wear my sarong evenly all around,” this is how you should train.’”<br><br>One should wear one’s sarong evenly all around, covering the navel and the knees.<br><br>If a nun, out of disrespect, wears her sarong hanging down in front or behind, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if it is unintentional;<br><br>if she is not mindful;<br><br>if she does not know;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>(Contracted.) Sekhiyā	Surusuruvaggo	[sound:Bi_SK_57.mp3]	516	At one time when the Buddha was staying in the Bhagga country at Susumāragira in the Bhesakaḷā Grove,<br><br>the monks from the group of six gave teachings to people holding a sunshade.<br><br>The monks of few desires complained and criticized those monks,<br><br>“How can the monks from the group of six give teachings to people holding a sunshade?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that you do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“Foolish men, how can you do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:<br><br>‘“I will not give a teaching to anyone holding a sunshade,” this is how you should train.’”<br><br>In this way the Buddha laid down this training rule for the monks.<br><br>Soon afterwards, being afraid of wrongdoing, the monks did not give teachings to sick people holding a sunshade.<br><br>People complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the Sakyan monastics not give teachings to someone who’s sick holding a sunshade?”<br><br>The monks heard the complaints of those people,<br><br>and they told the Buddha.<br><br>Soon afterwards he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, I allow you to give a teaching to someone who’s sick holding a sunshade.<br><br>And so, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	‘“I will not give a teaching to anyone holding a sunshade who is not sick,” this is how you should train.’”<br><br>A sunshade:<br><br>there are three kinds of sunshades: the white sunshade, the reed sunshade, the leaf sunshade. They are bound at the rim and bound at the ribs.<br><br>Teaching:<br><br>what has been spoken by the Buddha, what has been spoken by disciples, what has been spoken by sages, what has been spoken by gods, what is connected with what is beneficial, what is connected with the Teaching.<br><br>Give:<br><br>if he teaches by the line, then for every line he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>If he teaches by the syllable, then for every syllable he commits an offense of wrong conduct.<br><br>One should not give a teaching to anyone holding a sunshade who is not sick.<br><br>If a monk, out of disrespect, gives a teaching to someone holding a sunshade who is not sick, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if it is unintentional;<br><br>if he is not mindful;<br><br>if he does not know;<br><br>if he is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The seventh training rule is finished.	Tena samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū chattapāṇissa dhammaṁ desenti.<br><br>Ye te bhikkhū appicchā …pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū chattapāṇissa dhammaṁ desessantī”ti …pe…<br><br>“saccaṁ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, chattapāṇissa dhammaṁ desethā”ti?<br><br>“Saccaṁ, bhagavā”ti.<br><br>Vigarahi buddho bhagavā …pe…<br><br>kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, chattapāṇissa dhammaṁ desessatha.<br><br>Netaṁ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṁ vā pasādāya …pe…<br><br>evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—<br><br>“Na chattapāṇissa dhammaṁ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.<br><br>Evañcidaṁ bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ hoti.<br><br>Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chattapāṇissa gilānassa dhammaṁ desetuṁ kukkuccāyanti.<br><br>Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti—<br><br>“kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā chattapāṇissa gilānassa dhammaṁ na desessantī”ti.<br><br>Assosuṁ kho bhikkhū tesaṁ manussānaṁ ujjhāyantānaṁ khiyyantānaṁ vipācentānaṁ.<br><br>Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.<br><br>Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—<br><br>“anujānāmi, bhikkhave, chattapāṇissa gilānassa dhammaṁ desetuṁ.<br><br>Evañca pana, bhikkhave, imaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ uddiseyyātha—	“Na chattapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṁ desessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā”ti.<br><br>Chattaṁ nāma<br><br>tīṇi chattāni— setacchattaṁ, kilañjacchattaṁ, paṇṇacchattaṁ maṇḍalabaddhaṁ salākabaddhaṁ.<br><br>Dhammo nāma<br><br>buddhabhāsito sāvakabhāsito isibhāsito devatābhāsito atthūpasañhito dhammūpasañhito.<br><br>Deseyyāti<br><br>padena deseti, pade pade āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Akkharāya deseti, akkharakkharāya āpatti dukkaṭassa.<br><br>Na chattapāṇissa agilānassa dhammo desetabbo.<br><br>Yo anādariyaṁ paṭicca chattapāṇissa agilānassa dhammaṁ deseti, āpatti dukkaṭassa.	Anāpatti—<br><br>asañcicca …pe…<br><br>ādikammikassāti.<br><br>Sattamasikkhāpadaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ.	[sound:ABi_SK_57.mp3]	{-an umbrella in the hand} I will not teach Dhamma to a person with an umbrella in their hand and who is not ill: a training to be observed.

Sekhiyā	Pādukavaggo	[sound:Bi_SK_69.mp3]	529	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the monks from the group of six were sitting on low seats while giving teachings to people sitting on high seats.<br><br>The monks of few desires complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can the monks from the group of six sit on low seats while giving teachings to people sitting on high seats?” …<br><br>“Is it true, monks, that you do this?”<br><br>“It’s true, sir.”<br><br>The Buddha rebuked them …<br><br>“Foolish men, how can you do this?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …”<br><br>After rebuking them …<br><br>he gave a teaching and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Once upon a time in Bārāṇasī, monks, there was a low-caste man whose wife became pregnant.<br><br>She said to him,<br><br>‘I’m pregnant.<br><br>I crave mangoes.’<br><br>‘But there are no mangoes. It’s the wrong season.’<br><br>‘If I don’t get any, I’ll die.’<br><br>At that time the king had a mango tree that was always bearing fruit.<br><br>Then that low-caste man went to that mango tree, climbed it, and hid himself.<br><br>Just then the king and his brahmin counselor went to that same mango tree. There the king sat on a high seat while learning the Vedas.<br><br>The low-caste man thought,<br><br>‘How wrong-headed this king is, sitting on a high seat while learning the Vedas.<br><br>And the brahmin is wrong-headed too, sitting on a low seat while teaching the Vedas to one sitting on a high seat.<br><br>And I’m wrong-headed too, stealing mangoes from the king because of a woman.<br><br>This is all so low!’<br><br>And he fell out of the tree right there.<br><br>‘Neither understands what is good,<br><br>Neither sees the Truth:<br><br>Not he who teaches the Vedas,<br><br>Nor he who learns improperly.’<br><br>‘I’ve eaten the finest rice,<br><br>With a curry of pure meat:<br><br>Therefore I’m not practicing the Teaching,<br><br>The Teaching praised by the Noble Ones.’<br><br>‘A curse it is the obtaining of wealth,<br><br>And so is becoming popular, brahmin;<br><br>These things come with a low rebirth,<br><br>Or with wrong-headed behavior.<br><br>‘Go forth, great brahmin,<br><br>Other beings will do the cooking;<br><br>Don’t go against the Teaching,<br><br>Because you’ll break like a jar.’<br><br>Even at that time, monks, I was displeased by someone teaching the Vedas while sitting on a low seat to someone sitting on a high seat. How, then, could it not be displeasing now?<br><br>This will affect people’s confidence …” …<br><br>“And, monks, this training rule should be recited like this:	‘“I will not give a teaching while sitting on a low seat to anyone sitting on a high seat who is not sick,” this is how you should train.’”<br><br>One should not give a teaching while sitting on a low seat to anyone sitting on a high seat who is not sick.<br><br>If a monk, out of disrespect, gives a teaching while sitting on a low seat to someone sitting on a high seat who is not sick, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if it is unintentional;<br><br>if he is not mindful;<br><br>if he does not know;<br><br>if he is sick;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if he is insane;<br><br>if he is the first offender.<br><br>The ninth training rule is finished. Sekhiyā	Pādukavaggo	[sound:Bi_SK_75.mp3]	535	At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery.<br><br>At that time the nuns from the group of six were defecating, urinating, and spitting in water.<br><br>People complained and criticized them,<br><br>“How can nuns defecate, urinate, and spit in water? He then had the Sangha gathered and addressed the monks:<br><br>“Monks, I allow a sick nun to defecate, urinate, and spit in water.<br><br>And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule like this:	‘“When not sick, I will not defecate, urinate, or spit in water,” this is how you should train.’”<br><br>If one is not sick, one should not defecate, urinate, or spit in water.<br><br>If, out of disrespect, a nun who is not sick defecates, urinates, or spits in water, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.	There is no offense:<br><br>if it is unintentional;<br><br>if she is not mindful;<br><br>if she does not know;<br><br>if she is sick;<br><br>if she does it on dry ground, but it then spreads to water;<br><br>if there is an emergency;<br><br>if she is insane;<br><br>if she is deranged;<br><br>if she is overwhelmed by pain;<br><br>if she is the first offender.<br><br>The fifteenth training rule is finished.<br><br>The seventh subchapter on shoes is finished.<br><br>“Venerables, the rules of training have been recited.<br><br>In regard to this I ask you,<br><br>‘Are you pure in this?’<br><br>A second time I ask,<br><br>‘Are you pure in this?’<br><br>A third time I ask,<br><br>‘Are you pure in this?’<br><br>You are pure in this and therefore silent.
